children.text: atyaktaṃ tulyaśīlābhiḥ strībhiḥ pānena mṛgayayā vā prasañjayitvā rātrāv upagṛhyānayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he has not been abandoned, they should involve him with women of similar character through drinking or hunting, seize him at night, and bring him back.

children.text: upasthitaṃ ca rājyena madūrdhvam iti sāntvayet
children.translated_text: And when he has arrived, the king should conciliate him with the promise, "The kingdom will be yours after me."
Then he should confine him in one place; but if he has a son, he should send him into exile.
When the king is energetic, his servants are energetic after him.
When he is negligent, they too are negligent after him.
And they consume his undertakings.
He is also deceived by his enemies.
Therefore he should apply himself to personal exertion.

children.text: nālikābhir ahar aṣṭadhā rātriṃ ca vibhajet chāyāpramāṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: He should divide the day and the night each into eight parts by <s>nālikā</s>s, or by measuring the shadow.

children.text: tripauruṣī pauruṣī caturaṅgulā naṣṭacchāyo madhyāhneti catvāraḥ pūrve divasasyāṣṭabhāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A shadow three human lengths long, one human length long, four finger-breadths long, and absent at midday: these mark the first four eighth-parts of the day.
By these the later portions are explained.

children.text: tatra pūrve divasasyāṣṭabhāge rakṣāvidhānam āyavyayau ca śṛṇuyāt ||
children.translated_text: There, in the first eighth-part of the day, he should attend to arrangements for protection and hear the accounts of income and expenditure.
In the second, he should examine the affairs of the townspeople and country people.

children.text: tṛtīye snānabhojanaṃ seveta svādhyāyaṃ ca kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: In the third, he should bathe and eat, and he should perform recitation and study.
In the fourth, he should receive gold and appoint superintendents.

children.text: pañcame mantripariṣadā pattrasampreṣaṇena mantrayeta cāraguhyabodhanīyāni ca budhyeta ||
children.translated_text: In the fifth, he should deliberate with the council of ministers by dispatching written messages, and he should learn the secret matters to be made known by spies.
In the sixth, he should attend to free recreation or to counsel.
In the seventh, he should inspect the elephants, horses, chariots, and arms.
In the eighth, together with the commander of the army, he should consider military action.
When the day has ended, he should perform the twilight observance.
In the first part of the night, he should meet secret agents.
In the second, he should bathe and eat, and also perform recitation and study.
In the third, he should lie down at the sound of music and sleep through the fourth and fifth parts.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe tūryaghoṣeṇa pratibuddhaḥ śāstram itikartavyatāṃ ca cintayet ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth, awakened by the sound of music, he should reflect on the <s>śāstra</s> and on what is to be done.
In the seventh, he should sit in counsel and dispatch secret agents.
In the eighth, he should receive benedictions from officiating priests, teachers, household priests, and rites of blessing, and he should meet the physician, the chief cook, and the astrologer.

children.text: savatsāṃ dhenuṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca pradakṣiṇīkṛtyopasthānaṃ gacchet ||
children.translated_text: After circumambulating a cow with her calf and a bull, he should go to the audience hall.

children.text: ātmabalānukūlyena vā niśāharbhāgān pravibhajya kāryāṇi seveta ||
children.translated_text: Or, according to what suits his own strength, he should divide the parts of night and day and attend to his duties.
When he has gone to the audience hall, he should not allow obstruction at the door for those who have business.

children.text: durdarśo hi rājā kāryākāryaviparyāsam āsannaiḥ kāryate ||
children.translated_text: For a king who is hard to see is made by those close to him to reverse what should and should not be done.
Through that he may incur the anger of his constituents or come under the power of an enemy.

children.text: tasmād devatāśramapāṣaṇḍaśrotriyapaśupuṇyasthānānāṃ bālavṛddhavyādhitavyasanyanāthānāṃ strīṇāṃ ca krameṇa kāryāṇi paśyet kāryagauravād ātyayikavaśena vā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should examine in order the affairs of deities, hermitages, sectarians, <s>śrotriyas</s>, cattle, and sacred places, and of children, the aged, the sick, the distressed, the helpless, and women, according to the weight of the matter or under the pressure of urgency.
He should hear every urgent matter and should not let it pass by.
A matter hard to accomplish, when passed over, becomes impossible.
Having gone to the fire-house, he should examine the business of physicians and ascetics,
with the household priest and the teacher as companions, after rising to greet them respectfully.

children.text: tapasvināṃ tu kāryāṇi traividyaiḥ saha kārayet
children.translated_text: But the affairs of ascetics he should have handled together with those versed in the three Vedas,
and also those of men skilled in magical practices; he should not do so himself, because of the danger of causing anger.

children.text: rājño hi vratam utthānaṃ yajñaḥ kāryānuśāsanam
children.translated_text: For exertion is the king's vow, and the governance of affairs is his sacrifice.
Impartial maintenance of livelihoods is his sacrificial fee, and his consecration is his initiation.

children.text: prajāsukhe sukhaṃ rājñaḥ prajānāṃ ca hite hitam
children.translated_text: In the happiness of the subjects lies the king's happiness; in the welfare of the subjects lies his welfare.

children.text: nātmapriyaṃ hitaṃ rājñaḥ prajānāṃ tu priyaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: What is dear to himself is not beneficial to the king; what is dear to the subjects is beneficial.
Therefore the king, ever energetic, should carry out the administration of material affairs.
The root of gain is exertion; the root of loss is the opposite.
When there is no exertion, the destruction of what has been obtained and what is yet to be obtained is certain.
Through exertion the result is obtained, and material prosperity is acquired.

children.text: vāstukapraśaste deśe saprākāraparikhādvāram anekakakṣyāparigatam antaḥpuraṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: In a site approved by <s>vāstu</s>, he should construct the inner palace, furnished with rampart, moat, and gate, and surrounded by many courts.

children.text: kośagṛhavidhānena madhye vāsagṛham gūḍhabhittisaṃcāraṃ mohanagṛhaṃ tanmadhye vā vāsagṛham bhūmigṛhaṃ vāsannacaityakāṣṭhadevatāpidhānadvāram anekasuruṅgāsaṃcāraṃ tasyopari prāsādaṃ gūḍhabhittisopānaṃ suṣirastambhapraveśāpasāraṃ vā vāsagṛhaṃ yantrabaddhatalāvapātaṃ kārayet āpatpratīkārārtham āpadi vā ||
children.translated_text: According to the plan of a treasury building, in the middle he should construct a residence with hidden passages in the walls and a bewildering chamber; or, in the middle of that, a residence that is an underground chamber, its doorway concealed by a nearby shrine or wooden image, with movement through many tunnels; above it he should construct a palace with a stairway hidden in the wall, or a residence with entrance and escape through hollow pillars and with a mechanically fastened floor that drops away, for countering danger or in time of danger.
Or he may devise it otherwise, because of danger from fellow students.

children.text: mānuṣeṇāgninā trir apasavyaṃ parigatam antaḥpuram agnir anyo na dahati na cātrānyo 'gnir jvalati vaidyutena bhasmanā mṛtsaṃyuktena karakavāriṇāvaliptaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The inner apartment, when encircled three times counterclockwise by a man-made fire, is not burned by any other fire, and no other fire blazes there; likewise when it is smeared with lightning-produced ash mixed with earth and with hail-water.

children.text: jīvantīśvetāmuṣkakapuṣpavandākābhir akṣīve jātasyāśvatthasya pratānena guptaṃ sarpā viṣāṇi vā na prabhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When it is protected with the plants <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>muṣkaka</s> flowers, and <s>vandākā</s>, and with a shoot of an <s>aśvattha</s> born on an <s>akṣīva</s> tree, snakes or poisons have no power.
Peacocks, mongooses, and spotted deer, when released, eat snakes.

children.text: śukaḥ sārikā bhṛṅgarājo vā sarpaviṣaśaṅkāyāṃ krośati ||
children.translated_text: A parrot, a <s>sārikā</s>, or a <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> cries out when there is suspicion of snake poison.

children.text: krauñco viṣābhyāśe mādyati glāyati jīvaṃjīvakaḥ mriyate mattakokilaḥ cakorasyākṣiṇī virajyete ||
children.translated_text: In the vicinity of poison a <s>krauñca</s> bird becomes intoxicated, the <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> languishes, the <s>mattakokila</s> dies, and the eyes of the <s>cakora</s> lose their color.
Thus he should take countermeasures against fire, poison, and snakes.

children.text: pṛṣṭhataḥ kakṣyāvibhāge strīniveśo garbhavyādhisaṃsthā vṛkṣodakasthānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: At the back, in the division of the enclosure, should be the women's residence, the ward for pregnancy and sickness, and the place for trees and water.
Outside should be the quarters for maidens and princes.

children.text: purastād alaṅkārabhūmir mantrabhūmir upasthānaṃ kumārādhyakṣasthānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In front should be the adornment ground, the council ground, the audience hall, and the office of the superintendent of princes.
In the intervening enclosures the inner-guard troops should stand.
After entering the inner residence, he should see the queen only when she has been cleared by elderly women.

children.text: devīgṛhe līno hi bhrātā bhadrasenaṃ jaghāna mātuḥ śayyāntargataśca putraḥ kārūṣam ||
children.translated_text: For a brother, hidden in the queen's chamber, killed <s>Bhadrasena</s>, and a son, lying inside his mother's bed, killed <s>Kārūṣa</s>.

children.text: lājān madhuneti viṣeṇa paryasya devī kāśirājam viṣadigdhena nūpureṇa vairantyam mekhalāmaṇinā sauvīram jālūtham ādarśena veṇyāṃ gūḍhaṃ śastraṃ kṛtvā devī vidūrathaṃ jaghāna ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared parched grain and honey with poison, a queen killed the king of <s>Kāśi</s>; with a poison-smeared anklet, <s>Vairantya</s>; with a jewel in a girdle, <s>Sauvīra</s>; with a mirror, <s>Jālūtha</s>; and, making a weapon hidden in her braid, a queen killed <s>Vidūratha</s>.
Therefore he should avoid these occasions for danger.
He should prohibit contact with shaven ascetics, matted-hair ascetics, and deceivers, and also with outside female servants.

children.text: na caināḥ kulyāḥ paśyeyuḥ anyatra garbhavyādhisaṃsthābhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should respectable women see them, except those attached to the pregnancy and sick wards.
Courtesans may see them only when their bodies have been purified by bathing and rubbing and their clothes and ornaments have been changed.

children.text: aśītikāḥ puruṣāḥ pañcāśatkāḥ striyo vā mātāpitṛvyañjanāḥ sthaviravarṣadharābhyāgārikāścāvarodhānāṃ śaucāśaucaṃ vidyuḥ sthāpayeyuśca svāmihite ||
children.translated_text: Men of eighty, or women of fifty, who have the appearance of mothers and fathers, together with elderly eunuchs and chamber attendants, should know the purity and impurity of the secluded women and keep them in the master's interest.

children.text: svabhūmau ca vaset sarvaḥ parabhūmau na saṃcaret
children.translated_text: Everyone should remain in his own station and should not move through another's station.

children.text: na ca bāhyena saṃsargaṃ kaścid ābhyantaro vrajet ||
children.translated_text: And no one inside should enter into contact with anyone outside.
All goods, after inspection and with their entry and exit recorded,
should go out or come in only when they bear a seal as they pass from station to station.

children.text: śayanād utthitaḥ strīgaṇair dhanvibhiḥ parigṛhyate dvitīyasyāṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kaṃcukoṣṇīṣibhir varṣadharābhyāgārikaiḥ tṛtīyasyāṃ kubjavāmanakirātaiḥ caturthyāṃ mantribhiḥ sambandhibhir dauvārikaiśca prāsapāṇibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he rises from bed, he is surrounded by groups of women armed with bows; in the second enclosure by men wearing cuirasses and turbans, eunuchs, and chamber attendants; in the third by hunchbacks, dwarfs, and <s>Kirāta</s> guards; in the fourth by ministers, kinsmen, and door-keepers with spears in hand.

children.text: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ sambandhānubaddhaṃ śikṣitam anuraktaṃ kṛtakarmāṇaṃ ca janam āsannaṃ kurvīta nānyatodeśīyam akṛtārthamānaṃ svadeśīyaṃ vāpyapakṛtyopagṛhītam ||
children.translated_text: He should keep near him a person inherited from father and grandfather, bound by relationship, trained, loyal, and experienced in service; not a foreigner, nor even a native whose aims and honors have not been fulfilled, or one who has been wronged and then conciliated.
The inner-guard army should protect the king and the inner palace.

children.text: gupte deśe māhānasikaḥ sarvam āsvādabāhulyena karma kārayet ||
children.translated_text: In a guarded place the chief cook should have all the work done with repeated tasting.

children.text: tad rājā tathaiva pratibhuñjīta pūrvam agnaye vayobhyaśca baliṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: The king should partake of that in the same way, after first making offerings to fire and to the birds.

children.text: agner jvālādhūmanīlatā śabdasphoṭanaṃ ca viṣayuktasya vayasāṃ vipattiśca ||
children.translated_text: Blueness of the flame and smoke of the fire, sound and bursting, are signs of something mixed with poison, as is harm coming to the birds.

children.text: annasya ūṣmā mayūragrīvābhaḥ śaityam āśu kliṣṭasyeva vaivarṇyaṃ saudakatvam aklinnatvaṃ ca vyañjanānām āśu śuṣkatvaṃ ca kvāthadhyāmaphenapaṭalavicchinnabhāvo gandhasparśarasavadhaśca draveṣu hīnātiriktacchāyādarśanaṃ phenapaṭalasīmantordhvarājīdarśanaṃ ca rasasya madhye nīlā rājī payasastāmrā madyatoyayoḥ kālī dadhnaḥ śyāmā madhunaḥ śvetā dravyāṇām ārdrāṇām āśu pramlānatvam utpakvabhāvaḥ kvāthanīlaśyāvatā ca śuṣkāṇām āśu śātanaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ ca kaṭhinānāṃ mṛdutvaṃ mṛdūnāṃ ca kaṭhinatvam tadabhyāśe kṣudrasattvavadhaśca āstaraṇaprāvaraṇānāṃ dhyāmamaṇḍalatā tanturomapakṣmaśātanaṃ ca lohamaṇimayānāṃ paṅkamalopadehatā sneharāgagauravaprabhāvavarṇasparśavadhaśca iti viṣayuktasya liṅgāni ||
children.translated_text: In cooked food, steam with the sheen of a peacock's neck, coldness, quick discoloration as if spoiled, wateriness and failure to become moist; in side dishes, quick drying; in liquids, a boiled or scorched look, foam and film, separation, and loss of smell, touch, and taste; the appearance of diminished or excessive reflections, and the appearance of upward streaks at the edges of foam and film; in the middle of sauce a blue streak, in milk a copper-colored one, in liquor and water a black one, in curds a dark one, and in honey a white one; in moist substances quick withering, a state as if overcooked, and boiled blue-black discoloration; in dry substances quick crumbling and discoloration; softening of hard things and hardening of soft things; the death of small creatures nearby; in bedding and coverings, dark circular stains and the falling out of threads, hair, and down; in objects made of metal and gems, a coating of mud and dirt and loss of oiliness, color, weight, brilliance, appearance, and feel: these are the signs of what is mixed with poison.

children.text: viṣapradasya tu śuṣkaśyāvavaktratā vāksaṅgaḥ svedo vijṛmbhaṇaṃ cātimātraṃ vepathuḥ praskhalanaṃ vākyaviprekṣaṇam āvegaḥ karmaṇi svabhūmau cānavasthānam iti ||
children.translated_text: For the poison-giver, there are dryness and darkening of the face, obstruction of speech, sweating, excessive yawning, trembling, stumbling, looking away while speaking, agitation, and inability to remain at his work or in his own station.
Therefore men skilled in anti-poison lore and physicians should be near him.

children.text: bhiṣagbhaiṣajyāgārād āsvādaviśuddham auṣadhaṃ gṛhītvā pācakapeṣakābhyām ātmanā ca pratisvādya rājñe prayacchet ||
children.translated_text: A physician should take medicine from the pharmacy after it has been made safe by tasting, have it tasted in turn by the cook, the grinder, and himself, and then give it to the king.
Drinks and drinking water are explained by the rule for medicine.

children.text: kalpakaprasādhakāḥ snānaśuddhavastrahastāḥ samudram upakaraṇam antarvaṃśikahastād ādāya paricareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Barbers and dressers, with clothes and hands purified by bathing, should take the sealed implements from the hand of an inner-guard officer and attend him.

children.text: snāpakasaṃvāhakāstarakarajakamālākārakarma dāsyaḥ prasiddhaśaucāḥ kuryuḥ tābhir adhiṣṭhitā vā śilpinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Female servants of known cleanliness should perform the tasks of bath attendants, masseurs, bed-makers, washermen, and garland-makers, or artisans should do them under their supervision.

children.text: ātmacakṣuṣi niveśya vastramālyaṃ dadyuḥ snānānulepanapragharṣacūrṇavāsasnānīyāni ca svavakṣobāhuṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: After setting them before his own eyes, they should give garments and garlands, and also bathing articles, unguents, rubbing powders, scented garments, and bath substances, having applied them to their own breasts and arms.
By this, what has come from another person is also explained.
Performers should amuse him, avoiding play with weapons, fire, and poison.
Their musical instruments too should remain inside, as should the ornaments for horses, chariots, and elephants.
He should mount a conveyance or vehicle attended by a trustworthy man, and a boat attended by a trustworthy boatman.
He should not board a boat tied to another boat, nor one that is at the mercy of the force of the wind.
An army should be stationed at the water's edge.
He should enter water that has been cleared of fish and crocodiles.
He should go to a park that has been cleared by catchers of dangerous creatures.
With hunters and packs of dogs, after the danger from thieves, wild beasts, and hostile attacks has been removed, he should go to a deer forest in order to practice with moving targets.
Attended by trustworthy weapon-bearers, he should see an accomplished ascetic; and together with the council of ministers he should see an envoy from a neighboring ruler.

children.text: saṃnaddho 'śvaṃ hastinaṃ vārūḍhaḥ saṃnaddham anīkaṃ paśyet ||
children.translated_text: Armored and mounted on a horse or an elephant, he should inspect an armored army.

children.text: niryāṇe 'bhiyāne ca rājamārgam ubhayataḥ kṛtārakṣaṃ śastribhir daṇḍibhiścāpāstaśastrahastapravrajitavyaṅgaṃ gacchet ||
children.translated_text: When setting out or marching forth, he should go along the royal road, guarded on both sides by armed men and staff-bearers, with weapon-carriers, renunciants, and deformed persons removed.
He should not enter a crowd of men.
He should attend processions, gatherings, festivals, and public entertainments when they are supervised by groups of ten.
And just as a king keeps others under control by means of secret agents,
so this self-possessed man should protect himself from injuries caused by others.

children.text: bhūtapūrvam abhūtapūrvaṃ vā janapadaṃ paradeśāpavāhanena svadeśābhiṣyandavamanena vā niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: He should settle a territory, whether previously inhabited or not previously inhabited, by bringing people from another country or by emptying out the excess population of his own country.

children.text: śūdrakarṣakaprāyaṃ kulaśatāvaraṃ pañcakulaśataparaṃ grāmaṃ krośadvikrośasīmānam anyonyārakṣaṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: He should establish a village made up chiefly of <s>Śūdra</s> cultivators, with no fewer than one hundred families and no more than five hundred, with boundaries of one or two <s>krośas</s>, and capable of mutual protection.
At the ends of the boundaries he should set rivers, mountains, forests, ridges, ravines, embankments, <s>śamī</s> trees, <s>śālmalī</s> trees, and latex-bearing trees.

children.text: aṣṭaśatagrāmyā madhye sthānīyam catuḥśatagrāmyā droṇamukham dviśatagrāmyāḥ kārvaṭikam daśagrāmīsaṃgraheṇa saṃgrahaṃ sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In the center of eight hundred villages he should establish a <s>sthānīya</s> administrative station; for four hundred villages, a <s>droṇamukha</s>; for two hundred villages, a <s>kārvaṭika</s>; and for a collection of ten villages, a <s>saṃgraha</s>.
At the borders he should establish frontier-guard fortresses, the gateways of the territory, placed under frontier guards.
The spaces between them should be guarded by trappers, <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, and forest-dwellers.

children.text: ṛtvigācāryapurohitaśrotriyebhyo brahmadeyāny adaṇḍakarāṇy abhirūpadāyādakāni prayacchet adhyakṣasaṃkhyāyakādibhyo gopasthānikānīkasthacikitsakāśvadamakajaṅghākārikebhyaśca vikrayādhānavarjāni ||
children.translated_text: To officiating priests, teachers, household priests, and Vedic scholars he should grant <s>brahmadeya</s> lands, exempt from fines and taxes and inheritable by suitable heirs; and to superintendents, accountants, <s>gopas</s>, <s>sthānikas</s>, army officers, physicians, horse-trainers, and couriers he should grant lands that may not be sold or mortgaged.
To tax-paying people he should grant prepared fields as individual allotments.
Unprepared lands, when given to those who make them fit, are not to be taken away from their makers.
From those who do not cultivate them, he should confiscate them and grant them to others.
Or village laborers and merchants may cultivate them.
If they do not cultivate them, they should pay what is deficient.
He should assist them with grain, cattle, and money.
They should repay those afterward, when they are comfortable.

children.text: anugrahaparihārau caitebhyaḥ kośavṛddhikarau dadyāt kośopaghātakau varjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should grant them favors and exemptions that increase the treasury, and avoid those that injure the treasury.

children.text: alpakośo hi rājā paurajānapadān eva grasate ||
children.translated_text: For a king with a small treasury devours his townspeople and country people themselves.
He should grant an exemption at the time of settlement, or according to what has been received.
When their exemption has ended, he should favor them like a father.
He should establish mines, industrial works, resource forests, elephant forests, cattle stations, trade-route operations, and market towns for water routes and land routes.
He should build an irrigation embankment with water already present, or with water to be brought in.

children.text: anyeṣāṃ vā badhnatāṃ bhūmimārgavṛkṣopakaraṇānugrahaṃ kuryāt puṇyasthānārāmāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Or, for others who are building one, he should provide assistance in land, roads, trees, and equipment, and likewise for holy places and parks.

children.text: sambhūya setubandhād apakrāmataḥ karmakarabalīvardāḥ karma kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When someone withdraws from a jointly undertaken irrigation embankment, his workers and oxen should do the work.

children.text: vyayakarmaṇi ca bhāgī syāt na cāṃśaṃ labheta ||
children.translated_text: He should share in the expense and labor, but he should not receive a share.
In irrigation works the king obtains ownership over fish, waterfowl, and green produce for sale.
The king should make disobedient slaves, pledged servants, and relatives submit to discipline.

children.text: bālavṛddhavyasanyanāthāṃśca rājā bibhṛyāt striyam aprajātāṃ prajātāyāśca putrān ||
children.translated_text: The king should support children, the aged, those in distress, and the helpless, as well as a woman before childbirth and the sons of a woman who has given birth.

children.text: bāladravyaṃ grāmavṛddhā vardhayeyur ā vyavahāraprāpaṇāt devadravyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The village elders should increase the property of a minor until he reaches legal competence, and also the property of the gods.

children.text: apatyadāraṃ mātāpitarau bhrātṝn aprāptavyavahārān bhaginīḥ kanyā vidhavāścābibhrataḥ śaktimato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ anyatra patitebhyaḥ anyatra mātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: An able man who does not support his children and wife, his mother and father, brothers who have not reached legal competence, and sisters who are maidens or widows, is fined twelve <s>paṇas</s>, except in the case of those who are fallen, but not excepting his mother.

children.text: putradāram apratividhāya pravrajataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ striyaṃ ca pravrājayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who renounces without providing for his sons and wife, there is the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; the same applies to one who makes a woman renounce.
One whose active obligations have ceased may renounce after asking the judges of <s>dharma</s>.
Otherwise he should be restrained.

children.text: vānaprasthād anyaḥ pravrajitabhāvaḥ sajātād anyaḥ saṃghaḥ sāmutthāyikād anyaḥ samayānubandho vā nāsya janapadam upaniviśeta ||
children.translated_text: A renunciant status other than that of a forest-dweller, a corporate group other than one of the same birth-group, or a contractual association other than a cooperative one should not settle in his territory.

children.text: na ca tatrārāmā vihārārthā vā śālāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should there be parks there, or halls for the purpose of residence and recreation.
Actors, dancers, singers, musicians, professional speakers, and performers should not obstruct work.

children.text: nirāśrayatvād grāmāṇāṃ kṣetrābhiratatvācca puruṣāṇāṃ kośaviṣṭidravyadhānyarasavṛddhir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Because villages lack such shelters and because the men are devoted to the fields, there is growth in the treasury, corvée labor, raw materials, grain, and liquid produce.
A territory overrun by an enemy army or by forest tribes, afflicted by disease and famine...
The king should spare the countryside and restrain wasteful expenditure and amusements.
He should protect damaged agriculture from the pressures of punishment, forced labor, and taxes,
and herds of livestock from thieves, predatory beasts, poison, crocodiles, and diseases.
When the trade route is oppressed by favorites, officials, thieves, and frontier guards,
and is being depleted also by masses of livestock, he should clear it.
In the same way the king should protect raw-material forests, elephant forests, embankments, and mines
that were made formerly, and he should also set new ones in operation.
On land unfit for cultivation he should assign pasture grounds for animals.

children.text: pradiṣṭābhayasthāvarajaṅgamāni ca brahmasomāraṇyāni tapasvibhyo gorutaparāṇi prayacchet ||
children.translated_text: He should grant to ascetics <s>brahma</s>- and <s>soma</s>-forests, in which safety is proclaimed for stationary and moving beings, extending to the range marked by cattle sounds.

children.text: tāvanmātram ekadvāraṃ khātaguptaṃ svāduphalagulmaguccham akaṇṭakidrumam uttānatoyāśayaṃ dāntamṛgacatuṣpadaṃ bhagnanakhadaṃṣṭravyālaṃ mārgayukahastihastinīkalabhaṃ mṛgavanaṃ vihārārthaṃ rājñaḥ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: For the king's recreation he should have made a game forest of that extent, with one gate, protected by a ditch, with clumps and thickets bearing sweet fruits, with trees without thorns, with shallow reservoirs, with tame deer and quadrupeds, with dangerous beasts whose claws and fangs have been broken, and with male elephants, female elephants, and calves suited to the paths.

children.text: sarvātithimṛgaṃ pratyante cānyanmṛgavanaṃ bhūmivaśena vā niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: At the frontier, or according to the nature of the land, he should establish another animal forest open to all wild creatures.

children.text: kupyapradiṣṭānāṃ ca dravyāṇām ekaikaśo vanāni niveśayet dravyavanakarmāntān aṭavīśca dravyavanāpāśrayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For each of the raw materials designated as forest produce he should establish separate forests, workshops connected with the raw-material forests, and wilderness areas dependent on those forests.
At the frontier he should establish an elephant forest protected by forest guards.

children.text: nāgavanādhyakṣaḥ pārvataṃ nādeyaṃ sārasamānūpaṃ ca nāgavanaṃ viditaparyantapraveśaniṣkāsaṃ nāgavanapālaiḥ pālayet ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of elephant forests should maintain, through elephant-forest guards, a mountain, riverine, lake, or marsh elephant forest whose boundaries, entrances, and exits are known.
They should put to death a killer of elephants.
For bringing in the pair of tusks of an elephant that has died naturally, the reward is four and a quarter <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: nāgavanapālā hastipakapādapāśikasaumikavanacarakapārikarmikasakhā hastimūtrapurīṣacchannagandhā bhallātakīśākhāpracchannāḥ pañcabhiḥ saptabhir vā hastibandhakībhiḥ saha carantaḥ śayyāsthānapadyāleṇḍakūlaghātoddeśena hastikulaparyagraṃ vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Elephant-forest guards, accompanied by elephant keepers, foot-snare men, <s>saumikas</s>, forest-roving attendants, and assistants, should move about with their own scent covered by elephant urine and dung, hidden by branches of the <s>bhallātakī</s>, together with five or seven female decoy elephants; from sleeping places, standing places, footprints, dung, bank-breaking, and such signs, they should learn the full extent of elephant herds.

children.text: yūthacaram ekacaraṃ niryūthaṃ yūthapatiṃ hastinaṃ vyālaṃ mattaṃ potaṃ bandhamuktaṃ ca nibandhena vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By record they should know an elephant that ranges with a herd, one that ranges alone, one separated from the herd, a herd-leader, a dangerous one, a rutting one, a calf, and one released from captivity.
They should capture elephants whose marks and behavior are excellent, according to the standards for those stationed in the battle line.
A king's victory depends chiefly on elephants.
For elephants, with bodies of extraordinary size, do life-taking work by crushing an enemy army, its array, its fortress, and its camp.
The elephants of <s>Kāliṅga</s> and <s>Aṅga</s> are the best; those of the eastern regions and those born in <s>Cedi</s> and <s>Karūṣa</s>,
as well as those of <s>Daśārṇa</s> and <s>Aparānta</s>, are considered middling among elephants.
Those from <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> and <s>Pāñcanada</s> are remembered as inferior among them;
in all of them, power, speed, and energy increase through work.

children.text: caturdiśaṃ janapadānte sāmparāyikaṃ daivakṛtaṃ durgaṃ kārayet antardvīpaṃ sthalaṃ vā nimnāvaruddham audakam prāstaraṃ guhāṃ vā pārvatam nirudakastambam iriṇaṃ vā dhānvanam khañjanodakaṃ stambagahanaṃ vā vanadurgam ||
children.translated_text: In the four directions, at the borders of the country, he should have natural strategic forts built: a water fort on an island or on ground enclosed by low-lying land; a mountain fort on rocky ground or in a cave; a desert fort in a waterless, stump-filled, or barren tract; or a forest fort in marshy water or dense thickets.

children.text: teṣāṃ nadīparvatadurgaṃ janapadārakṣasthānam dhānvanavanadurgam aṭavīsthānam āpadyapasāro vā ||
children.translated_text: Of these, a river fort or mountain fort is a place for protecting the country; a desert fort or forest fort is a station for forest people, or a refuge in calamity.

children.text: janapadamadhye samudayasthānaṃ sthānīyaṃ niveśayet vāstukapraśaste deśe nadīsaṅgame hradasyāviśoṣasyāṅke sarasastaṭākasya vā vṛttaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vā vāstuvaśena vā pradakṣiṇodakaṃ paṇyapuṭabhedanam aṃsapathavāripathābhyām upetam ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of the country he should establish a <s>sthānīya</s> (central fortified settlement), in a place approved for building: at the confluence of rivers, in the bend of a lake that does not dry up, or on the bank of a lake or reservoir; it may be circular, oblong, square, or shaped according to the site, with water running to the right, a place where bundles of merchandise can be opened, and furnished with both a land route and a water route.

children.text: tasya parikhāstisro daṇḍāntarāḥ kārayet caturdaśa dvādaśa daśeti daṇḍān vistīrṇāḥ vistārād avagāḍhāḥ pādonam ardhaṃ vā tribhāgamūlāḥ mūlacaturaśrā vā pāṣāṇopahitāḥ pāṣāṇeṣṭakābaddhapārśvā vā toyāntikīr āgantutoyapūrṇā vā saparivāhāḥ padmagrāhavatīśca ||
children.translated_text: For it he should have three moats made, separated by intervals of one <s>daṇḍa</s>, fourteen, twelve, and ten <s>daṇḍas</s> wide respectively; in depth they should be a quarter, a half, or a third less than their width, square at the bottom, lined with stone or with sides bound by stone and brick, reaching water or filled by incoming water, provided with overflow channels, and containing lotuses and crocodiles.

children.text: caturdaṇḍāpakṛṣṭaṃ parikhāyāḥ ṣaḍdaṇḍocchritam avaruddhaṃ taddviguṇaviṣkambhaṃ khātād vapraṃ kārayed ūrdhvacayaṃ mañcapṛṣṭhaṃ kumbhakukṣikaṃ vā hastibhir gobhiśca kṣuṇṇaṃ kaṇṭakigulmaviṣavallīpratānavantam ||
children.translated_text: Four <s>daṇḍas</s> back from the moat he should have a rampart made from the excavated earth, six <s>daṇḍas</s> high, enclosed, twice that in breadth, rising upward, with a platform-like top or pot-bellied shape, trampled firm by elephants and cattle, and furnished with thorny shrubs and spreading poisonous creepers.
Or with the remaining earth he should fill gaps in the building site or in the royal palace.

children.text: vaprasyopari prākāraṃ viṣkambhadviguṇotsedham aiṣṭakaṃ dvādaśahastād ūrdhvamojaṃ yugmaṃ vā ā caturviṃśatihastād iti kārayet rathacaryāsaṃcāraṃ tālamūlaṃ murajakaiḥ kapiśīrṣakaiścācitāgram ||
children.translated_text: On top of the rampart he should build a brick wall whose height is twice its breadth, from twelve <s>hastas</s> upward, in odd or even measure, up to twenty-four <s>hastas</s>; it should allow the movement of chariots, have a palm-trunk-like base, and have its top furnished with <s>murajaka</s> and <s>kapiśīrṣaka</s> battlements.

children.text: pṛthuśilāsaṃhataṃ vā śailaṃ kārayet na tveva kāṣṭhamayam ||
children.translated_text: Or he should make a stone wall compacted from broad slabs; but never one made of wood.
For fire, once lodged in it, remains there.

children.text: viṣkambhacaturaśram aṭṭālakam utsedhasamāvakṣepasopānaṃ kārayet triṃśaddaṇḍāntaraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He should make a square watchtower, equal in elevation, with recessed stairways, and at intervals of thirty <s>daṇḍas</s>.

children.text: dvayor aṭṭālakayor madhye saharmyadvitalām adhyardhāyāmāṃ pratolīṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Between two watchtowers he should make a gateway, with an upper chamber, two-storied and one and a half times as long.
Between the watchtower and the gateway he should make an <s>indrakośa</s> (defensive chamber), a station for three archers, constructed with covered loopholes and joined planks.

children.text: antareṣu dvihastaviṣkambhaṃ pārśve caturguṇāyāmaṃ devapathaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: In the intervals he should make a <s>devapatha</s> (defensive passage), two <s>hastas</s> wide, and on the side four times as long.

children.text: daṇḍāntarā dvidaṇḍāntarā vā caryāḥ kārayet agrāhye deśe pradhāvanikāṃ niṣkiradvāraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He should make patrol paths at intervals of one <s>daṇḍa</s> or two <s>daṇḍa</s>s, and, in a place hard to seize, a sally-passage and an exit gate.

Outside, he should make a hidden covered path concealed with knee-breaking devices, spikes, palisades, pits, false drops, thorns, retreats, snake-back devices, palm-leaf spikes, caltrops, dog-tooth obstacles, bars, climbing obstacles, foot-traps, fire-pits, and water holes.

children.text: prākāram ubhayato meṇḍhakam adhyardhadaṇḍaṃ kṛtvā pratolīṣaṭtulāntaraṃ dvāraṃ niveśayet pañcadaṇḍād ekottaram ā aṣṭadaṇḍād iti caturaśraṃ ṣaḍbhāgam āyāmādadhikam aṣṭabhāgaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: After making the rampart with a battlement on both sides, one and a half <s>daṇḍa</s>s wide, he should set the gateway door between six crossbeams: from five <s>daṇḍa</s>s, increasing by one up to eight <s>daṇḍa</s>s, square, with the length greater by a sixth, or by an eighth.

children.text: pañcadaśahastād ekottaram ā aṣṭādaśahastād iti talotsedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The height of the floor should be from fifteen <s>hasta</s>s, increasing by one, up to eighteen <s>hasta</s>s.

children.text: stambhasya parikṣepaḥ ṣaḍāyāmo dviguṇo nikhātaḥ cūlikāyāścaturbhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The circumference of the pillar should be one-sixth of its length; the part sunk in the ground should be twice that, and the capital one-fourth.

children.text: āditalasya pañcabhāgāḥ śālā vāpī sīmāgṛhaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Five parts of the first storey should be the hall, the reservoir, and the boundary chamber.

children.text: daśabhāgikau dvau pratimañcau antaram āṇīharmyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The two side platforms should each occupy a tenth part, and between them should be the <s>āṇīharmya</s>.
At half a storey from the full height there should also be the fastening of the pillars.

children.text: ardhavāstukam uttamāgāram tribhāgāntaraṃ vā iṣṭakāvabaddhapārśvam vāmataḥ pradakṣiṇasopānaṃ gūḍhabhittisopānam itarataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The upper chamber should occupy half the site, or have an interval of one-third; its sides should be bonded with brick, with a clockwise stairway on the left and, on the other side, a stairway hidden in the wall.
The head of the archway should be two <s>hasta</s>s.
The two fittings for the door leaves should be in proportions of three and five parts.
There should be two locking bars.
The <s>indrakīla</s> door-pin should be an <s>aratni</s> long.
The <s>āṇi</s>-door should be five <s>hasta</s>s.
There should be four elephant-bars.
The <s>hastinakha</s> should be half the emplacement.

children.text: mukhasamaḥ saṃkramaḥ saṃhāryo bhūmimayo vā nirudake ||
children.translated_text: The bridge should be equal to the opening, removable, or, where there is no water, made of earth.

children.text: prākārasamaṃ mukham avasthāpya tribhāgagodhāmukhaṃ gopuraṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After setting the opening equal to the rampart, he should build a gate-tower with a <s>godhāmukha</s> of one-third.

children.text: prākāramadhye vāpīṃ kṛtvā puṣkariṇīdvāram catuḥśālam adhyardhāntaraṃ sāṇikaṃ kumārīpuram muṇḍaharmyadvitalaṃ muṇḍakadvāram bhūmidravyavaśena vā niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of the rampart, after making a reservoir, he should lay out a lotus-pool gate, a four-halled structure with an interval of one and a half, furnished with <s>āṇi</s>s, a <s>kumārīpura</s>, a two-storeyed flat-roofed palace, and a flat gate, or else according to the ground and materials available.
He should make channels for carrying stores, their length greater by one-third.
In them there should be stone picks, axes, and prepared pieces of timber,
cudgels, hammers, rods, wheel-engines, and <s>śataghnī</s>s.
Ironworkers' implements, spears, and bamboos with piercing tips should be made,
along with camel-neck devices, fire-combinations, and the procedure prescribed for the preparation of inflammable materials.

children.text: trayaḥ prācīnā rājamārgāstraya udīcīnā iti vāstuvibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Three royal roads should run eastward and three northward: this is the division of the site.
It should have twelve gates and be furnished with water, winding ways, and hidden paths.
The streets should have intervals of four <s>daṇḍa</s>s.

The royal roads, the roads to <s>droṇamukha</s>s, local centers, districts, and pastures, and the roads to assembly grounds, battle formations, cremation grounds, and villages should be eight <s>daṇḍa</s>s wide.

children.text: caturdaṇḍaḥ setuvanapathaḥ dvidaṇḍo hastikṣetrapathaḥ pañcāratnayo rathapathaḥ catvāraḥ paśupathaḥ dvau kṣudrapaśumanuṣyapathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A road to bridges and forests should be four <s>daṇḍa</s>s wide; a road to elephant grounds, two <s>daṇḍa</s>s; a chariot road, five <s>aratni</s>s; a cattle road, four; and a road for small animals and men, two.
On the best site, with communities and livelihoods for the four <s>varṇa</s>s, there should be the royal residence.

children.text: vāstuhṛdayād uttare navabhāge yathoktavidhānam antaḥpuraṃ prāṅmukham udaṅmukhaṃ vā kārayet ||
children.translated_text: North of the heart of the site, in the ninth division, he should construct the inner palace according to the prescribed rule, facing east or north.

children.text: tasya pūrvottaraṃ bhāgam ācāryapurohitejyātoyasthānaṃ mantriṇaścāvaseyuḥ pūrvadakṣiṇaṃ bhāgam mahānasaṃ hastiśālā koṣṭhāgāraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In its northeastern part the teacher, the household priest, the places for sacrifice and water, and the ministers should reside; in the southeastern part should be the great kitchen, the elephant stable, and the granary.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ gandhamālyarasapaṇyāḥ prasādhanakāravaḥ kṣatriyāśca pūrvāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that, dealers in perfumes, garlands, essences, and wares, makers of ornaments and cosmetics, and <s>kṣatriya</s>s should inhabit the eastern direction.

children.text: dakṣiṇapūrvaṃ bhāgaṃ bhāṇḍāgāram akṣapaṭalaṃ karmaniṣadyāśca dakṣiṇapaścimaṃ bhāgaṃ kupyagṛham āyudhāgāraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the southeastern part should be the storehouse, the accounts office, and the work-stations; in the southwestern part, the storehouse for raw materials and the armory.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ nagaradhānyavyāvahārikakārmāntikabalādhyakṣāḥ pakvānnasurāmāṃsapaṇyā rūpājīvāstālāvacarā vaiśyāśca dakṣiṇāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that, the superintendents of the city, royal grain, legal affairs, workshops, and the army, sellers of cooked food, liquor, and meat, women who live by beauty, performers, and <s>vaiśya</s>s should inhabit the southern direction.

children.text: paścimadakṣiṇaṃ bhāgaṃ kharoṣṭraguptisthānaṃ karmagṛhaṃ ca paścimottaraṃ bhāgaṃ yānarathaśālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the southwestern part should be the station for guarding donkeys and camels and the workshop; in the northwestern part, the sheds for vehicles and chariots.

children.text: tataḥ param ūrṇāsūtraveṇucarmavarmaśastrāvaraṇakāravaḥ śūdrāśca paścimāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that, makers of wool, thread, bamboo, leather, armor, weapons, and coverings, and <s>śūdra</s>s should inhabit the western direction.

children.text: uttarapaścimaṃ bhāgaṃ paṇyabhaiṣajyagṛham uttarapūrvaṃ bhāgaṃ kośo gavāśvaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the northwestern part should be the house for merchandise and medicines; in the northeastern part, the treasury and the cattle and horses.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ nagararājadevatālohamaṇikāravo brāhmaṇāścottarāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that, the city and royal deities, workers in metal and jewels, and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s should inhabit the northern direction.
In the vacant spaces and adjoining halls of the site, guilds, traders, and corporate groups should reside.

In the middle of the city he should construct sanctuaries for <s>Aparājitā</s>, <s>Apratihata</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Vaijayanta</s>, and houses for <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, and <s>Madirā</s>.
He should establish the <s>vāstu</s>-deities in their designated places.
The gates should be those of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and the commander of the army.

children.text: bahiḥ parikhāyā dhanuḥśatāpakṛṣṭāś caityapuṇyasthānavanasetubandhāḥ kāryāḥ yathādiśaṃ ca digdevatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Outside the moat, set back by a hundred bows, he should make shrines, sacred places, groves, and embankments, and he should place the directional deities according to the directions.

children.text: uttaraḥ pūrvo vā śmaśānabhāgo varṇottamānām dakṣiṇena śmaśānaṃ varṇāvarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: The northern or eastern cremation ground should be for the higher <s>varṇa</s>s; the cremation ground to the south should be for the lower <s>varṇa</s>s.
For transgressing that, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies.
The residence of sectarians and <s>caṇḍāla</s>s should be at the end of the cremation ground.
He should establish the boundaries of householders according to the workshops and fields.
In those areas, when permitted, they may make flower and fruit gardens and stores of grain and merchandise.
The site for a well should be a ten-<s>kulī</s> enclosure.

He should have stores made of all oils and fats, grain, alkali, salt, perfumes, medicines, dried vegetables, fodder, dried meat, grass, wood, metal, hides, charcoal, sinew, poison, horn, bamboo, bark, hard timber, weapons, armor, and stones, sufficient for use over many years.
He should keep the old stock fresh by replacing it with new.
He should station elephant, horse, chariot, and infantry forces under multiple chiefs.
For, when it has multiple chiefs, it does not yield to enemy instigation because of mutual fear.
By this, the preparation of frontier-guard forts has been explained.

children.text: na ca bāhirikān kuryāt pure rāṣṭropaghātakān
children.translated_text: And he should not place in the city outsiders who would injure the realm;

children.text: kṣipejjanapade caitān sarvān vā dāpayet karān ||
children.translated_text: he should send these into the countryside, or cause them all to pay taxes.

children.text: saṃnidhātā kośagṛhaṃ paṇyagṛhaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ kupyagṛham āyudhāgāraṃ bandhanāgāraṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃnidhātā</s> should have a treasury, a merchandise store, a granary, a raw-materials store, an armory, and a prison constructed.

children.text: caturaśrāṃ vāpīm anudakopasnehāṃ khānayitvā pṛthuśilābhir ubhayataḥ pārśvaṃ mūlaṃ ca pracitya sāradārupañjaraṃ bhūmisamaṃ tritalam anekavidhānaṃ kuṭṭimadeśasthānatalam ekadvāraṃ yantrayuktasopānaṃ bhūmigṛhaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After having a square pit dug, free from water-seepage, and lining its sides and bottom with broad stones on both sides, he should construct an underground chamber with a frame of hard timber, level with the ground, three-storied, with many arrangements, with paved areas and floors, a single door, and a mechanized stairway.

children.text: tasyoparyubhayatoniṣedhaṃ sapragrīvam aiṣṭakaṃ bhāṇḍavāhinīparikṣiptaṃ kośagṛhaṃ kārayet prāsādaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Above it he should construct the treasury, or a palace: a brick building with barriers on both sides, with a projecting neck, and enclosed by a passage for carrying goods.
At the edge of the countryside he should have a permanent hidden reserve made by men who have been cast off, for use in emergencies.

children.text: pakveṣṭakāstambhaṃ catuḥśālam ekadvāram anekasthānatalaṃ vivṛtastambhāpasāram ubhayataḥ paṇyagṛhaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ ca dīrghabahuśālaṃ kakṣyāvṛtakuḍyam antaḥ kupyagṛham tad eva bhūmigṛhayuktam āyudhāgāraṃ pṛthagdharmasthīyaṃ mahāmātrīyaṃ vibhaktastrīpuruṣasthānam apasārataḥ suguptakakṣyaṃ bandhanāgāraṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should construct the merchandise store and the granary with baked-brick pillars, four halls, one door, many rooms and floors, and open passage around the pillars on both sides; the raw-materials store should be inside, long, with many halls, its wall enclosed by chambers; the armory should be the same but furnished with an underground chamber; and the prison should be separate from the court and the officials' quarters, with men's and women's places divided, withdrawn, and with well-guarded cells.
He should make the halls of all of them furnished with pits and wells, bathing rooms, protection against fire and poison, guards of cats and mongooses, and worship of their respective deities.
In the granary he should set up a rain-measuring basin with a mouth one <s>aratni</s> wide.

children.text: tajjātakaraṇādhiṣṭhitaḥ purāṇaṃ navaṃ ca ratnaṃ sāraṃ phalgu kupyaṃ vā pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Under the supervision of officials skilled in each class, he should receive old and new jewels, high-grade goods, inferior goods, or raw materials.

children.text: tatra ratnopadhāv uttamo daṇḍaḥ kartuḥ kārayituśca sāropadhau madhyamaḥ phalgukupyopadhau tacca tāvacca daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, for adulteration of jewels the highest fine applies to the doer and to the one who caused it to be done; for adulteration of high-grade goods, the middle fine; for adulteration of inferior goods or raw materials, a fine of that value and the same amount besides.
He should accept gold certified as pure by the assayer.
He should have impure metal cut apart.
The bringer incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: śuddhaṃ pūrṇam abhinavaṃ ca dhānyaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should accept grain that is pure, full in measure, and fresh.
In the opposite case, the fine is twice the value.

children.text: tena paṇyaṃ kupyam āyudhaṃ ca vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: By this, merchandise, raw materials, and weapons have been explained.

In all departments, for officials, subordinate officials, and their servants, in cases of embezzlement beginning with one <s>paṇa</s> and extending up to four <s>paṇa</s>s, the penalties are the first, middle, and highest fines, ending in death.
For the officer placed over the treasury, death is the penalty when the treasury is breached.
For those who do service for him, the fines are half.
If it is not known, there should be formal questioning.
For thieves who break in violently, the penalty is death by torture.
Therefore the <s>saṃnidhātā</s>, with trustworthy men in charge, should manage the stores.

children.text: bāhyam abhyantaraṃ cāyaṃ vidyād varṣaśatād api
children.translated_text: He should know both this external and internal income, even after a hundred years,

children.text: yathā pṛṣṭo na sajjeta vyaye śeṣe ca saṃcaye ||
children.translated_text: so that, when questioned, he does not become confused about expenditure, balance, and accumulation.

children.text: samāhartā durgaṃ rāṣṭraṃ khaniṃ setuṃ vanaṃ vrajaṃ vaṇikpathaṃ cāvekṣeta ||
children.translated_text: The <s>samāhartā</s> should inspect the fort, the countryside, the mine, the irrigation works, the forest, the herd, and the trade route.

children.text: śulkaṃ daṇḍaḥ pautavaṃ nāgariko lakṣaṇādhyakṣo mudrādhyakṣaḥ surā sūnā sūtraṃ tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣāraḥ sauvarṇikaḥ paṇyasaṃsthā veśyā dyūtaṃ vāstukaṃ kāruśilpigaṇo devatādhyakṣo dvārabāhirikādeyaṃ ca durgam ||
children.translated_text: Customs, fines, weights and measures, the city superintendent, the superintendent of marks, the superintendent of seals, liquor, slaughterhouses, thread, oil, ghee, alkali, the goldsmith, the market establishment, prostitutes, gambling, building property, the guild of artisans and craftsmen, the superintendent of temples, and dues from gates and outsiders: these are the fort revenues.

children.text: sītā bhāgo baliḥ karo vaṇik nadīpālastaro nāvaḥ pattanaṃ vivicitaṃ vartanī rajjuścorarajjuśca rāṣṭram ||
children.translated_text: Crown land, the king's share, <s>bali</s>, tax, merchants, river-guards, ferry dues, boats, ports, grazing grounds, road tolls, <s>rajju</s> (measuring-rope dues), and <s>corarajju</s> (thief-related dues): these are the countryside revenues.
Gold, silver, diamonds, gems, pearls, coral, shells, metals, salt, earth, stone, mineral substances, and ores are the mine revenues.
Flower and fruit gardens, plantations, fields, roots, and reservoirs are the irrigation-works revenues.
The holdings of domestic animals, wild animals, forest produce, and elephant forests are the forest revenues.

children.text: gomahiṣam ajāvikaṃ kharoṣṭram aśvāśvataraṃ ca vrajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cattle and buffaloes, goats and sheep, donkeys and camels, and horses and mules are the herd revenues.
Land routes and water routes are the trade routes.
Thus is the body of revenue.

children.text: mūlyaṃ bhāgo vyājī parighaḥ kﾱptaṃ rūpikam atyayaścāyamukham ||
children.translated_text: Price, share, surcharge, barrier-duty, fixed dues, coinage fee, and penalties are the heads of income.

children.text: devapitṛpūjādānārtham svastivācanam antaḥpuram mahānasam dūtaprāvartimam koṣṭhāgāram āyudhāgāram paṇyagṛham kupyagṛham karmānto viṣṭiḥ pattyaśvarathadvipaparigraho gomaṇḍalam paśumṛgapakṣivyālavāṭāḥ kāṣṭhatṛṇavāṭāśceti vyayaśarīram ||
children.translated_text: The body of expenditure consists of benedictory rites for worship of gods and ancestors and for gifts, the inner palace, the great kitchen, dispatch of messengers, the granary, the armory, the merchandise store, the raw-materials store, workshops, forced labor, the maintenance of infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants, the cattle herd, enclosures for domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and dangerous beasts, and plantations of timber and grass.

children.text: rājavarṣaṃ māsaḥ pakṣo divasaśca vyuṣṭam varṣāhemantagrīṣmāṇāṃ tṛtīyasaptamā divasonāḥ pakṣāḥ śeṣāḥ pūrṇāḥ pṛthagadhimāsakaḥ iti kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The royal year, the month, the fortnight, the day, and the elapsed time; in the rainy, winter, and summer seasons the third and seventh fortnights are deficient by a day, the remaining ones are full, and there is a separate intercalary month: this is time.

children.text: karaṇīyaṃ siddhaṃ śeṣam āyavyayau nīvī ca ||
children.translated_text: What is to be done, what has been completed, what remains, income and expenditure, and the net reserve.

children.text: saṃsthānaṃ pracāraḥ śarīrāvasthāpanam ādānaṃ sarvasamudayapiṇḍaḥ saṃjātaṃ etat karaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: The establishment, operation, arrangement of the body, receipt, the aggregate total of all collections, and what has accrued: this is what is to be done.

children.text: kośārpitaṃ rājahāraḥ puravyayaśca praviṣṭaṃ paramasaṃvatsarānuvṛttaṃ śāsanamuktaṃ mukhājñaptaṃ cāpātanīyaṃ etat siddham ||
children.translated_text: Deposited in the treasury, the royal due, city expenditure that has been entered, what has continued from a previous year, what has been remitted by written order, and what has been commanded orally to be brought in: this is <s>siddha</s> (realized revenue).

children.text: siddhikarmayogaḥ daṇḍaśeṣam āharaṇīyaṃ balātkṛtapratiṣṭabdham avamṛṣṭaṃ ca praśodhyaṃ etaccheṣam asāram alpasāraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The arrangement of work for realization, arrears of fines, what is to be collected, what has been forcibly obstructed, and what has been seized should be cleared; this is the <s>śeṣa</s> (outstanding balance), either without substance or of little substance.
<s>Āya</s> (income) is current, stale, and of another kind.
Current income is what continues day by day.
Stale income is what belongs to more than one year, or what has passed over from another operating account.

children.text: naṣṭaprasmṛtam āyuktadaṇḍaḥ pārśvaṃ pārihīṇikam aupāyanikaṃ ḍamaragatakasvam aputrakaṃ nidhiścānyajātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lost or forgotten property, fines imposed on officials, side income, compensation for deficiency, presents, property of those gone into rebellion, heirless property, and treasure trove are income of another kind.
The grounds for expenditure are balances left from delay, illness, or the start of another undertaking.

children.text: vikriye paṇyānām arghavṛddhir upajā mānonmānaviśeṣo vyājī krayasaṃgharṣe vārdhavṛddhiḥ ityāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In sales, an increase in the price of merchandise, incidental profit, differences in measuring and weighing, <s>vyājī</s> (surcharge), and an increase caused by competition in buying are income.

children.text: nityo nityotpādiko lābho lābhotpādika iti vyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyaya</s> (expenditure) is regular, productive of regular income, profit, and productive of profit.
What continues day by day is regular.
Profit is gain over a fortnight, a month, or a year.

children.text: tayor utpanno nityotpādiko lābhotpādika iti vyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Expenditure arising from the two is called productive of regular income and productive of profit.

children.text: saṃjātād āyavyayaviśuddhā nīvī prāptā cānuvṛttā ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nīvī</s> (net balance), cleared from accrued income and expenditure, is either received or carried forward.

children.text: evaṃ kuryāt samudayaṃ vṛddhiṃ cāyasya darśayet
children.translated_text: In this way the wise man should make the aggregate and show the increase of income;

children.text: hrāsaṃ vyayasya ca prājñaḥ sādhayecca viparyayam ||
children.translated_text: and the decrease of expenditure; he should also determine the reverse.

children.text: akṣapaṭalam adhyakṣaḥ prāṅmukham udaṅmukhaṃ vā vibhaktopasthānaṃ nibandhapustakasthānaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent should have the <s>akṣapaṭala</s> (accounts office) built facing east or north, with separate stations and a place for the account books.

children.text: tatrādhikaraṇānāṃ saṃkhyāpracārasaṃjātāgram karmāntānāṃ dravyaprayogavṛddhikṣayavyayaprayāmavyājīyogasthānavetanaviṣṭipramāṇam ratnasāraphalgukupyānām arghaprativarṇakamānapratimānonmānāvamānabhāṇḍam deśagrāmajātikulasaṃghānāṃ dharmavyavahāracaritrasaṃsthānam rājopajīvināṃ pragrahapradeśabhogaparihārabhaktavetanalābham rājñaśca patnīputrāṇāṃ ratnabhūmilābhaṃ nirdeśotpātikapratīkāralābham mitrāmitrāṇāṃ ca saṃdhivigrahapradānādānaṃ nibandhapustakasthaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: There he should have entered in the account book: for the departments, the totals of number, operation, and accrued revenue; for workshops, the quantity of materials, use, increase, loss, expenditure, extent, surplus, balances, location, wages, and forced labor; for jewels, valuable goods, lesser goods, and forest produce, price, description by grade, measure, standard measure, weighing, deficient weighing, and vessels; for regions, villages, castes, families, and guilds, their <s>dharma</s> (norm), legal practice, custom, and constitution; for those maintained by the king, grants, assigned districts, enjoyments, exemptions, rations, salaries, and gains; for the king's wives and sons, jewels, land, acquisitions, instructed grants, occasional receipts, and compensatory receipts; and for friends and enemies, giving and taking in treaties and hostilities.

children.text: tataḥ sarvādhikaraṇānāṃ karaṇīyaṃ siddhaṃ śeṣam āyavyayau nīvīm upasthānaṃ pracāraṃ caritraṃ saṃsthānaṃ ca nibandhena prayacchet ||
children.translated_text: Then for all departments he should provide by written register what is to be done, what has been realized, the remainder, income and expenditure, net balance, attendance, operations, custom, and constitution.

children.text: uttamamadhyamāvareṣu ca karmasu tajjātikam adhyakṣaṃ kuryāt sāmudayikeṣvavakﾱptikam vyayam upahatya rājā nānutapyeta ||
children.translated_text: In works of superior, middling, and inferior rank he should appoint a superintendent of the same class; in collective works, one suited to the aggregate. Once expenditure has been properly checked, the king should not regret it.

children.text: sahagrāhiṇaḥ pratibhuvaḥ karmopajīvinaḥ putrā bhrātaro bhāryā duhitaro bhṛtyāścāsya karmacchedaṃ vaheyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: His co-receivers, sureties, those who live from the work, sons, brothers, wife, daughters, and servants should bear responsibility for an interruption of his work.
Three hundred and fifty-four days and nights make the working year.

children.text: tam āṣāḍhīparyavasānam ūnaṃ pūrṇaṃ vā dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should submit that account, deficient or complete, ending with <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>.
He should make the intercalary month dependent on the calculating office.
And he should make the operations dependent on secret agents.

children.text: pracāracaritrasaṃsthānānyanupalabhamāno hi prakṛtaḥ samudayam ajñānena parihāpayati utthānakleśāsahatvād ālasyena śabdādiṣvindriyārtheṣu prasaktaḥ pramādena saṃkrośādharmānarthabhīrubhayena kāryārthiṣvanugrahabuddhiḥ kāmena hiṃsābuddhiḥ kopena vidyādravyavallabhāpāśrayād darpeṇa tulāmānatarkagaṇitāntaropadhānāl lobhena ||
children.translated_text: For an appointed officer who does not grasp operations, custom, and institutional arrangements reduces the total through ignorance; through idleness, because he cannot endure exertion and hardship; through negligence, when attached to sense objects such as sound; through fear, when afraid of denunciation, unrighteousness, or material harm; through desire, when he is minded to favor petitioners; through anger, when he is minded to injure; through arrogance, relying on learning, wealth, or favorites; and through greed, by inserting discrepancies in balance, measure, reasoning, and calculation.

children.text: teṣām ānupūrvyā yāvān arthopaghātastāvān ekottaro daṇḍaḥ iti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For these, in their order, the fine should rise one step above the amount of injury to wealth, say the <s>Mānava</s>s.
The <s>Pārāśara</s>s say that it is eightfold in every case.
The <s>Bārhaspatya</s>s say that it is tenfold.
The <s>Auśanasa</s>s say that it is twentyfold.
<s>Kauṭilya</s> says: according to the offense.
The accounting officers should arrive at <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>.
After those with seals, books, goods, and balances have arrived, he should have them confined in one place without conversation.
After hearing the totals of income, expenditure, and balances, he should have the net balance set down.

children.text: yaccāgrād āyasyāntaraparṇe nīvyāṃ vardheta vyayasya vā yat parihāpayet tad aṣṭaguṇam adhyakṣaṃ dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever, beyond the total, increases on the inner page in income or in the balance, or whatever of expenditure he causes to be reduced, he should make the superintendent pay eightfold.
In the opposite case, the same should apply against him.

children.text: yathākālam anāgatānām apustakabhāṇḍanīvīkānāṃ vā deyadaśabandho daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those who do not arrive at the proper time, or who lack books, goods, or balances, the fine is one-tenth of what is payable.
When the <s>kārmika</s> (work official) is present, if the <s>kāraṇika</s> (clerk) fails to enter him, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies.
In the reverse case, it is double for the <s>kārmika</s>.
The high officers, assembled and unanimous in counsel, should announce the account in conformity with the operations.

children.text: pṛthagbhūto mithyāvādī caiṣām uttamaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Any one of them who stands apart and speaks falsely should pay the highest fine.
He should wait one month for a daily statement-remittance not yet made.
After a month, he should pay a fine increased by two hundred per month.
He should wait five nights for a written balance entry and <s>nīvī</s> when only a small remainder is outstanding.

After that, beginning with the treasury, he should examine the daily statement-remittance by methods of compiling and determining <s>dharma</s>, legal practice, custom, and institutional arrangement, and by inference and the use of spies.
And he should reconcile them by day, five-night period, fortnight, month, four-month season, and year.
He should reconcile the income according to the posted date, place, time, account-head, source, continuance, amount, payer, payment-enforcer, registrar, and receiver.
He should reconcile expenditure according to the posted date, place, time, account-head, cause of gain, payment due, apportionment, amount, authorizer, drawer, allocator, and recipient.
He should reconcile the <s>nīvī</s> (net balance) according to the posted date, place, time, account-head, continuance, form, identifying marks, amount, deposit vessel, and custodians.

children.text: rājārthe kāraṇikasyāpratibadhnataḥ pratiṣedhayato vājñāṃ nibandhād āyavyayam anyathā nīvīm avalikhato dviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a clerk who, in a royal matter, fails to prevent wrongdoing or obstructs an order, or who records income, expenditure, or <s>nīvī</s> otherwise than according to the register, the penalty is double.

children.text: kramāvahīnam utkramam avijñātaṃ punaruktaṃ vā vastukam avalikhato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For recording an item as deficient in sequence, out of sequence, unknown, or repeated, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
For falsely recording the <s>nīvī</s> (net balance), the penalty is double.
For consuming it, the penalty is eightfold.
For destroying it, there is a <s>pañcabandha</s> penalty and restitution.
For a false statement, the penalty is that for theft.
If it is admitted later, or if a forgotten item comes to light, the penalty is double.
He should tolerate a small offense and be satisfied even with a small recovery,
and he should honor with favor a superintendent who has rendered great service.
All undertakings have the treasury as their prerequisite.
Therefore he should examine the treasury first.

children.text: pracārasamṛddhiścaritrānugrahaścoranigraho yuktapratiṣedhaḥ sasyasampat paṇyabāhulyam upasargapramokṣaḥ parihārakṣayo hiraṇyopāyanam iti kośavṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The growth of the <s>kośa</s> (treasury) consists in prosperity of circulation, encouragement of proper conduct, suppression of thieves, restraint of assigned officials, abundance of crops, plenty of merchandise, relief from calamities, reduction of exemptions, and bringing in money.

children.text: pratibandhaḥ prayogo vyavahāro 'vastāraḥ parihāpaṇam upabhogaḥ parivartanam apahāraśceti kośakṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Obstruction, investment, trade, misdating, diminution, use, exchange, and misappropriation are depletion of the <s>kośa</s> (treasury).

children.text: siddhīnām asādhanam anavatāraṇam apraveśanaṃ vā pratibandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Obstruction is the failure to realize, bring in, or enter revenues that have been secured.
There the fine is the <s>daśabandha</s> penalty.
Investment is the placing out of treasury goods for increase.
Trade is dealing in merchandise.
There the fine is twice the profit.

children.text: siddhaṃ kālam aprāptaṃ karoty aprāptaṃ prāptaṃ vetyavastāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Avastāra</s> is making a secured amount appear not yet due, or an amount not yet due appear due.
There the fine is the <s>pañcabandha</s> penalty.

children.text: kﾱptam āyaṃ parihāpayati vyayaṃ vā vivardhayatīti parihāpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parihāpaṇa</s> is causing prescribed income to be diminished or expenditure to be increased.
There the fine is four times the deficiency.

children.text: svayam anyair vā rājadravyāṇām upabhojanam upabhogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upabhoga</s> is the use of royal goods by oneself or by others.

children.text: tatra ratnopabhoge ghātaḥ sāropabhoge madhyamaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ phalgukupyopabhoge tacca tāvacca daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, for using jewels there is death; for using valuable goods, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine; and for using inferior raw materials, the fine is that item and the same amount again.
<s>Parivartana</s> (exchange) is taking royal goods by means of other goods.
That has been explained by the rule on <s>upabhoga</s>.

children.text: siddham āyaṃ na praveśayati nibaddhaṃ vyayaṃ na prayacchati prāptāṃ nīvīṃ vipratijānīta ityapahāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Apahāra</s> (misappropriation) is not entering income that has been secured, not paying expenditure that has been registered, or denying a received <s>nīvī</s> balance.
There the fine is twelvefold.
There are forty methods for taking them away.

children.text: pūrvaṃ siddhaṃ paścād avatāritam paścāt siddhaṃ pūrvam avatāritam sādhyaṃ na siddham asādhyaṃ siddham siddham asiddhaṃ kṛtam asiddhaṃ siddhaṃ kṛtam alpasiddhaṃ bahu kṛtam bahusiddham alpaṃ kṛtam anyat siddham anyat kṛtam anyataḥ siddham anyataḥ kṛtam deyaṃ na dattam adeyaṃ dattam kāle na dattam akāle dattam alpaṃ dattaṃ bahu kṛtam bahu dattam alpaṃ kṛtam anyad dattam anyat kṛtam anyato dattam anyataḥ kṛtam praviṣṭam apraviṣṭaṃ kṛtam apraviṣṭaṃ praviṣṭaṃ kṛtam kupyam adattamūlyaṃ praviṣṭam dattamūlyaṃ na praviṣṭaṃ saṃkṣepo vikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ vikṣepaḥ saṃkṣepo vā mahārgham alpārgheṇa parivartitam alpārghaṃ mahārgheṇa vā samāropito 'rghaḥ pratyavaropito vā saṃvatsaro māsaviṣamaḥ kṛtaḥ māso divasaviṣamo vā samāgamaviṣamaḥ mukhaviṣamaḥ kārmikaviṣamaḥ nirvartanaviṣamaḥ piṇḍaviṣamaḥ varṇaviṣamaḥ arghaviṣamaḥ mānaviṣamaḥ māpanaviṣamaḥ bhājanaviṣamaḥ iti haraṇopāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are: entering what was secured earlier as later; entering what was secured later as earlier; treating what is to be secured as not secured; treating what is not to be secured as secured; making the secured unsecured; making the unsecured secured; making a small secured amount large; making a large secured amount small; treating one secured item as another; treating what was secured from one source as from another; not giving what is payable; giving what is not payable; not giving at the proper time; giving at an improper time; making a small payment into a large one; making a large payment into a small one; making one payment into another; making what was given from one source into what was given from another; making an entered item unentered; making an unentered item entered; entering a commodity whose price has not been paid; not entering one whose price has been paid; making an aggregate into a dispersion, or a dispersion into an aggregate; exchanging a high-priced item for a low-priced one, or a low-priced item for a high-priced one; raising the price or lowering it; making a year uneven by months, or a month uneven by days; discrepancy in totals, account-heads, workers, output, lump sums, quality, price, measure, measuring, or containers. These are the methods of taking away.
In that matter he should interrogate one by one the official in charge, the keeper, the registrar, the receiver, the giver, the payer, the minister, and the attendants.
For false statements by these, the fine is the same as for the assigned official.

children.text: pracāre cāvaghoṣayet amunā prakṛtenopahatāḥ prajñāpayantu iti ||
children.translated_text: And he should have a proclamation made publicly: 'Those harmed by this man under inquiry should report it.'
When someone reports, he should make compensation paid according to the injury.

children.text: anekeṣu cābhiyogeṣvapavyayamānaḥ sakṛd eva paroktaḥ sarvaṃ bhajeta ||
children.translated_text: And when there are many accusations, if he cannot clear himself and is accused even once by another, he should be liable for all.
In every discrepancy he should institute an inquiry.
In a great embezzlement of property, if he is proved guilty even by a small part, he should be liable for the whole.

children.text: kṛtapratighātāvasthaḥ sūcako niṣpannārthaḥ ṣaṣṭham aṃśaṃ labheta dvādaśam aṃśaṃ bhṛtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: An informer, when counter-obstruction has been made and the matter is successful, should receive a sixth share; a hired informer should receive a twelfth share.
If, after a large accusation, only a small amount is proved, he should receive a share of the amount proved.

children.text: aniṣpanne śārīraṃ hairaṇyaṃ vā daṇḍaṃ labheta na cānugrāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is not proved, he should receive a corporal or monetary punishment and should not be favored.
If, when the case succeeds, he abandons the charge or withdraws himself,
then, when this is due to subornation by the accused, the informer incurs death.
All superintendents, endowed with the qualities of ministers, should be assigned to duties according to their ability.

children.text: karmasu caiṣāṃ nityaṃ parīkṣāṃ kārayet cittānityatvān manuṣyānām ||
children.translated_text: And in their duties he should always have them examined, because human minds are unstable.

children.text: aśvasadharmāṇo hi manuṣyā niyuktāḥ karmasu vikurvate ||
children.translated_text: For men, like horses, change their nature when appointed to tasks.

children.text: tasmāt kartāraṃ karaṇaṃ deśaṃ kālaṃ kāryaṃ prakṣepam udayaṃ caiṣu vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in these matters he should know the doer, the means, the place, the time, the work, the outlay, and the yield.

children.text: te yathāsaṃdeśam asaṃhatā avigṛhītāḥ karmāṇi kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should perform their tasks according to instruction, neither joined in collusion nor split by quarrel.
If joined together, they would embezzle; if quarrelling, they would destroy the work.

children.text: na cānivedya bhartuḥ kaṃcid ārambhaṃ kuryuḥ anyatrāpatpratīkārebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should not undertake any enterprise without informing the master, except for countermeasures in emergencies.
For occasions of negligence he should set their penalty at twice the cost of a day's wages and expenses.

children.text: yaścaiṣāṃ yathādiṣṭam arthaṃ saviśeṣaṃ vā karoti sa sthānamānau labheta ||
children.translated_text: And whichever of them accomplishes the assigned matter as ordered, or with some distinction, should receive office and honor.
If income is small while expense is great, he is embezzling.
In the opposite case, and when expense accords with income, he is not embezzling, say the teachers.
<s>Kauṭilya</s> says that this is to be detected only through an <s>apasarpa</s> (secret agent).

children.text: yaḥ samudayaṃ parihāpayati sa rājārthaṃ bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: One who diminishes the total revenue is embezzling the king's wealth.

children.text: sa ced ajñānādibhiḥ parihāpayati tad enaṃ yathāguṇaṃ dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: If he diminishes it through ignorance and the like, then he should be made to pay according to the degree of fault.

children.text: yaḥ samudayaṃ dviguṇam udbhāvayati sa janapadaṃ bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: One who declares the total revenue to be doubled is consuming the countryside.

children.text: sa ced rājārtham upanayatyalpāparādhe vārayitavyaḥ mahati yathāparādhaṃ daṇḍayitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he brings the king's wealth in, he should be checked for a minor offense; for a great one he should be punished according to the offense.

children.text: yaḥ samudayaṃ vyayam upanayati sa puruṣakarmāṇi bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: One who turns the total revenue into expenditure is consuming the labor of men.
He should be punished according to the offense for misappropriations involving work-days, materials, prices, and men's wages.

children.text: tasmād asya yo yasminn adhikaraṇe śāsanasthaḥ sa tasya karmaṇo yāthātathyam āyavyayau ca vyāsasamāsābhyām ācakṣīta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, whoever is appointed by order in whatever department should report truthfully on its work, and on income and expenditure, both in detail and in summary.
He should also prohibit the <s>mūlahara</s>, the <s>tādātvika</s>, and the <s>kadarya</s>.

children.text: yaḥ pitṛpaitāmaham artham anyāyena bhakṣayati sa mūlaharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who unjustly consumes paternal and ancestral wealth is a <s>mūlahara</s> (root-capital devourer).

children.text: yo yad yad utpadyate tat tad bhakṣayati sa tādātvikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who consumes whatever arises as it arises is a <s>tādātvika</s> (immediate consumer).
One who piles up wealth by oppressing his servants and himself is a <s>kadarya</s> (miser).
If such a man has a faction, he is not to be taken on; in the opposite case, he should be stripped of his assets.

children.text: yo mahatyarthasamudaye sthitaḥ kadaryaḥ saṃnidhatte 'vanidhatte 'vasrāvayati vā saṃnidhatte svaveśmani avanidhatte paurajānapadeṣu avasrāvayati paraviṣaye tasya sattrī mantrimitrabhṛtyabandhupakṣam āgatiṃ gatiṃ ca dravyāṇām upalabheta ||
children.translated_text: When a <s>kadarya</s> who is placed over a great accumulation of wealth stores, deposits, or drains it away--he stores it in his own house, deposits it among townsmen and country people, or drains it into another realm--a <s>sattrī</s> (secret agent) should discover his ministers, friends, servants, kinsmen, faction, and the coming and going of his property.

children.text: yaścāsya paraviṣaye saṃcāraṃ kuryāt tam anupraviśya mantraṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: And whoever carries out his movements in another realm, the agent should infiltrate that man and learn the plan.
When it is well known, he should have him killed under the pretext of an enemy's order.
Therefore, in his work, he should appoint superintendents who are associates of the accountant, scribe, examiner of coin-stamps, receiver of the reserve fund, and superior superintendent.
The superior superintendents should be elephant-, horse-, and chariot-riders.
Their resident apprentices, endowed with technical skill and integrity, should be <s>apasarpa</s>s (secret informants) among the accountants and the others.
He should establish a department with many heads and with non-permanent tenure.

children.text: yathā hyanāsvādayituṃ na śakyaṃ jihvātalasthaṃ madhu vā viṣaṃ vā
children.translated_text: For just as honey or poison placed on the tip of the tongue cannot be left untasted,

children.text: arthastathā hyarthacareṇa rājñaḥ svalpo 'pyanāsvādayituṃ na śakyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so even a little of the king's wealth cannot be left untasted by an official who handles wealth.

children.text: matsyā yathāntaḥ salile caranto jñātuṃ na śakyāḥ salilaṃ pibantaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as fish moving inside the water cannot be known when they are drinking water,

children.text: yuktāstathā kāryavidhau niyuktā jñātuṃ na śakyā dhanam ādadānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so officials appointed to the execution of work cannot be known when they are taking money.

children.text: api śakyā gatir jñātuṃ patatāṃ khe patatriṇām
children.translated_text: It may be possible to know the course of birds flying in the sky,

children.text: na tu pracchannabhāvānāṃ yuktānāṃ caratāṃ gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but not the course of officials who move about with hidden dispositions.
He should make those who have accumulated wealth discharge it and should rotate them among duties,

children.text: yathā na bhakṣayantyarthaṃ bhakṣitaṃ nirvamanti vā ||
children.translated_text: so that they do not embezzle wealth, or else vomit out what has been embezzled.

children.text: na bhakṣayanti ye tvarthān nyāyato vardhayanti ca
children.translated_text: But those who do not embezzle wealth and increase it lawfully
should be made permanent officers, devoted to what is dear and beneficial to the king.
In the matter of command, they call the written command <s>śāsana</s>.
For kings depend chiefly on <s>śāsana</s>, since alliance and conflict have it as their root.

children.text: tasmād amātyasampadopetaḥ sarvasamayavid āśugranthaścārvakṣaro lekhanavācanasamartho lekhakaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a scribe should possess the qualities of a minister, know all conventions, draft swiftly, write handsome letters, and be competent in writing and reading.

children.text: so 'vyagramanā rājñaḥ saṃdeśaṃ śrutvā niścitārthaṃ lekhaṃ vidadhyāt deśaiśvaryavaṃśanāmadheyopacāram īśvarasya deśanāmadheyopacāram anīśvarasya ||
