children.translated_text: With an undistracted mind, after hearing the king's message, he should compose a document whose meaning is fixed: for a sovereign, including the proper forms for country, sovereignty, lineage, and name; for a non-sovereign, the proper forms for country and name.
Caste, family, position, age, learning, actions, prosperity, character, and then place and time,

children.text: yaunānubandhaṃ ca samīkṣya kārye lekhaṃ vidadhyāt puruṣānurūpam ||
children.translated_text: and also marital connection: after considering these in the matter, he should compose the document according to the person.

children.text: arthakramaḥ sambandhaḥ paripūrṇatā mādhuryam audāryaṃ spaṣṭatvam iti lekhasampat ||
children.translated_text: Order of subject matter, coherence, completeness, sweetness, dignity, and clarity are the excellences of a document.

children.text: tatra yathāvad anupūrvakriyā pradhānasyārthasya pūrvam abhiniveśa ityarthakramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, correct sequential arrangement and setting down the principal matter first is order of subject matter.

children.text: prastutasyārthasyānuparodhād uttarasya vidhānam ā samāpter iti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Coherence is the statement of what follows, up to the conclusion, without obstructing the matter already introduced.
Completeness is there being neither too little nor too much in meanings, words, and syllables, the exposition of the matter with reasons, examples, and analogies, and wording that does not weary.
Sweetness is expression through pleasant and attractive meanings and words.
Dignity is expression without vulgar words.
Clarity is the use of well-known words.
The letters, beginning with <s>a</s>, are sixty-three.
A combination of letters is a word.
That is fourfold: noun, verb, prefix, and particle.
Among these, a noun denotes an entity.
A verb, not distinguished by gender, expresses an action.
Prefixes such as <s>pra</s> specify the action.
Indeclinables such as <s>ca</s> are particles.
A collection of words is a sentence when the meaning is complete.
A group should be made with one word at minimum and three words at maximum, without obstructing the meanings of the other words.
For concluding a document there is the word <s>iti</s>, and also the phrase, "This is his oral message."

children.text: nindā praśaṃsā pṛcchā ca tathākhyānam athārthanā
children.translated_text: Blame, praise, inquiry, and likewise statement, then request;
refusal, reproach, prohibition, and then command;
conciliation, assistance, and likewise intimidation and persuasion:
these are the thirteen matters arising in letters.
Among them, stating defects in lineage, body, or conduct is blame.
Stating the virtues of these same things is praise.
"How is this?" is inquiry.
"Thus it is" is statement.
"Give" is request.
"I do not give" is refusal.
"This is not fitting for you" is reproach.
"Do not do it" is prohibition.
"Let this be done" is command.

children.text: yo 'haṃ sa bhavān yan mama dravyaṃ tad bhavataḥ ityupagrahaḥ sāntvam ||
children.translated_text: The supportive formula, "As I am, so are you; what is my property is yours," is conciliation.
Assistance in calamity is help.
Pointing out a faulty future consequence is intimidation.
Persuasion is threefold: in an offence committed for gain, in a calamity involving persons and the like, and so on.
Notifications, commands, letters of grant, and likewise letters of exemption and delegation,

children.text: prāvṛttikaśca pratilekha eva sarvatragaśceti hi śāsanāni ||
children.translated_text: as well as reports, replies, and universal passes: these are royal documents.

children.text: anena vijñāpitam evam āha tad dīyatāṃ ced yadi tattvam asti
children.translated_text: "This has been reported by this person; he says thus. Let that be given, if there is truth in it."

children.text: rājñaḥ samīpe varakāram āha prajñāpanaiṣā vividhopadiṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: When it states a petition in the king's presence, this is a notification, taught in various forms.

children.text: bhartur ājñā bhaved yatra nigrahānugrahau prati
children.translated_text: Where there is an order of the master concerning punishment and favor,
especially in relation to servants, that is the mark of a letter of command.
Where honor endowed with qualities appropriate to rank is indicated,
whether in distress or in a grant, those two are favors.

children.text: jāter viśeṣeṣu pareṣu caiva grāmeṣu deśeṣu ca teṣu teṣu
children.translated_text: In special cases of birth, and also among others, in those various villages and regions,

children.text: anugraho yo nṛpater nideśāt tajjñaḥ parīhāra iti vyavasyet ||
children.translated_text: whatever favor is given by the king's order, the expert should determine that to be an exemption.
A communication that delegates and appoints, for carrying out a task and likewise for speech,

children.text: eṣa vācikalekhaḥ syād bhaven naisṛṣṭiko 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: may be an oral document; it may also be a delegated order.
A report may be varied, connected with fate, and also factual and human;

children.text: dvividhāṃ tāṃ vyavasyanti pravṛttiṃ śāsanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: with respect to an order, they determine that occurrence as twofold.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lekhaṃ yathātattvaṃ tataḥ pratyanubhāṣya ca
children.translated_text: After seeing a document according to the facts and then repeating it in reply,
a reply should be made just as the king's words require.
Where the king addresses lords and officials about protection and assistance for travelers,

children.text: sarvatrago nāma bhavet sa mārge deśe ca sarvatra ca veditavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is called a universal pass; it should be recognized everywhere, on the road and in the country.
The means are <s>sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>upapradāna</s> (material inducement), <s>bheda</s> (division), and <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment).

children.text: tatra sāma pañcavidhaṃ guṇasaṃkīrtanam sambandhopākhyānam parasparopakārasaṃdarśanam āyatipradarśanam ātmopanidhānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Among these, <s>sāma</s> is fivefold: praising qualities, recounting a relationship, showing mutual benefit, showing future advantage, and placing oneself at another's disposal.
There, taking up the merits of lineage, body, conduct, disposition, learning, wealth, and the like is praise, laudation, and praising of qualities.
Recounting connections through kinship, marriage, oral association, sacred learning, family, affection, and friendship is narration of relationship.
Mentioning the mutual benefit of one's own side and the other side is showing mutual benefit.

children.text: asmin evaṃ kṛta idam āvayor bhavati ityāśājananam āyatipradarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Creating the expectation, "When this has been done in this way, this will result for us both," is showing future advantage.

children.text: yo 'haṃ sa bhavān yan mama dravyaṃ tad bhavatā svakṛtyeṣu prayojyatām ityātmopanidhānam
children.translated_text: "As I am, so are you; whatever property is mine may be used by you in your own affairs" is placing oneself at another's disposal.
Thus.
<s>Upapradāna</s> is material assistance.
<s>Bheda</s> is creating suspicion and stern intimidation.
<s>Daṇḍa</s> is killing, harassment, and seizure of property.
Thus.

children.text: akāntir vyāghātaḥ punaruktam apaśabdaḥ samplava iti lekhadoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lack of appeal, contradiction, repetition, improper language, and confusion are faults of a document.
Among these, dark paper, unattractive and uneven writing, and letters without clear coloring are lack of appeal.
Contradiction is when the later part does not fit with the earlier.
A second utterance of what has already been said, without any distinction, is repetition.
The wrong use of gender, number, tense, and case is improper language.
Grouping where there should be no group, failing to group where there should be a group, and reversing qualities is confusion.
Thus.
After reviewing all the śāstras and observing practical usage,
<s>Kauṭilya</s> has made this rule for royal documents for the sake of kings.

children.text: kośādhyakṣaḥ kośapraveśyaṃ ratnaṃ sāraṃ phalguṃ kupyaṃ vā tajjātakaraṇādhiṣṭhitaḥ pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of the treasury should receive into the treasury jewels, superior goods, inferior goods, or raw materials, after they have been supervised by the officials responsible for their kind and processing.

children.text: tāmraparṇikaṃ pāṇḍyakavāṭakaṃ pāśikyaṃ kauleyaṃ caurṇeyaṃ māhendraṃ kārdamikaṃ srautasīyaṃ hrādīyaṃ haimavataṃ ca mauktikam ||
children.translated_text: Pearls are of the varieties <s>Tāmraparṇika</s>, <s>Pāṇḍyakavāṭaka</s>, <s>Pāśikya</s>, <s>Kauleya</s>, <s>Caurṇeya</s>, <s>Māhendra</s>, <s>Kārdamika</s>, <s>Srautasīya</s>, <s>Hrādīya</s>, and <s>Haimavata</s>.
Oyster shell, conch shell, and miscellaneous deposits are their sources.

children.text: masūrakaṃ tripuṭakaṃ kūrmakam ardhacandrakaṃ kañcukitaṃ yamakaṃ kartakaṃ kharakaṃ siktakaṃ kāmaṇḍalukaṃ śyāvaṃ nīlaṃ durviddhaṃ cāpraśastam ||
children.translated_text: The disapproved kinds are <s>masūraka</s> (lentil-shaped), <s>tripuṭaka</s> (triple), <s>kūrmaka</s> (turtle-shaped), <s>ardhacandraka</s> (half-moon-shaped), <s>kañcukita</s> (sheathed), <s>yamaka</s> (twinned), <s>kartaka</s>, <s>kharaka</s> (rough), <s>siktaka</s> (sprinkled-looking), <s>kāmaṇḍaluka</s> (water-pot-shaped), dark, blue, and badly pierced.

children.text: sthūlaṃ vṛttaṃ nistalaṃ bhrājiṣṇu śvetaṃ guru snigdhaṃ deśaviddhaṃ ca praśastam ||
children.translated_text: The approved kind is large, round, without flatness, brilliant, white, heavy, smooth, and pierced in the proper place.

children.text: śīrṣakam upaśīrṣakaṃ prakāṇḍakam avaghāṭakaṃ taralapratibaddhaṃ ceti yaṣṭiprabhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The subdivisions of a pearl-string are <s>Śīrṣaka</s>, <s>Upaśīrṣaka</s>, <s>Prakāṇḍaka</s>, <s>Avaghāṭaka</s>, and <s>Taralapratibaddha</s>.
Among strings, one of eight thousand is <s>Indracchanda</s>.
Half of that is <s>Vijayacchanda</s>.
Sixty-four make an <s>Ardhahāra</s>.
Fifty-four make a <s>Raśmikalāpa</s>.
Thirty-two make a <s>Guccha</s>.
Twenty-seven make a <s>Nakṣatramālā</s>.
Twenty-four make an <s>Ardhaguccha</s>.
Twenty make a <s>Māṇavaka</s>.
Half of that makes an <s>Ardhamāṇavaka</s>.
These same types, when they have a gem in the middle, become the corresponding <s>Māṇavaka</s> types.
A pure <s>Hāra</s> has a single head-piece.
The remaining kinds are similar.
An <s>Ardhamāṇavaka</s> has a gem in the middle.
A <s>Phalakahāra</s> has three plaques, or else five plaques.
A pure <s>Ekāvalī</s> is a single strand.
That same strand, when it has a gem in the middle, is a <s>Yaṣṭi</s>.
A <s>Ratnāvalī</s> is variegated with gold and gems.
An <s>Apavartaka</s> has intervals of gold, gems, and pearls.
A <s>Sopānaka</s> has intervals of gold thread.
Or, when it has a gem in the middle, it is a <s>Maṇisopānaka</s>.
By this, the variations of ornaments for the head, hands, feet, waist, clusters, and net-like ornaments have been explained.
Gems are <s>Kauṭa</s>, <s>Māleyaka</s>, and <s>Pārasamudraka</s>.
There are <s>Saugandhika</s>, <s>Padmarāga</s>, <s>Anavadyarāga</s>, <s>Pārijātapuṣpaka</s>, and <s>Bālasūryaka</s>.

children.text: vaiḍūryam utpalavarṇaḥ śirīṣapuṣpaka udakavarṇo vaṃśarāgaḥ śukapattravarṇaḥ puṣyarāgo gomūtrako gomedakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Vaiḍūrya</s>, <s>Utpalavarṇa</s>, <s>Śirīṣapuṣpaka</s>, <s>Udakavarṇa</s>, <s>Vaṃśarāga</s>, <s>Śukapattravarṇa</s>, <s>Puṣyarāga</s>, <s>Gomūtraka</s>, and <s>Gomedaka</s>.

children.text: indranīlo nīlāvalīyaḥ kalāyapuṣpako mahānīlo jambvābho jīmūtaprabho nandakaḥ sravanmadhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Indranīla</s>, <s>Nīlāvalīya</s>, <s>Kalāyapuṣpaka</s>, <s>Mahānīla</s>, <s>Jambvābha</s>, <s>Jīmūtaprabha</s>, <s>Nandaka</s>, and <s>Sravanmadhya</s>.
There are <s>Śuddhasphaṭika</s>, <s>Mūlāṭavarṇa</s>, <s>Śītavṛṣṭi</s>, and <s>Sūryakānta</s>.
Thus the gems.

children.text: ṣaḍaśraś caturaśro vṛtto vā tīvrarāgaḥ saṃsthānavān acchaḥ snigdho gurur arciṣmān antargataprabhaḥ prabhānulepī ceti maṇiguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The qualities of gems are these: six-sided, square, or round shape; intense color; good formation; clarity; smoothness; heaviness; radiance; inner brilliance; and a sheen spread over the surface.

children.text: mandarāgaprabhaḥ saśarkaraḥ puṣpacchidraḥ khaṇḍo durviddho lekhākīrṇa iti doṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their defects are dim color and luster, grittiness, flower-like holes, breakage, bad piercing, and being filled with streaks.

children.text: vimalakaḥ sasyako 'ñjanamūlakaḥ pittakaḥ sulabhako lohitākṣo mṛgāśmako jyotīrasako māleyako 'hicchatrakaḥ kūrpaḥ pratikūrpaḥ sugandhikūrpaḥ kṣīravakaḥ śukticūrṇakaḥ śilā pravālakaḥ pulakaḥ śuklapulaka ityantarajātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalaka</s>, <s>Sasyaka</s>, <s>Añjanamūlaka</s>, <s>Pittaka</s>, <s>Sulabhaka</s>, <s>Lohitākṣa</s>, <s>Mṛgāśmaka</s>, <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, <s>Māleyaka</s>, <s>Ahicchatraka</s>, <s>Kūrpa</s>, <s>Pratikūrpa</s>, <s>Sugandhikūrpa</s>, <s>Kṣīravaka</s>, <s>Śukticūrṇaka</s>, <s>Śilā</s>, <s>Pravālaka</s>, <s>Pulaka</s>, and <s>Śuklapulaka</s> are the secondary varieties.
The remaining kinds are glass-gems.

children.text: sabhārāṣṭrakaṃ tajjam ārāṣṭrakaṃ kāstīrarāṣṭrakaṃ śrīkaṭanakaṃ maṇimantakam indravānakaṃ ca vajram ||
children.translated_text: Diamond is of the kinds <s>Sabhārāṣṭraka</s>, <s>Tajja</s>, <s>Ārāṣṭraka</s>, <s>Kāstīrarāṣṭraka</s>, <s>Śrīkaṭanaka</s>, <s>Maṇimantaka</s>, and <s>Indravānaka</s>.
Its sources are mines, streams, and scattered deposits.

children.text: mārjārākṣakaṃ śirīṣapuṣpakaṃ gomūtrakaṃ gomedakaṃ śuddhasphaṭikaṃ mūlāṭīvarṇaṃ maṇivarṇānām anyatamavarṇam iti vajravarṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The colors of diamond are cat's-eye-like, <s>Śirīṣapuṣpaka</s>, cow-urine-colored, <s>Gomedaka</s>, pure crystal, <s>Mūlāṭī</s>-colored, or any one of the colors of gems.

children.text: sthūlaṃ guru prahārasahaṃ samakoṭikaṃ bhājanalekhi tarkubhrāmi bhrājiṣṇu ca praśastam ||
children.translated_text: The approved diamond is large, heavy, resistant to blows, even-cornered, able to scratch vessels, turning on a spindle, and brilliant.
One with lost corners, lacking edges, or turned aside at the flank is disapproved.

children.text: pravālakam ālakandakaṃ vaivarṇikaṃ ca raktaṃ padmarāgaṃ ca karaṭagarbhiṇikāvarjam iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pravālaka</s>, <s>Ālakandaka</s>, <s>Vaivarṇika</s>, the red kind, and <s>Padmarāga</s> are included, except for <s>Karaṭagarbhiṇikā</s>.
As for sandalwood, <s>Sātana</s> is red and earth-scented.
<s>Gośīrṣaka</s> is dark copper-colored and fish-scented.
<s>Haricandana</s> is parrot-feather-colored and mango-scented, and so is <s>Tārṇasa</s>.
<s>Grāmeruka</s> is red or dark red and smells of goat urine.
<s>Daivasabheya</s> is red, lotus-scented, and <s>Jāpaka</s>.

children.text: joṅgakaṃ raktaṃ raktakālaṃ vā snigdham taurūpaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Joṅgaka</s> is red or dark red, smooth, and <s>Taurūpa</s>.
<s>Māleyaka</s> is pale red.

children.text: kucandanaṃ rūkṣam agurukālaṃ raktaṃ raktakālaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kucandana</s> is rough, black like agarwood, red, or dark red.
<s>Kālaparvataka</s> is dark red or of faultless color.
<s>Kośāgāraparvataka</s> is black or variegated with black.
<s>Śītodakīya</s> is lotus-like, or black and smooth.
<s>Nāgaparvataka</s> is rough or the color of waterweed.
<s>Śākala</s> is tawny.
Thus.

children.text: laghu snigdham aśyānaṃ sarpiḥsnehalepi gandhasukhaṃ tvaganusāryanulbaṇam avirāgyuṣṇasahaṃ dāhagrāhi sukhasparśanam iti candanaguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The qualities of sandalwood are these: lightness, smoothness, absence of clamminess, an unctuous coating like ghee, pleasant fragrance, spreading over the skin, not being overpowering, not fading, bearing heat, taking fire, and pleasantness to the touch.

children.text: aguru joṅgakaṃ kālaṃ kālacitraṃ maṇḍalacitraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: As for agarwood, <s>Joṅgaka</s> is black, variegated with black, or marked with circles.
<s>Doṅgaka</s> is dark.
<s>Pārasamudraka</s> is variegated in appearance and smells of <s>uśīra</s> or fresh <s>mālikā</s> jasmine.
Thus.

children.text: guru snigdhaṃ peśalagandhi nirhāryagnisaham asaṃplutadhūmaṃ vimardasaham ityaguruguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The qualities of agarwood are these: heaviness, smoothness, delicate fragrance, endurance of fire when brought out, smoke that is not billowing, and endurance under rubbing.
As for <s>Tailaparṇika</s>, <s>Aśokagrāmika</s> is flesh-colored and lotus-scented.
<s>Joṅgaka</s> is reddish-yellow and smells of blue lotus or cow urine.
<s>Grāmeruka</s> is smooth and smells of cow urine.
<s>Sauvarṇakuḍyaka</s> is reddish-yellow and citron-scented.
<s>Pūrṇakadvīpaka</s> smells of lotus or fresh butter.
<s>Bhadraśriya</s> and <s>Pāralauhityaka</s> are jasmine-colored.
<s>Āntaravatya</s> is the color of <s>uśīra</s>.
Both have the scent of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Thus.
<s>Kāleyaka</s> born in <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> is smooth and yellowish.
The northern-mountain kind is reddish-yellow.
It withstands lumping, decoction, and smoke, does not fade, and conforms to mixtures.
Their qualities are like those of sandalwood and <s>aguru</s> (aloeswood).
The skins are <s>Kāntanāvaka</s>, <s>Praiyaka</s>, and <s>Uttaraparvataka</s>.
The <s>Kāntanāvaka</s> has the appearance of a peacock's neck.
The <s>Praiyaka</s> is variegated with blue, yellow, and white lines and spots.
Both of these are eight aṅgulas in length.
The <s>Dvādaśagrāmīya</s> skins are <s>Bisī</s> and <s>Mahābisī</s>.
The <s>Bisī</s> is indistinct in appearance, or <s>Duhilitikā</s>, or mottled.
The <s>Mahābisī</s> is rough and mostly white.
Both are twelve aṅgulas in length.

children.text: śyāmikā kālikā kadalī candrottarā śākulā cārohajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ārohaja</s> skins are <s>Śyāmikā</s>, <s>Kālikā</s>, <s>Kadalī</s>, <s>Candrottarā</s>, and <s>Śākulā</s>.
The <s>Śyāmikā</s> is tawny or spotted with speckles.
The <s>Kālikā</s> is tawny or pigeon-colored.
Both of these are eight aṅgulas in length.
The <s>Kadalī</s> is rough and a hand's length.
That same skin, when marked with moon-like spots, is <s>Candrottarā</s>.
The <s>Śākulā</s> is one third of a <s>Kadalī</s>; it is marked with circular patches, or with patterns like a prepared hide with ear-marks.
Thus.
The <s>Bāhlaveya</s> skins are <s>Sāmūra</s>, <s>Cīnasī</s>, and <s>Sāmūlī</s>.
The <s>Sāmūra</s> is thirty-six aṅgulas long and black like collyrium.
The <s>Cīnasī</s> is red-black or pale-black.
The <s>Sāmūlī</s> is wheat-colored.
Thus.
The <s>Audra</s> skins are <s>Sāṃtinā</s>, <s>Nalatūlā</s>, and <s>Vṛttapṛcchā</s>.
The <s>Sātinā</s> is black.
The <s>Nalatūlā</s> has the color of reed-floss.
The <s>Vṛttapucchā</s> is tawny.

children.text: carmaṇāṃ mṛdu snigdhaṃ bahularoma ca śreṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: Among skins, what is soft, glossy, and thick-haired is best.

children.text: śuddhaṃ śuddharaktaṃ pakṣaraktaṃ cāvikam khacitaṃ vānacitraṃ khaṇḍasaṃghātyaṃ tantuvicchinnaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Sheep-wool material may be pure, pure red, red at the edges, quilted, forest-patterned, assembled from pieces, or with broken threads.

children.text: kambalaḥ kaucapakaḥ kulamitikā saumitikā turagāstaraṇaṃ varṇakaṃ talicchakaṃ vāravāṇaḥ paristomaḥ samantabhadrakaṃ cāvikam ||
children.translated_text: The sheep-wool goods are <s>kambala</s> (blanket), <s>kaucapaka</s>, <s>kulamitikā</s>, <s>saumitikā</s>, <s>turagāstaraṇa</s> (horse-covering), <s>varṇaka</s>, <s>talicchaka</s>, <s>vāravāṇa</s>, <s>paristoma</s>, and <s>samantabhadraka</s>.

children.text: picchilam ārdram iva ca sūkṣmaṃ mṛdu ca śreṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: What is smooth, as if moist, fine, and soft is best.

children.text: aṣṭaprotisaṃghātyā kṛṣṇā bhiṅgisī varṣavāraṇam apasāraka iti naipālakam ||
children.translated_text: The Nepalese goods are the black <s>Bhiṅgisī</s>, joined from eight woven strips, <s>Varṣavāraṇa</s> (rain-cover), and <s>Apasāraka</s>.

children.text: sampuṭikā caturaśrikā lambarā kaṭavānakaṃ prāvarakaḥ sattaliketi mṛgaroma ||
children.translated_text: The deer-hair goods are <s>Sampuṭikā</s>, <s>Caturaśrikā</s>, <s>Lambarā</s>, <s>Kaṭavānaka</s>, <s>Prāvaraka</s>, and <s>Sattalikā</s>.
The <s>Vāṅgaka</s> <s>dukūla</s> (fine cloth) is white and glossy.
The <s>Pauṇḍraka</s> is dark and lustrous like a gem.

children.text: sauvarṇakuḍyakaṃ sūryavarṇaṃ maṇisnigdhodakavānaṃ caturaśravānaṃ vyāmiśravānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sauvarṇakuḍyaka</s> is sun-colored, jewel-lustrous, and may have watered, square, or mixed patterns.
The grades of these are said to be one-cloth, one-and-a-half-cloth, two-cloth, three-cloth, and four-cloth.

children.text: tena kāśikaṃ pauṇḍrakaṃ ca kṣaumaṃ vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: By this, <s>Kāśika</s> and <s>Pauṇḍraka</s> linen are also explained.
The <s>pattrorṇā</s> (leaf-fiber cloths) are <s>Māgadhikā</s>, <s>Pauṇḍrikā</s>, and <s>Sauvarṇakuḍyakā</s>.
Their sources are the <s>Nāgavṛkṣa</s>, <s>Likuca</s>, <s>Bakula</s>, and <s>Vaṭa</s> trees.
The <s>Nāgavṛkṣikā</s> is yellow.
The <s>Laikucī</s> is wheat-colored.
The <s>Bākulī</s> is white.
The remaining varieties are butter-colored.
Among them, the <s>Sauvarṇakuḍyakā</s> is best.
By that, <s>kauśeya</s> (silk) and <s>Cīnapaṭṭa</s> cloths produced in China are explained.

children.text: mādhuram āparāntakaṃ kāliṅgaṃ kāśikaṃ vāṅgakaṃ vātsakaṃ māhiṣakaṃ ca kārpāsikaṃ śreṣṭham
children.translated_text: The best cottons are those from <s>Mādhura</s>, <s>Āparānta</s>, <s>Kāliṅga</s>, <s>Kāśi</s>, <s>Vāṅga</s>, <s>Vatsa</s>, and <s>Māhiṣaka</s>.
Thus.
After this, one should know, for the remaining jewels, their measure and the marks of their value,

children.text: jātiṃ rūpaṃ ca jānīyān nidhānaṃ navakarma ca ||
children.translated_text: their class and appearance, their deposits, and new workmanship;
the restoration of old pieces, the work itself, secret procedures, and implements;
their use according to place and time, and countermeasures for harmful effects.

children.text: ākarādhyakṣaḥ śulbadhātuśāstrarasapākamaṇirāgajñas tajjñasakho vā tajjātakarmakaropakaraṇasampannaḥ kiṭṭamūṣāṅgārabhasmaliṅgaṃ vākaraṃ bhūtapūrvam abhūtapūrvaṃ vā bhūmiprastararasadhātum atyarthavarṇagauravam ugragandharasaṃ parīkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of mines, knowing copper and other metals, the science of metallurgy, ore-smelting, gems, and coloring, or assisted by experts, and equipped with workers and implements appropriate to that kind of operation, should examine a mine, whether formerly worked or never worked before, by signs such as slag, crucibles, charcoal, and ash, and should test the earth, rock, ores, and mineral exudations for exceptionally strong color and weight and for pungent smell and taste.

children.text: parvatānām abhijñātoddeśānāṃ bilaguhopatyakālayanagūḍhakhāteṣvantaḥ prasyandino jambūcūtatālaphalapakvaharidrābhedaguḍaharitālamanaḥśilākṣaudrahiṅgulukapuṇḍarīkaśukamayūrapattravarṇāḥ savarṇodakauṣadhiparyantāścikkaṇā viśadā bhārikāśca rasāḥ kāñcanikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In mountains whose indications are known, in holes, caves, hollows, channels, and hidden excavations, the mineral exudations flowing within are gold-bearing when they are the colors of ripe <s>jambu</s>, mango, and palm fruits, turmeric, broken jaggery, orpiment, realgar, honey, cinnabar, lotus, parrot, or peacock feathers, when they are bordered by water and herbs of the same color, and when they are smooth, clear, and heavy.

children.text: apsu niṣṭhyūtāstailavadvisarpiṇaḥ paṅkamalagrāhiṇaśca tāmrarūpyayoḥ śatād upari veddhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When cast into water, they spread like oil and take hold of mud and dirt; they penetrate copper and silver in proportions greater than one hundred.
One should recognize <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) as resembling that, with pungent smell and taste.

children.text: pītakās tāmrakāstāmrapītakā vā bhūmiprastaradhātavo bhinnā nīlarājīvanto mudgamāṣakṛsaravarṇā vā dadhibindupiṇḍacitrā haridrāharītakīpadmapattraśaivalayakṛtplīhānavadyavarṇā bhinnāś cuñcuvālukālekhābindusvastikavantaḥ sugulikā arciṣmantastāpyamānā na bhidyante bahuphenadhūmāśca suvarṇadhātavaḥ pratīvāpārthās tāmrarūpyavedhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Earths, rocks, and ores that are yellow, coppery, or copper-yellow; that, when broken, show blue lines; that are the color of green gram, black gram, or gruel; that are marked with lumps like drops of curd; that, when broken, have the color of turmeric, <s>harītakī</s>, lotus leaf, moss, liver, or spleen; that have fine sand-like streaks, dots, or svastika marks; that have good globules and flame-like brightness; and that when heated do not split and give off much foam and smoke: these are gold ores, suitable for admixture and capable of penetrating copper and silver.

children.text: śaṅkhakarpūrasphaṭikanavanītakapotapārāvatavimalakamayūragrīvāvarṇāḥ sasyakagomedakaguḍamatsyaṇḍikāvarṇāḥ kovidārapadmapāṭalīkalāyakṣaumātasīpuṣpavarṇāḥ sasīsāḥ sāñjanā visrā bhinnāḥ śvetābhāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ kṛṣṇābhāḥ śvetāḥ sarve vā lekhābinducitrā mṛdavo dhmāyamānā na sphuṭanti bahuphenadhūmāśca rūpyadhātavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ores that are the colors of conch, camphor, crystal, fresh butter, dove, pigeon, <s>vimalaka</s>, or peacock's neck; the colors of <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>gomedaka</s>, jaggery, or coarse sugar; the colors of <s>kovidāra</s>, lotus, <s>pāṭalī</s>, pea, linen, or flax flowers; containing lead or collyrium, foul-smelling; which, when broken, are white-looking, black, black-looking, white, or all marked with streaks and spots; soft, not cracking when smelted, and giving much foam and smoke: these are silver ores.
In all metals, an increase in heaviness means an increase in metallic essence (<s>sattva</s>).

children.text: teṣām aśuddhā mūḍhagarbhā vā tīkṣṇamūtrakṣārabhāvitā rājavṛkṣavaṭapīlugopittarocanāmahiṣakharakarabhamūtraleṇḍapiṇḍabaddhās tatpratīvāpāstadavalepā vā viśuddhāḥ sravanti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, those that are impure, or whose contents are obstructed, flow out purified when they have been treated with sharp urine and alkali and bound with lumps made from <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, banyan, <s>pīlu</s>, cow-bile, <s>rocanā</s>, and the urine and dung of buffaloes, donkeys, and camels, or when admixtures and coatings of these are applied.
An admixture of plantain and <s>vajrakanda</s>, with alkalis from barley, black gram, sesame, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>pīlu</s>, or with cow's milk and goat's milk, produces softness.
Honey with <s>madhuka</s>, goat's milk with oil, mixed with ghee, jaggery, ferment, and plantain:

children.text: yad api śatasahasradhā vibhinnaṃ bhavati mṛdu tribhir eva tanniṣekaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: even what has split a hundred thousand ways becomes soft with only three immersions in that.
An admixture of cow's tooth and horn hardens what is soft.

children.text: bhārikaḥ snigdho mṛduśca prastaradhātur bhūmibhāgo vā piṅgalo haritaḥ pāṭalo lohito vā tāmradhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: A rocky ore or tract of earth that is heavy, smooth, and soft, and is tawny, green, pale red, or red, is copper ore.

children.text: kākamecakaḥ kapotarocanāvarṇaḥ śvetarājinaddho vā visraḥ sīsadhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ore that is black like a crow, the color of pigeon-yellow pigment, or bound with white streaks, and foul-smelling, is lead ore.
Ore that is saline and variegated, or the color of baked clay, is tin ore.
Ore that is rough, pale red, or the color of a <s>sinduvāra</s> flower, is <s>tīkṣṇa</s> ore, iron ore.
Ore the color of a crow's egg or of birch bark is <s>vaikṛntaka</s> ore.

children.text: acchaḥ snigdhaḥ saprabho ghoṣavān śītastīvrastanurāgaśca maṇidhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gem ore is clear, smooth, lustrous, resonant, cool, vivid, and delicately colored.
What is produced from an ore should be employed in the workshops belonging to that class.

children.text: kṛtabhāṇḍavyavahāram ekamukham atyayaṃ cānyatra kartṛkretṛvikretṝṇāṃ sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: He should establish trade in finished goods through a single outlet, and a penalty for artisans, buyers, and sellers who act elsewhere.

children.text: ākarikam apaharantam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpayed anyatra ratnebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who steals mine produce should be made to pay eightfold, except in the case of jewels.

children.text: stenam anisṛṣṭopajīvinaṃ ca baddhaṃ karma kārayet daṇḍopakāriṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He should make a thief and a person living from an unauthorized trade work in confinement, and also one whose labor can serve as punishment.

children.text: vyayakriyābhārikam ākaraṃ bhāgena prakrayeṇa vā dadyāl lāghavikam ātmanā kārayet ||
children.translated_text: A mine that is burdensome in expenditure and operation should be leased for a share or a fixed payment; an easy one he should work himself.
The superintendent of metals should have workshops run for copper, lead, tin, <s>vaikṛntaka</s>, <s>ārakūṭa</s>, <s>vṛtta</s>, bronze, <s>tāla</s>, and iron, and should manage trade in metal goods.

children.text: lakṣaṇādhyakṣaścaturbhāgatāmraṃ rūpyarūpaṃ tīkṣṇatrapusīsāñjanānām anyatamamāṣabījayuktaṃ kārayet paṇam ardhapaṇaṃ pādam aṣṭabhāgam iti pādājīvaṃ tāmrarūpaṃ māṣakam ardhamāṣakaṃ kākaṇīm ardhakākaṇīm iti ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of coinage should have silver coinage made with one quarter copper and mixed with a <s>māṣa</s>-seed weight of any one among iron, tin, lead, and antimony: the <s>paṇa</s>, half-<s>paṇa</s>, quarter, and eighth; and copper coinage, namely the <s>māṣaka</s>, half-<s>māṣaka</s>, <s>kākaṇī</s>, and half-<s>kākaṇī</s>.

children.text: rūpadarśakaḥ paṇayātrāṃ vyāvahārikīṃ kośapraveśyāṃ ca sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: The coin examiner should regulate the circulation of <s>paṇas</s>, both for ordinary transactions and for entry into the treasury.

children.text: rūpikam aṣṭakaṃ śataṃ pañcakaṃ śataṃ vyājīm pārīkṣikam aṣṭabhāgikaṃ śatam pañcaviṃśatipaṇam atyayaṃ ca anyatrakartṛkretṛvikretṛparīkṣitṛbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There should be an eight-per-hundred coinage fee, a five-per-hundred surcharge, an assay fee of one eighth per hundred, and a penalty of twenty-five <s>paṇas</s> for making, buying, selling, or testing elsewhere.
The superintendent of mines should have workshops run for conch shell, diamonds, gems, pearls, coral, and alkali, and should manage their buying and selling.

children.text: lavaṇādhyakṣaḥ pākamuktaṃ lavaṇabhāgaṃ prakrayaṃ ca yathākālaṃ saṃgṛhṇīyād vikrayācca mūlyaṃ rūpaṃ vyājīṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of salt should collect at the proper time the salt share released after boiling and the fixed payment; from sales he should collect the price, the coinage charge, and the surcharge.
Imported salt should pay a sixth part.

children.text: dattabhāgavibhāgasya vikrayaḥ pañcakaṃ śataṃ vyājīṃ rūpaṃ rūpikaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For salt whose share and division have been paid, sale involves a five-per-hundred surcharge, together with the <s>vyājī</s>, the <s>rūpa</s>, and the <s>rūpika</s>.

children.text: kretā śulkaṃ rājapaṇyacchedānurūpaṃ ca vaidharaṇaṃ dadyāt anyatra kretā ṣaṭchatam atyayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The buyer should pay customs duty and a <s>vaidharaṇa</s> charge proportionate to the loss to the king's merchandise; if he buys elsewhere, the buyer should also pay a penalty of six hundred.

children.text: vilavaṇam uttamaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyād anisṛṣṭopajīvī cānyatra vānaprasthebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who deals in salt outside the rule should pay the highest fine, as should a person living from it without permission, except for forest hermits.
Vedic scholars, ascetics, and corvée laborers may take salt for their food.
Other products in the class of salt and alkali should pay customs duty.

children.text: evaṃ mūlyaṃ ca bhāgaṃ ca vyājīṃ parigham atyayam
children.translated_text: Thus the price, the share, the surcharge, the barrier charge, and the penalty,

children.text: śulkaṃ vaidharaṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ rūpaṃ rūpikam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: customs duty, <s>vaidharaṇa</s>, the fine, the <s>rūpa</s>, and also the <s>rūpika</s>,

children.text: khanibhyo dvādaśavidhaṃ dhātuṃ paṇyaṃ ca saṃharet
children.translated_text: from the mines he should collect the twelvefold metal and the saleable goods;
thus, for all commodities, he should establish collection through a single outlet.
The treasury has mines as its source; from the treasury arises coercive power.
The earth, adorned by the treasury, is obtained by means of the treasury and coercive power.

children.text: suvarṇādhyakṣaḥ suvarṇarajatakarmāntānām asambandhāveśanacatuḥśālām ekadvārām akṣaśālāṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of gold should have an assaying hall made for gold and silver workshops, unattached to other buildings, with four halls and a single door.

children.text: viśikhāmadhye sauvarṇikaṃ śilpavantam abhijātaṃ prātyayikaṃ ca sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of the workshop street he should appoint a goldsmith who is skilled, well-born, and trustworthy.

children.text: jāmbūnadaṃ śātakumbhaṃ hāṭakaṃ vaiṇavaṃ śṛṅgaśuktijaṃ jātarūpaṃ rasaviddham ākarodgataṃ ca suvarṇam ||
children.translated_text: The kinds of gold are <s>Jāmbūnada</s>, <s>Śātakumbha</s>, <s>Hāṭaka</s>, <s>Vaiṇava</s>, that produced from horn and shell, native gold, mercury-treated gold, and mine-born gold.

children.text: kiñjalkavarṇaṃ mṛdu snigdham anādi bhrājiṣṇu ca śreṣṭhaṃ raktapītakaṃ madhyamaṃ raktam avaram ||
children.translated_text: The best is the color of a filament, soft, smooth, flawless, and shining; reddish yellow is middling, and red is inferior.
Among the superior kinds, what is pale or white has not fully attained its proper quality.
Whatever is deficient in that way should be purified with four times as much lead.
What breaks because of admixture with lead should be smelted with dry sheets of fuel.
What breaks because of dryness should be quenched in oil and cow dung.

children.text: ākarodgataṃ sīsānvayena bhidyamānaṃ pākapattrāṇi kṛtvā gaṇḍikāsu kuṭṭayet kadalīvajrakandakalke vā niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: Mine-born gold that breaks because of admixture with lead should be made into roasting sheets and hammered into lumps, or quenched in a paste of plantain and <s>vajrakanda</s>.

children.text: tutthodgataṃ gauḍikaṃ kāmbukaṃ cākravālikaṃ ca rūpyam ||
children.translated_text: The kinds of silver are <s>Tutthodgata</s>, <s>Gauḍika</s>, <s>Kāmbuka</s>, and <s>Cākravālika</s>.
White, smooth, and soft silver is the best.
The opposite, and silver that blisters or cracks, is defective.
It should be purified with one-fourth as much lead.

children.text: udgatacūlikam acchaṃ bhrājiṣṇu dadhivarṇaṃ ca śuddham ||
children.translated_text: Pure silver has a raised crest, is clear and shining, and is the color of curd.
For the purified metal, one <s>suvarṇa</s> of yellow colorant is the coloring agent.

children.text: tataḥ śulbakākaṇyuttarāpasāritā ā catuḥsīmāntād iti ṣoḍaśa varṇakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that point, with copper increased or diminished by one <s>kākaṇī</s> at a time up to the fourth limit, there are sixteen color standards.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ pūrvaṃ nikaṣya paścād varṇikāṃ nikaṣayet ||
children.translated_text: After first rubbing the gold on the touchstone, he should then rub the <s>varṇikā</s> (color standard).

children.text: samarāgalekham animnonnate deśe nikaṣitaṃ parimṛditaṃ parilīḍhaṃ nakhāntarād vā gairikeṇāvacūrṇitam upadhiṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: A tested streak of uniform color, made on a level spot, if it has been rubbed over, licked over, or dusted from beneath the fingernail with red ochre, should be recognized as a fraud.

children.text: jātihiṅgulukena puṣpakāsīsena vā gomūtrabhāvitena digdhenāgrahastena saṃspṛṣṭaṃ suvarṇaṃ śvetībhavati ||
children.translated_text: Gold touched with the fingertip smeared with natural cinnabar, or with <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s> steeped in cow urine, becomes white.

children.text: sakesaraḥ snigdho mṛdur bhrājiṣṇuśca nikaṣarāgaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A touchstone streak that has fine filaments, is glossy, soft, and brilliant is the best.
A <s>Kāliṅgaka</s> stone or a <s>Tāpī</s> stone, green-gram colored, is the best touchstone.
One of uniform color is useful for both selling and buying.
One that is elephant-skin colored, greenish, and gives a counter-color is useful for selling.
One that is firm, rough, and uneven in color, and does not give a counter-color, is useful for buying.

children.text: chedaścikkaṇaḥ samavarṇaḥ ślakṣṇo mṛdur bhrājiṣṇuśca śreṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A cut that is smooth, even-colored, polished, soft, and brilliant is the best.

children.text: tāpo bahirantaśca samaḥ kiñjalkavarṇaḥ kuraṇḍakapuṣpavarṇo vā śreṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Heating is best when it is the same outside and inside and has the color of pollen or of the <s>kuraṇḍaka</s> flower.
Grey and blue indicate that it has not been properly brought to completion.
Scales and measures we shall explain under the Superintendent of Weights and Measures.
According to that instruction, he should give and receive silver and gold.
No one who has not been appointed should enter the assay workshop.
If he enters it, he is to be destroyed.
Or, if an appointed official is found with silver or gold on him, he should be convicted by that very fact.
With their clothes, hands, and hidden parts searched, artisans in gold-work, speckled work, fabrication, and <s>tapanīya</s> work, smelters, and washers of crucible dust should enter and leave.
All their equipment and their unfinished operations should remain there itself.

children.text: gṛhītaṃ suvarṇaṃ dhṛtaṃ ca prayogaṃ karaṇamadhye dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: The gold received and the operation undertaken should be deposited in the middle of the workroom.
In the evening and in the morning, after it has been marked with the seals of the maker and the commissioner, he should put it away.
The operations are <s>kṣepaṇa</s>, <s>guṇa</s>, and <s>kṣudraka</s>.
<s>Kṣepaṇa</s> includes setting glass and the like.
<s>Guṇa</s> includes making thread or wire and the like.
A solid or hollow object connected with speckled work and the like is <s>kṣudraka</s>.

children.text: arpayet kācakarmaṇaḥ pañcabhāgaṃ kāñcanaṃ daśabhāgaṃ kaṭumānam ||
children.translated_text: For glass work, he should allot one fifth as gold and ten parts as <s>kaṭumāna</s>.

children.text: tāmrapādayuktaṃ rūpyaṃ rūpyapādayuktaṃ vā suvarṇaṃ saṃskṛtakaṃ tasmād rakṣet ||
children.translated_text: For that reason he should guard against processed silver containing a quarter copper, or gold containing a quarter silver.

children.text: pṛṣatakācakarmaṇaḥ trayo hi bhāgāḥ paribhāṇḍaṃ dvau vāstukaṃ catvāro vā vāstukaṃ trayaḥ paribhāṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: For speckled glass work, three parts are <s>paribhāṇḍa</s> and two are <s>vāstuka</s>, or four are <s>vāstuka</s> and three are <s>paribhāṇḍa</s>.
In fabrication work, he should plate a copper vessel with an equal amount of gold.
A silver vessel, whether solid or hollow, he should overlay with half as much gold.

children.text: caturbhāgasuvarṇaṃ vā vālukāhiṅgulukasya rasena cūrṇena vā vāsayet ||
children.translated_text: Or he should color it with one-quarter gold, using the liquid or powder of sand and cinnabar.

children.text: tapanīyaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ suvarṇaṃ surāgaṃ samasīsātikrāntaṃ pākapattrapakvaṃ saindhavikayojjvālitaṃ nīlapītaśvetaharitaśukapattravarṇānāṃ prakṛtir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tapanīya</s>, the superior gold, richly colored, processed beyond an equal quantity of lead, baked with processing leaves, and brightened with salt, is the base for blue, yellow, white, green, and parrot-feather colors.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ cāsya mayūragrīvābhaṃ śvetabhaṅgaṃ cimicimāyitaṃ pītacūrṇitaṃ kākaṇikaḥ suvarṇarāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its sharp metal, resembling a peacock's neck, with a white fracture, sparkling and reduced to yellow powder, is the <s>kākaṇika</s> gold colorant.

children.text: tāram upaśuddhaṃ vā asthitutthe catuḥ samasīse catuḥ śuṣkatutthe catuḥ kapāle trir gomaye dvir evaṃ saptadaśatutthātikrāntaṃ saindhavikayojjvālitam ||
children.translated_text: Silver, whether fully or partly purified, passed four times through bone-vitriol, four times through equal lead, four times through dry vitriol, three times through potsherd, and twice through cow dung, thus passed through seventeen vitriol processes, is brightened with salt.

children.text: etasmāt kākaṇyuttaramād vimāṣād iti suvarṇe deyaṃ paścād rāgayogaḥ śvetatāraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Of this, from one <s>kākaṇī</s> upward as far as a <s>vimāṣa</s>, should be added to gold; after that, by applying the color mixture, it becomes white silver.
Three parts of <s>tapanīya</s>, suffused with a thirty-second part of white silver, become pale red.
Copper makes it yellow.

children.text: tapanīyam ujjvālya rāgatribhāgaṃ dadyāt pītarāgaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After brightening <s>tapanīya</s>, he should add one third of the colorant; it becomes yellow-colored.
Two parts of white silver and one of <s>tapanīya</s> make it green-gram colored.
Smeared with a half part of black iron, it becomes black.

children.text: pratilepinā rasena dviguṇābhyaktaṃ tapanīyaṃ śukapattravarṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tapanīya</s> smeared with twice as much coating liquid becomes parrot-feather colored.
At the beginning of that process, for the special colorings, he should take a corresponding color standard.
And he should understand the processing of sharp metal and copper.

children.text: tasmād vajramaṇimuktāpravālarūpāṇām apaneyimānaṃ ca rūpyasuvarṇabhāṇḍabandhapramāṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: From that he should know the amount removable from diamonds, jewels, pearls, and corals, and the measurements for binding silver and gold vessels.
Uniform in color, evenly paired, free from clinging speckles, firm,
well polished, not over-yellow, distinct, and comfortable to wear,
well finished, endowed with luster, pleasing in form, and even,
and delightful to the mind and eye: these are remembered as the qualities of <s>tapanīya</s>.
The goldsmith official should have the silver and gold of townsmen and country people worked by registered workshop artisans.

children.text: nirdiṣṭakālakāryaṃ ca karma kuryur anirdiṣṭakālaṃ kāryāpadeśam ||
children.translated_text: They should perform work whose time and task have been specified; where the time is not specified, they should follow the specification of the task.
If the work is done otherwise, there is loss of wages and a fine twice that amount.
For passing beyond the time, the wage is reduced by one quarter, and there is a fine twice that amount.
They should receive a deposit according to its color and measure, and should return exactly that kind.

children.text: kālāntarād api ca tathāvidham eva pratigṛhṇīyuḥ anyatra kṣīṇapariśīrṇābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Even after the lapse of time, they should accept only that same kind, except in cases of diminution or decay.
Through the workshop artisans he should know each particular in the tests and operations concerning pieces of gold.
For heated and washed metal, a loss of one <s>kākaṇī</s> per <s>suvarṇa</s> is to be allowed.

children.text: tīkṣṇakākaṇī rūpyadviguṇaḥ rāgaprakṣepas tasya ṣaḍbhāgaḥ kṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The coloring admixture consists of a sharp <s>kākaṇī</s> and twice as much silver; its wastage is one-sixth.

children.text: varṇahīne māṣāvare pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ pramāṇahīne madhyamas tulāpratimānopadhāv uttamaḥ kṛtabhāṇḍopadhau ca ||
children.translated_text: If the color is deficient by a <s>māṣa</s> or less, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; if the measure is deficient, the middle fine; for fraud with scales and weights, and also for fraud in finished goods, the highest fine applies.

children.text: sauvarṇikenādṛṣṭam anyatra vā prayogaṃ kārayato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who has a goldsmith perform an operation unseen, or somewhere else, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
For the maker it is double, if there has been removal by fraud.
If there has been no removal by fraud, he should be taken before the office for the removal of criminal elements.
For the maker there is also a fine of two hundred, or amputation of the hand.
They should buy scales, weights, and measuring vessels from the superintendent of weights and measures.
Otherwise the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: ghanaṃ suṣiraṃ saṃyūhyam avalepyaṃ saṃghātyaṃ vāsitakaṃ ca kārukarma ||
children.translated_text: Artisans' work is solid, hollow, compacted, coated, joined, and impregnated.

children.text: tulāviṣamam apasāraṇaṃ visrāvaṇaṃ peṭakaḥ piṅkaśceti haraṇopāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The means of stealing are an uneven balance, removal, draining off, the <s>peṭaka</s>, and the <s>piṅka</s>.

children.text: saṃnāminyutkīrṇikā bhinnamastakopakaṇṭhī kuśikyā sakaṭukakṣyā parivelyāyaskāntā ca duṣṭatulāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The faulty balances are the <s>saṃnāminī</s>, the <s>utkīrṇikā</s>, the broken-headed side-necked balance, the <s>kuśikī</s>, the balance with a rough socket, the <s>parivelyā</s>, and the magnetic one.
Two parts of silver and one of copper make a <s>tripuṭaka</s>.
By means of that, what has come from the ore is removed; that is removal by <s>tripuṭaka</s>.

children.text: śulbena śulbāpasāritaṃ vellakena vellakāpasāritaṃ śulbārdhasāreṇa hemnā hemāpasāritam ||
children.translated_text: Removal by copper is done with copper, removal by <s>vellaka</s> with <s>vellaka</s>, and removal by gold with gold whose substance is half copper.

children.text: mūkamūṣā pūtikiṭṭaḥ karaṭukamukhaṃ nālī saṃdaṃśo joṅganī suvarcikālavaṇaṃ tad eva suvarṇam ityapasāraṇamārgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A blind crucible, foul slag, a rough-mouthed implement, a tube, tongs, a <s>joṅganī</s>, <s>suvarcikā</s> salt, and the claim, 'this itself is gold,' are methods of removal.

children.text: pūrvapraṇihitā vā piṇḍavālukā mūṣābhedād agniṣṭhād uddhriyante ||
children.translated_text: Or lumps of sand placed beforehand are taken out from the fire-place when the crucible breaks.

children.text: paścād bandhane ācitakapattraparīkṣāyāṃ vā rūpyarūpeṇa parivartanaṃ visrāvaṇam piṇḍavālukānāṃ lohapiṇḍavālukābhir vā ||
children.translated_text: At the later fastening, or during the examination of layered sheets, substitution with a silver form is draining off; or the lumps of sand may be replaced with lumps of iron sand.
The <s>peṭaka</s> is fixed or removable, and it is made in compacted, coated, and joined work.

children.text: sīsarūpaṃ suvarṇapattreṇāvaliptam abhyantaram aṣṭakena baddhaṃ gāḍhapeṭakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A lead form coated with gold leaf and fixed inside with <s>aṣṭaka</s> is a fixed <s>peṭaka</s>.
That same thing, in layered cases, is removable.
A closely attached sheet, or a double sheet, is made in coated works.

children.text: śulbaṃ tāraṃ vā garbhaḥ pattrāṇāṃ saṃghātyeṣu kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Copper or silver is made the core of the sheets in joined works.

children.text: śulbarūpaṃ suvarṇapattrasaṃhataṃ pramṛṣṭaṃ supārśvaṃ tad eva yamakapattrasaṃhataṃ pramṛṣṭaṃ tāmratārarūpaṃ cottaravarṇakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A copper form joined with gold leaf, polished and well-sided, that same form joined with double leaf and polished, and a form of copper and silver are an <s>uttaravarṇaka</s>, a piece with only an outer color.

children.text: tad ubhayaṃ tāpanikaṣābhyāṃ niḥśabdollekhanābhyāṃ vā vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should detect both of these by heating and by the touchstone, or by dullness of sound and by scratching.
They loosen the removable piece in jujube acid or in salt water.

children.text: ghane suṣire vā rūpe suvarṇamṛnmālukāhiṅgulukakalpo vā tapto 'vatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: In a solid or hollow form, a heated preparation of gold-colored clay, <s>mālukā</s>, and cinnabar remains in place.

children.text: dṛḍhavāstuke vā rūpe vālukāmiśraṃ jatu gāndhārapaṅko vā tapto 'vatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Or, in a form with a firm body, lac mixed with sand, or Gandhāra mud, remains in place when heated.
For those two, heating or rubbing away is the purification test.

children.text: saparibhāṇḍe vā rūpe lavaṇam ulkayā kaṭuśarkarayā taptam avatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Or, in a form with its accessories, salt heated with a firebrand and sharp alkali remains in place.
Boiling it is the purification test.

children.text: abhrapaṭalam aṣṭakena dviguṇavāstuke vā rūpe badhyate ||
children.translated_text: A mica layer is fixed with <s>aṣṭaka</s> in a form whose material is doubled.

children.text: tasyāpihitakācakasyodake nimajjata ekadeśaḥ sīdati paṭalāntareṣu vā sūcyā bhidyate ||
children.translated_text: When that form, covered with glass, is immersed in water, one part sinks; or it is pierced with a needle between the layers.

children.text: maṇayo rūpyaṃ suvarṇaṃ vā ghanasuṣirāṇāṃ piṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Stones, silver, or gold in solid and hollow forms constitute the <s>piṅka</s>.

children.text: tasya tāpanam avadhvaṃsanaṃ vā śuddhir iti piṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its purification test is heating or rubbing away: thus the <s>piṅka</s>.
Therefore he should ascertain the marks of diamonds, gems, pearls, coral, and worked forms with respect to kind, shape, color, measure, and substance.

children.text: kṛtabhāṇḍaparīkṣāyāṃ purāṇabhāṇḍapratisaṃskāre vā catvāro haraṇopāyāḥ parikuṭṭanam avacchedanam ullekhanaṃ parimardanaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: In the examination of finished goods, or in the repair of old goods, there are four means of stealing: chipping off, cutting away, scratching, or rubbing.

children.text: peṭakāpadeśena pṛṣataṃ guṇaṃ piṭakāṃ vā yat pariśātayanti tatparikuṭṭanam ||
children.translated_text: When, under the pretext of a <s>peṭaka</s>, they cause a speck, a thread-like ridge, or a blister to fall off, that is chipping off.

children.text: yaddviguṇavāstukānāṃ vā rūpe sīsarūpaṃ prakṣipyābhyantaram avacchindanti tad avacchedanam ||
children.translated_text: When, in forms whose material is doubled, they insert a lead form and cut away the interior, that is cutting away.
When they scratch solid objects with a sharp instrument, that is scratching.

children.text: haritālamanaḥśilāhiṅgulukacūrṇānām anyatamena kuruvindacūrṇena vā vastraṃ saṃyūhya yat parimṛdnanti tat parimardanam ||
children.translated_text: When they prepare a cloth with one of the powders of orpiment, realgar, or cinnabar, or with powdered ruby, and rub the object, that is rubbing.

children.text: tena sauvarṇarājatāni bhāṇḍāni kṣīyante na caiṣāṃ kiṃcid avarugṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this, gold and silver goods are diminished, but no damage to them is visible.
For compacted goods that are broken, fragmented, or rubbed, he should make an estimate by comparison with a similar item.

children.text: virūpāṇāṃ vā tāpanam udakapeṣaṇaṃ ca bahuśaḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, for misshapen goods, he should repeatedly apply heating and grinding in water.

children.text: avakṣepaḥ pratimānam agnir gaṇḍikā bhaṇḍikādhikaraṇī piñchaḥ sūtraṃ cellaṃ bollanaṃ śira utsaṅgo makṣikā svakāyekṣā dṛtir udakaśarāvam agniṣṭham iti kācaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should recognize as <s>kāca</s> devices: throwing in, the measure, fire, a pellet, a vessel-holder, a brush, thread, cloth, <s>bollana</s>, the head, the lap, the fly, inspection of one's own body, a bag, a water-bowl, and the fire-stand.

children.text: rājatānāṃ visraṃ malagrāhi paruṣaṃ prastīnaṃ vivarṇaṃ vā duṣṭam iti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: Among silver goods, what is rank, dirt-catching, rough, encrusted, or discolored should be known as defective.

children.text: evaṃ navaṃ ca jīrṇaṃ ca virūpaṃ cāpi bhāṇḍakam
children.translated_text: Thus, both new and old goods, and also misshapen goods,
he should examine, and he should assign their penalty as prescribed.

The superintendent of storehouses should ascertain the stocks, expenditures, returns, and balances arising from crown lands, the countryside, purchases, exchanges, measured receipts, measured issues, collections, and miscellaneous sources.
The class of grain brought in by the superintendent of crown lands is <s>sītā</s>.

children.text: piṇḍakaraḥ ṣaḍbhāgaḥ senābhaktaṃ baliḥ kara utsaṅgaḥ pārśvaṃ pārihīṇikam aupāyanikaṃ kauṣṭheyakaṃ ca rāṣṭram ||
children.translated_text: The revenues from the countryside are the lump tax, the sixth share, provisions for the army, tribute, regular tax, surcharge, collateral payment, deficiency charge, presents, and the storehouse levy.
Receipts from the price of grain, withdrawals from the treasury, and repayment of advances are the category called <s>krayima</s>.
Exchange of varieties of crops at a difference in price is called <s>parivartaka</s>.
Soliciting grain from elsewhere is called <s>prāmityaka</s>.
That same transaction, when intended for repayment, is called <s>āpamityaka</s>.

children.text: kuṭṭakarocakasaktuśuktapiṣṭakarma tajjīvaneṣu tailapīḍanam audracākrikeṣvikṣūṇāṃ ca kṣārakarma saṃhanikā ||
children.translated_text: The levies from pounding, processing, parched meal, sour gruel, and flour-work among those who live by these trades, from oil pressing, from water-wheel workers, and from alkali-processing of sugarcane form the <s>saṃhanikā</s>.
Lost, forgotten, and similar property is miscellaneous income.
Remainders from deposits, illness, and undertakings left unfinished are recoveries of expenditure.

children.text: tulāmānāntaraṃ hastapūraṇam utkaro vyājī paryuṣitaṃ prārjitaṃ copasthānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Differences in scales and measures, hand-fillings, surplus, profit, stale stock, and accumulated gain are called <s>upasthāna</s>.
We shall state the grain schedule for grain, fats, alkalis, and salts under the Superintendent of Agriculture.
Ghee, oil, fat, and marrow are the fats.
Phāṇita, jaggery, matsyaṇḍikā, lump sugar, and sugar-candy are the class here called <s>kṣāra</s>.
Rock salt, sea salt, biḍa salt, yavakṣāra, sauvarcala, and salt produced from outcrops are the salt class.
Kṣaudra and mārdvīka are the kinds of honey.

children.text: ikṣurasaguḍamadhuphāṇitajāmbavapanasānām anyatamo meṣaśṛṅgīpippalīkvāthābhiṣuto māsikaḥ ṣāṇmāsikaḥ sāṃvatsariko vā cidbhiṭorvārukekṣukāṇḍāmraphalāmalakāvasutaḥ śuddho vā śuktavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Any one of sugarcane juice, jaggery, honey, phāṇita, jambu fruit, or jackfruit, steeped with a decoction of meṣaśṛṅgī and long pepper for a month, six months, or a year, or set with cidbhiṭa, cucumber, sugarcane stalk, mango fruit, or āmalaka, or left pure, is the sour-ferment class.
Vṛkṣāmla, karamarda, mango, vidala, āmalaka, citron, kola, badara, sauvīraka, parūṣaka, and the like are the fruit-acid class.
Curds, grain-sour preparations, and the like are the liquid-acid class.
Long pepper, black pepper, ginger, ajājī, kirātatikta, white mustard, coriander, coraka, damanaka, maruvaka, drumstick stalks, and the like are the pungent class.
Dried fish, meat, tubers, roots, fruits, leafy vegetables, and the like are the relish class.

children.text: tato 'rdham āpadarthaṃ jānapadānāṃ sthāpayed ardham upayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: Of that stock, he should set aside half as an emergency reserve for the people of the countryside and use half.
And with new stock he should clear out the old.

children.text: kṣuṇṇaghṛṣṭapiṣṭabhṛṣṭānām ārdraśuṣkasiddhānāṃ ca dhānyānāṃ vṛddhikṣayapramāṇāni pratyakṣīkurvīta ||
children.translated_text: He should directly ascertain the measures of increase and loss for grains that are crushed, rubbed, ground, roasted, wet, dry, and cooked.

children.text: kodravavrīhīṇām ardhaṃ sāraḥ śālīnām ardhabhāgonaḥ tribhāgono varakāṇām ||
children.translated_text: For kodrava millet and vrīhi rice, half is the cleaned yield; for śāli rice it is less by half a share, and for varaka it is less by a third.
For priyaṅgu the cleaned yield is half, with an increase of one ninth.

children.text: udārakastulyaḥ yavā godhūmāśca kṣuṇṇāḥ tilā yavā mudgamāṣāśca ghṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For udāraka the same applies. Barley and wheat are in the crushed category; sesame, barley, mung beans, and black gram are in the rubbed category.
Wheat and parched meal have an increase of one fifth.
Kalāya and camasi are less by a quarter.
Mung beans and black gram are less by an eighth.
For śaumbya beans, half is the cleaned yield; for lentils it is less by a third.
Raw flour and kulmāṣa beans are one and a half times the original amount.

children.text: dviguṇo yāvakaḥ pulākaḥ piṣṭaṃ ca siddham ||
children.translated_text: Yāvaka, pulāka, and cooked flour are double.

children.text: kodravavarakodārakapriyaṅgūṇāṃ triguṇam annam caturguṇaṃ vrīhīṇām pañcaguṇaṃ śālīnām ||
children.translated_text: Cooked food from kodrava, varaka, udāraka, and priyaṅgu is threefold, from vrīhi fourfold, and from śāli fivefold.
Moistened secondary grain is double, and sprouted grain is one and a half times the original.
Roasted grains have an increase of one fifth.
Kalāya peas are double, as are parched grains and bharuja grains.
Oil from linseed is one sixth.
From neem, kuśa, mango, kapittha, and the like, it is one fifth.
Sesame, safflower, madhūka, and iṅgudī oils are one fourth.
For cotton and flax, from five palas there is one pala of thread.

children.text: pañcadroṇe śālīnāṃ dvādaśāḍhakaṃ taṇḍulānāṃ kalabhabhojanam ekādaśakaṃ vyālānām daśakam aupavāhyānāṃ navakaṃ sāmnāhyānām aṣṭakaṃ pattīnām saptakaṃ mukhyānām ṣaṭkaṃ devīkumārāṇām pañcakaṃ rājñām akhaṇḍapariśuddhānāṃ vā tuaṇḍulānāṃ prasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From five droṇas of śāli, twelve āḍhakas of rice make the ration for an elephant-calf, eleven for vyāla animals, ten for riding animals, nine for war-harnessed animals, eight for foot soldiers, seven for chief servants, six for queens and princes, and five for kings; alternatively, there is a prastha of unbroken, clean rice grains.

children.text: taṇḍulānāṃ prasthaḥ caturbhāgaḥ sūpaḥ sūpaṣoḍaśo lavaṇasyāṃśaḥ caturbhāgaḥ sarpiṣastailasya vaikam āryabhaktaṃ puṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man's noble ration is a prastha of rice, a quarter as much pulse-soup, salt in the amount of one sixteenth of the soup, and a quarter as much ghee or, alternatively, oil.
For those of lower status, the pulse-soup is one sixth and the fat is half as much.
For women it is less by a quarter.
For children it is half.

children.text: māṃsapalaviṃśatyā snehārdhakuḍubaḥ paliko lavaṇasyāṃśaḥ kṣārapalayogo dvidharaṇikaḥ kaṭukayogo dadhnuścārdhaprasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With twenty palas of meat go half a kuḍuba of fat, a pala's portion of salt, a pala-measure of alkali, two dharaṇas of pungents, and half a prastha of curds.
By this, the higher quantities are explained.

children.text: śākānām adhyardhaguṇaḥ śuṣkāṇāṃ dviguṇaḥ sa caiva yogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For vegetables the amount is one and a half times; for dried ones, double; and the same seasoning applies.
The prescribed ration quantities for elephants and horses will be stated under their respective superintendents.

children.text: balīvardānāṃ māṣadroṇaṃ yavānāṃ vā pulākaḥ śeṣam aśvavidhānam ||
children.translated_text: For oxen, a droṇa of black gram or of barley, or coarse grain, is given; the rest follows the horse ration.
The special addition is a tulā of oil-cake from the press, or ten āḍhakas of broken grain and bran.
For buffaloes and camels, it is double.
For donkeys, pṛṣata deer, and rohit deer, it is half a droṇa.
For eṇa antelopes and kuraṅga deer, it is one āḍhaka.
For goats, sheep, and pigs, it is half an āḍhaka, or twice that in broken grain and bran.
For dogs, there is a prastha of cooked rice.
For geese, krauñca birds, and peacocks, there is half a prastha.

children.text: śeṣāṇām ato mṛgapaśupakṣivyālānām ekabhaktād anumānaṃ grāhayet ||
children.translated_text: For the remaining deer, domestic animals, birds, and wild beasts, he should have the estimate made from a single meal.
He should have charcoal and husks supplied for iron workshops and for plastering walls.
He should give the fine grits to slaves, laborers, and soup-makers; anything else should be given to rice-cooks and cake-makers.

Scales, measuring vessels, the <s>rocanī</s>-stone, pestles, mortars, pounding implements, cleaning devices, trays, winnowing baskets, sieves, <s>kaṇḍolī</s> baskets, <s>piṭaka</s> baskets, and brooms are the equipment.
The body of sweepers, guards, carriers, measurers, apportioners, issuers, distributors, tally-stick receivers, slaves, and laborers is the forced labor force.

children.text: uccair dhānyasya nikṣepo mūtāḥ kṣārasya saṃhatāḥ
children.translated_text: Grain is to be stored high up; alkali in tightly packed sacks;
oils in earthen and wooden bins, and salt on the ground.

children.text: āyudhāgārādhyakṣaḥ sāṃgrāmikaṃ daurgakarmikaṃ parapurābhighātikaṃ ca yantram āyudham āvaraṇam upakaraṇaṃ ca tajjātakāruśilpibhiḥ kṛtakarmapramāṇakālavetanaphalaniṣpattibhiḥ kārayet svabhūmiṣu ca sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of the armory should have machines, weapons, defensive coverings, and equipment for battle, fortress work, and assault on enemy cities made by craftsmen and artisans of the appropriate kinds, with account taken of work done, measure, time, wages, and finished output; and he should store them in their proper places.
He should frequently shift their position and give them exposure to sun and air.
What is being damaged by heat, moisture, or worms he should store in another way.
He should ascertain them by kind, form, marks, measure, source, value, and deposit.

The <s>sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>jāmadagnya</s>, <s>bahumukha</s>, <s>viśvāsaghātin</s>, <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>yānaka</s>, <s>parjanyaka</s>, <s>bāhu</s>, <s>ūrdhvabāhu</s>, and <s>ardhabāhu</s> are stationary machines.

The <s>pāñcālika</s>, <s>devadaṇḍa</s>, <s>sūkarikā</s>, <s>musala</s>, <s>yaṣṭi</s>, <s>hastivāraka</s>, <s>tālavṛnta</s>, <s>mudgara</s>, <s>gadā</s>, <s>spṛktalā</s>, <s>kuddāla</s>, <s>āsphāṭima</s>, <s>utpāṭima</s>, <s>udghāṭima</s>, <s>śataghnī</s>, <s>triśūla</s>, and <s>cakra</s> are movable machines.

The <s>śakti</s>, <s>prāsa</s>, <s>kunta</s>, <s>hāṭaka</s>, <s>bhiṇḍipāla</s>, <s>śūla</s>, <s>tomara</s>, <s>varāhakarṇa</s>, <s>kaṇaya</s>, <s>karpaṇa</s>, <s>trāsikā</s>, and the like are weapons with spear-like points.
The <s>tāla</s>, <s>cāpa</s>, <s>dārava</s>, <s>śārṅga</s>, <s>kārmuka</s>, <s>kodaṇḍa</s>, and <s>drūṇa</s> are bows.
Bowstrings are made of <s>mūrvā</s> fiber, <s>arka</s> fiber, hemp, <s>gavedhu</s>, bamboo, and sinew.
Bamboo shafts, reeds, small rods, staff-arrows, and <s>nārāca</s> iron arrows are arrows.
Their points are for cutting, piercing, or striking, and are made of iron, bone, or wood.
The <s>nistriṃśa</s>, <s>maṇḍalāgra</s>, and <s>asiyaṣṭi</s> are swords.
Hilts are made from rhinoceros, buffalo, and elephant horn, wood, and bamboo root.
Axes, hatchets, broad-bladed weapons, picks, spades, saws, and stem-cutters are razor-like implements.
Engine-stones, sling-stones, fist-stones, stones, and <s>rocanī</s>-stones are stone weapons.
Armor consists of iron mesh, plates, cuirasses, corded armor, <s>kaṅkaṭa</s>, <s>śiṃśumāra</s>, rhinoceros-hide armor, <s>dhenuka</s>, elephant-hide and cowhide, and combinations of hoof and horn.

Head-guards, neck-guards, jackets, cuirasses, <s>vāravāṇa</s>, plates, and <s>nāgodarikā</s>, together with <s>peṭī</s>, hide, elephant-ear shields, palm-root shields, <s>dhamanikā</s>, doors, <s>kiṭikā</s>, <s>pratihata</s>, <s>balāhaka</s>, and end-coverings, are protective coverings.
Suitable gear for elephants, chariots, and horses, ornaments, and harness arrangements are equipment.
There is also work involving illusionist and esoteric practices.

children.text: karmāntānāṃ ca icchām ārambhaniṣpattiṃ prayogaṃ vyājam uddayam
children.translated_text: For the workshops, the armory chief should know the demand, undertaking, completion, use, incidental charge, and yield;
and he should know the loss and expenditure of materials.
The superintendent of weights and measures should have the workshops for weights and measures operated.

children.text: dhānyamāṣā daśa suvarṇamāṣakaḥ pañca vā guñjāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ten grain-<s>māṣa</s>s make one gold <s>māṣaka</s>, or five <s>guñjā</s> berries do so.
Sixteen of these make a <s>suvarṇa</s>, or a <s>karṣa</s>.
Four <s>karṣa</s>s make a <s>pala</s>.
Eighty-eight white mustard seeds make one silver <s>māṣaka</s>.

children.text: te ṣoḍaśa dharaṇaṃ śaimbyāni vā viṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sixteen of these make a <s>dharaṇa</s>, or twenty <s>śaimbya</s> beans do so.
Twenty rice grains make a diamond-<s>dharaṇa</s>.

children.text: ardhamāṣakaḥ māṣakaḥ dvau catvāraḥ aṣṭau māṣakāḥ suvarṇo dvau catvāraḥ aṣṭau suvarṇāḥ daśa viṃśatiḥ triṃśat catvāriṃśat śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: The series is a half-<s>māṣaka</s>, one <s>māṣaka</s>, two, four, and eight <s>māṣaka</s>s; one <s>suvarṇa</s>, two, four, and eight <s>suvarṇa</s>s; ten, twenty, thirty, forty, and one hundred.
By that same rule, the <s>dharaṇa</s> weights are explained.

children.text: pratimānānyayomayāni māgadhamekalaśailamayāni yāni vā nodakapradehābhyāṃ vṛddhiṃ gaccheyur uṣṇena vā hrāsam ||
children.translated_text: The standard weights should be made of iron, or of stone from <s>Magadha</s> or <s>Mekala</s>, or of materials that would not increase by water or smearing, nor diminish through heat.

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgulād ūrdhvam aṣṭāṅgulottarā daśa tulāḥ kārayel lohapalād ūrdhvam ekapalottarāḥ yantram ubhayataḥśikyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: He should make ten balances, beginning above six <s>aṅgula</s>s and increasing by eight <s>aṅgula</s>s, beginning above one iron <s>pala</s> and increasing by one <s>pala</s>, either as a mechanism or with a sling-pan on each side.
He should make one of thirty-five <s>pala</s>s of iron, seventy-two <s>aṅgula</s>s long, and evenly rounded.

children.text: tasyāḥ pañcapalikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ baddhvā samakaraṇaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having attached a five-<s>pala</s> disk to it, he should have it calibrated.

children.text: tataḥ karṣottaraṃ palaṃ palottaraṃ daśapalaṃ dvādaśa pañcadaśa viṃśatir iti padāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should have marks made for a <s>karṣa</s> and upward, for a <s>pala</s> and upward to ten <s>pala</s>s, and for twelve, fifteen, and twenty.
After that, up to one hundred, he should have marks made in increments of ten.
He should have it fastened on the pivots with <s>nāndī</s> fittings.

children.text: dviguṇalohāṃ tulām ataḥ ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulāyāmāṃ parimāṇīṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After this, he should make a <s>parimāṇī</s> balance with twice the iron, ninety-six <s>aṅgula</s>s long.

children.text: tasyāḥ śatapadād ūrdhvaṃ viṃśatiḥ pañcāśat śatam iti padāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: On it, above the hundred-mark, he should make marks for twenty, fifty, and one hundred.
A <s>bhāra</s> load is twenty <s>tulā</s>s.
A <s>pala</s> is ten <s>dharaṇa</s>s.
One hundred such <s>pala</s>s make the <s>āyamānī</s> balance.
The <s>vyāvahārikī</s>, the <s>bhājanī</s>, and the <s>antaḥpurabhājanī</s> are each lower by five <s>pala</s>s.

children.text: tāsām ardhadharaṇāvaraṃ palam dvipalāvaram uttaraloham ṣaḍaṅgulāvarāścāyāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For these, the <s>pala</s> is reduced by half a <s>dharaṇa</s>, the upper iron by two <s>pala</s>s, and the lengths by six <s>aṅgula</s>s.
For the first two, an allowance of five <s>pala</s>s is made, except in the case of meat, metal, salt, and jewels.
The wooden balance is eight <s>hasta</s>s long, furnished with marks and standard weights, and set on a peacock-foot base.
A wooden standard of twenty-five <s>pala</s>s serves to establish a <s>prastha</s> of rice.
This is the rule for larger and smaller quantities.
Thus scales and standard weights have been explained.

children.text: atha dhānyamāṣadvipalaśataṃ droṇam āyamānam saptāśītipalaśatam ardhapalaṃ ca vyāvahārikam pañcasaptatipalaśataṃ bhājanīyam dviṣaṣṭipalaśatam ardhapalaṃ cāntaḥpurabhājanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Now, for grain and beans, the receipt <s>droṇa</s> is two hundred <s>pala</s>s; the transactional one is one hundred eighty-seven and a half <s>pala</s>s; the distributive one is one hundred seventy-five <s>pala</s>s; and the distributive measure for the inner palace is one hundred sixty-two and a half <s>pala</s>s.
For these, the <s>āḍhaka</s>, <s>prastha</s>, and <s>kuḍuba</s> are successively smaller by quarters.
Sixteen <s>droṇa</s>s make a <s>khārī</s>.
A <s>kumbha</s> contains twenty <s>droṇa</s>s.
A <s>vaha</s> consists of ten <s>kumbha</s>s.

children.text: śuṣkasāradārumayaṃ samaṃ caturbhāgaśikhaṃ mānaṃ kārayet antaḥśikhaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: He should have the measuring vessel made of dry hard wood, even, with a quarter-height rim, or with the rim on the inside.

children.text: rasasya tu surāyāḥ puṣpaphalayostuṣāṅgārāṇāṃ sudhāyāśca śikhāmānaṃ dviguṇottarā vṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for juice, liquor, flowers and fruits, husks, charcoal, and lime, the increase in the heaped measure is successively doubled.

children.text: sapādapaṇo droṇamūlyam āḍhakasya pādonaḥ ṣaṇmāṣakāḥ prasthasya māṣakaḥ kuḍubasya ||
children.translated_text: The price of a <s>droṇa</s> measure is one and a quarter <s>paṇa</s>s; that of an <s>āḍhaka</s> is three-quarters of a <s>paṇa</s>; that of a <s>prastha</s> is six <s>māṣaka</s>s; and that of a <s>kuḍuba</s> is one <s>māṣaka</s>.
For liquids and the like, the price of the measure is double.
For a counter-standard measure, the price is twenty <s>paṇa</s>s.
The price of a balance is one-third of that.
He should have the periodical stamping done every four months.
For an unstamped measure, the penalty is twenty-seven and a quarter <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: prātivedhanikaṃ kākaṇīkam ahar ahaḥ pautavādhyakṣāya dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should pay a daily stamping fee of one <s>kākaṇī</s> to the superintendent of weights and measures.
The allowance for heating is one thirty-second part for ghee and one sixty-fourth part for oil.
For liquids, the leakage in measuring is one fiftieth part.
He should have measures made of one <s>kuḍuba</s>, one half, one quarter, and one eighth.
Eighty-four <s>kuḍuba</s>s are regarded as a <s>vāraka</s> of ghee.
For oil, however, it is sixty-four, and for the two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s there is a quarter.

children.text: surādhyakṣaḥ surākiṇvavyavahārān durge janapade skandhāvāre vā tajjātasurākiṇvavyavahāribhiḥ kārayed ekamukham anekamukhaṃ vā vikrayakrayavaśena vā ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of liquor should have the business in liquor and ferment carried on in the fort, the countryside, or the military camp by dealers in liquor and ferment produced there, either through a single outlet, through many outlets, or according to buying and selling.
He should impose a penalty of six hundred on makers, buyers, and sellers elsewhere.

children.text: grāmād anirṇayaṇam asaṃpātaṃ ca surāyāḥ pramādabhayāt karmasu nirdiṣṭānām maryādātikramabhayād āryāṇām utsāhabhayācca tīkṣṇānām ||
children.translated_text: Because of the danger of negligence among those assigned to work, of respectable persons overstepping proper bounds, and of violent men becoming emboldened, liquor should not be carried out from a village, nor should there be crowding together over it.

children.text: lakṣitam alpaṃ vā caturbhāgam ardhakuḍubaṃ kuḍubam ardhaprasthaṃ prasthaṃ veti jñātaśaucā nirhareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Persons known to be clean and trustworthy may carry out only a marked small amount: a quarter, half a <s>kuḍuba</s>, a <s>kuḍuba</s>, half a <s>prastha</s>, or a <s>prastha</s>.
Or, without moving about, they may drink in the drinking houses.

children.text: nikṣepopanidhiprayogāpahṛtānām aniṣṭopagatānāṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ jñānārtham asvāmikaṃ kupyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ copalabhya nikṣeptāram anyatra vyapadeśena grāhayed ativyayakartāram anāyativyayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For learning about goods lost from deposits, entrusted deposits, loans, thefts, and goods that have come into improper hands, on finding ownerless merchandise or gold, he should have the depositor seized under some other pretext, and likewise one who spends excessively or spends without an income.

children.text: na cānargheṇa kālikāṃ vā surāṃ dadyād anyatra duṣṭasurāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he should not give liquor at an improper price or on credit, except in the case of spoiled liquor.
He should have that sold elsewhere.
Or he should give it as wages to slaves and laborers.
Or he should give it as drink for draft animals or for feeding pigs.

children.text: pānāgārāṇyanekakakṣyāṇi vibhaktaśayanāsanavanti pānoddeśāni gandhamālyodakavanti ṛtusukhāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should establish taverns with many rooms, with separate beds and seats, with drinking areas furnished with perfumes, garlands, and water, and comfortable according to the season.

children.text: tatrasthāḥ prakṛtyautpattikau vyayau gūḍhā vidyuḥ āgantūṃśca ||
children.translated_text: Secret agents stationed there should learn both the ordinary and incidental expenditures, and also the newcomers.
They should learn about the ornaments, clothing, and gold of buyers who are drunk or asleep.
If those are lost, the merchants should pay back that property and also an equal fine.

children.text: vaṇijastu saṃvṛteṣu kakṣyāvibhāgeṣu svadāsībhiḥ peśalarūpābhir āgantūnāṃ vāstavyānāṃ cāryarūpāṇāṃ mattasuptānāṃ bhāvaṃ vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the enclosed compartmented rooms, the merchants, through their own female slaves who are graceful in appearance, should learn the intentions of visitors and residents of respectable appearance who are drunk or asleep.
The preparations of <s>medaka</s>, <s>prasannā</s>, <s>āsava</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and <s>madhu</s> are as follows.

children.text: udakadroṇaṃ taṇḍulānām ardhāḍhakaṃ trayaḥ prasthāḥ kiṇvasyeti medakayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>droṇa</s> of water, half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of rice, and three <s>prastha</s>s of ferment: this is the recipe for <s>medaka</s>.

children.text: dvādaśāḍhakaṃ piṣṭasya pañca prasthāḥ kiṇvasya kramukatvakphalayukto vā jātisambhāraḥ prasannāyogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>āḍhaka</s>s of flour and five <s>prastha</s>s of ferment, or a spice mixture joined with the bark and fruit of <s>kramuka</s>: this is the recipe for <s>prasannā</s>.

children.text: kapitthatulā phāṇitaṃ pañcataulikaṃ prastho madhuna ityāsavayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>tulā</s> of <s>kapittha</s>, five <s>tulā</s>s of <s>phāṇita</s>, and a <s>prastha</s> of honey: this is the recipe for <s>āsava</s>.
The superior kind has one quarter more, and the inferior kind one quarter less.
<s>Ariṣṭa</s>s, each for particular disorders, follow the standards of physicians.
<s>Maireya</s> is jaggery infused with a decoction of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> bark, or with a mixture of long pepper and black pepper and combined with <s>triphalā</s>.
Or, for all drinks made with jaggery, <s>triphalā</s> is the additive mixture.
<s>Madhu</s> is the juice of grapes.

children.text: tasya svadeśo vyākhyānaṃ kāpiśāyanaṃ hārahūrakam iti ||
children.translated_text: Its local explanation is <s>Kāpiśāyana</s> and <s>Hārahūraka</s>.

children.text: māṣakalanīdroṇamāmaṃ siddhaṃ vā tribhāgādhikataṇḍulaṃ moraṭādīnāṃ kārṣikabhāgayuktaṃ kiṇvabandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>droṇa</s> of <s>māṣa</s> and <s>kalanī</s>, raw or cooked, with rice increased by one third and with one-<s>kārṣa</s> portions of <s>moraṭa</s> and the rest, is the binding preparation for ferment.

For <s>medaka</s> and <s>prasannā</s>, the ingredient mixture consists of five-<s>kārṣa</s> portions each of <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>tejovatī</s>, <s>elā</s>, <s>vāluka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madhurasā</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>dāruharidrā</s>, black pepper, and long pepper.
Rock sugar mixed with a decoction of <s>madhuka</s> clarifies the color.

The ingredients for <s>āsava</s> are one <s>kārṣa</s> each of <s>coca</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vilaṅga</s>, and <s>gajapippalī</s>, and two <s>kārṣa</s>s each of <s>kramuka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>.
One tenth part of these is the seed-ferment preparation.
The recipe for white liquor is the recipe for <s>prasannā</s>.

children.text: sahakārasurā rasottarā bījottarā vā mahāsurā saṃbhārikī vā ||
children.translated_text: Mango liquor has a predominance of juice, or else a predominance of seed-ferment; <s>mahāsurā</s> is made with additional ingredients.

children.text: tāsāṃ moraṭāpalāśapattūrameṣaśṛṅgīkarañjakṣīravṛkṣakaṣāyabhāvitaṃ dagdhakaṭaśarkarācūrṇaṃ lodhracitrakavilaṅgapāṭhāmustākaliṅgayavadāruharidrendīvaraśatapuṣpāpāmārgasaptaparṇanimbāsphotakalkārdhayuktam antarnakho muṣṭiḥ kumbhīṃ rājapeyāṃ prasādayati ||
children.translated_text: For these, a closed handful of powder of burnt <s>kaṭaśarkarā</s>, steeped in a decoction of <s>moraṭa</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>pattūra</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and milk-trees, and mixed with half as much paste of <s>lodhra</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vilaṅga</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>kaliṅga</s>, barley, <s>dāruharidrā</s>, blue lotus, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>āsphoṭa</s>, clarifies a jar of the royal drink.
Here five <s>pala</s>s of <s>phāṇita</s> syrup should also be added to increase the flavor.

children.text: kuṭumbinaḥ kṛtyeṣu śvetasurām auṣadhārthaṃ vāriṣṭam anyad vā kartuṃ labheran ||
children.translated_text: Householders may receive permission to make white <s>surā</s> for rites, or <s>āriṣṭa</s> or some other drink for medicinal use.
At festivals, assemblies, and processions a four-day liquor concession should be granted.
From those who engage in these without permission, he should collect the daily penalty until the end of the celebration.
Women and children should do the collecting of <s>surā</s> and ferment.

children.text: arājapaṇyāḥ pañcakaṃ śataṃ śulkaṃ dadyuḥ surakāmedakāriṣṭamadhuphalāmlāmlaśīdhūnāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Private dealers should pay a duty of five per hundred on <s>surā</s>, <s>medaka</s>, <s>āriṣṭa</s>, <s>madhu</s>, fruit-sour liquor, sour liquor, and <s>śīdhu</s>.
Having determined the day's sales and the surcharge in measures and cash,
he should likewise make the balancing adjustment and follow the established practice.
Three <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s> officers, each with three ministers, should carry out the removal of criminal elements.

children.text: arthyapratīkārāḥ kāruśāsitāraḥ saṃnikṣeptāraḥ svavittakāravaḥ śreṇīpramāṇā nikṣepaṃ gṛhṇīyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Depositaries who are able to make restitution, supervisors of artisans, trustees, artisans with property of their own, and persons vouched for by the guild should accept deposits.
