In case of misfortune, the guild should bear responsibility for the deposit.

children.text: nirdiṣṭadeśakālakāryaṃ ca karma kuryuḥ anirdiṣṭadeśakālaṃ kāryāpadeśam ||
children.translated_text: They should perform work whose place, time, and task have been specified; when place and time are not specified, they should follow the statement of the task.
For delay beyond the time, the wage is reduced by a quarter and the fine is twice that.
Except in cases of error or accident, they should make good what is lost or destroyed.
If the work is done otherwise than ordered, there is loss of the wage and a fine twice that.
Weavers should increase the thread in the ratio of ten to eleven.
If that increase is cut short, the fine is twice the amount cut.

children.text: sūtramūlyaṃ vānavetanaṃ kṣaumakauśeyānām adhyardhaguṇaṃ pattrorṇākambaladukūlānāṃ dviguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Or the weaving wage is the value of the thread; for linen and silk it is one and a half times that, and for <s>pattrorṇa</s>, blankets, and <s>dukūla</s> it is double.

children.text: mānahīne hīnāvahīnaṃ vetanaṃ taddviguṇaśca daṇḍas tulāhīne hīnacaturguṇo daṇḍaḥ sūtraparivartane mūlyadviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the measure is deficient, the wage is reduced by the deficiency and the fine is twice that; if the weight is deficient, the fine is four times the deficiency; for substitution of thread, the fine is twice the value.
By this, the weaving of double cloth is explained.
For a <s>tulā</s> of wool, the allowance for beating and shearing the hair is five <s>pala</s>s.
Washermen should wash garments on wooden boards, planks, or smooth stones.

children.text: anyatra nenijato vastropaghātaṃ ṣaṭpaṇaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If they wash them elsewhere, they should pay for damage to the garment and a fine of six <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: mudgarāṅkād anyad vāsaḥ paridadhānāstripaṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who wear a garment other than one bearing the <s>mudgarāṅka</s> mark should pay a fine of three <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: paravastravikrayāvakrayādhāneṣu ca dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ parivartane mūlyadviguṇo vastradānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For selling, letting out, or pledging another's garment, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s; for exchanging it, the fine is twice its value, and the garment must be given back.

children.text: mukulāvadātaṃ śilāpaṭṭaśuddhaṃ dhautasūtravarṇaṃ pramṛṣṭaśvetaṃ caikarātrottaraṃ dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should return after one night a garment whitened like a bud, cleaned on a stone slab, of washed-thread color, or rubbed clean and white.

children.text: pañcarātrikaṃ tanurāgaṃ ṣaḍrātrikaṃ nīlaṃ puṣpalākṣāmañjiṣṭhāraktaṃ guruparikarma yatnopacāryaṃ jātyaṃ vāsaḥ saptarātrikam ||
children.translated_text: A lightly dyed garment is due after five nights, a blue one after six nights, and one reddened with flowers, lac, or madder, one requiring heavy processing, one to be handled carefully, or a fine garment after seven nights.
After that they incur a loss of wages.
In disputes about dyeing, trustworthy skilled persons should determine the wage.

children.text: parārdhyānāṃ paṇo vetanaṃ madhyamānām ardhapaṇaḥ pratyavarāṇāṃ pādaḥ sthūlakānāṃ māṣakadvimāṣakaṃ dviguṇaṃ raktakānām ||
children.translated_text: For superior garments the wage is one <s>paṇa</s>, for middle ones half a <s>paṇa</s>, for inferior ones a quarter, for coarse ones one or two <s>māṣaka</s>s, and for red ones double.
At the first washing the loss is one quarter; at the second it is one fifth.
By this, the subsequent cases are explained.
Tailors are explained by the rules for washermen.

children.text: suvarṇakārāṇām aśucihastād rūpyaṃ suvarṇam anākhyāya sarūpaṃ krīṇatāṃ dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍo virūpaṃ caturviṃśatipaṇaś corahastād aṣṭacatvāriṃśatpaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For goldsmiths, if they buy silver or gold from an impure hand without reporting it, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s when it is in the same form, twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s when it is altered, and forty-eight <s>paṇa</s>s when it is from a thief's hand.
For secret purchase, purchase of altered goods, purchase below value, and fraud in finished goods, the penalty is the penalty for theft.

children.text: suvarṇān māṣakam apaharato dviśato daṇḍaḥ rūpyadharaṇān māṣakam apaharato dvādaśapaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For stealing a <s>māṣaka</s> from a <s>suvarṇa</s> of gold, the fine is two hundred; for stealing a <s>māṣaka</s> from a <s>dharaṇa</s> of silver, it is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the further cases are explained.

children.text: varṇotkarṣam apasāraṇaṃ yogaṃ vā sādhayataḥ pañcaśato daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For carrying out enhancement of color, removal, or alloying, the fine is five hundred.
In malpractice with either of these, he should recognize it as theft of color.
The wage is one <s>māṣaka</s> for a <s>dharaṇa</s> of silver, and one eighth for a <s>suvarṇa</s> of gold.
With special skill, the increase in wages is doubled.
By this, the further cases are explained.
For workers in copper, <s>vṛtta</s>, bell-metal, <s>vaikṛnta</s>, and <s>ārakūṭa</s>, the wage is five per hundred.
For a lump of copper, the loss is one tenth.
If the weight is deficient by a <s>pala</s>, the fine is twice the deficiency.
By this, the further cases are explained.
For a lump of lead or tin, the loss is one twentieth.
Its wage per <s>pala</s> is one <s>kākaṇī</s>.
For a lump of black iron, the loss is one fifth.
Its wage per <s>pala</s> is two <s>kākaṇī</s>s.
By this, the further cases are explained.

children.text: rūpadarśakasya sthitāṃ paṇayātrām akopyāṃ kopayataḥ kopyām akopayato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a coin examiner who rejects an established currency that should not be rejected, or fails to reject one that should be rejected, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
The circulation of currency depends on the clearing of the exchange surcharge.
For one who lives by taking a <s>māṣaka</s> from each <s>paṇa</s>, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the further cases are explained.

children.text: kūṭarūpaṃ kārayataḥ pratigṛhṇato niryāpayato vā sahasraṃ daṇḍaḥ kośe prakṣipato vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who has counterfeit coin made, accepts it, or issues it, the fine is one thousand; for one who puts it into the treasury, the penalty is death.

children.text: carakapāṃsudhāvakāḥ sāratribhāgaṃ labheran dvau rājā ratnaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Collectors and washers of mineral dust should receive one-third of the valuable yield; the king should receive two shares and the gem.
For stealing a gem, the highest fine applies.

children.text: khaniratnanidhinivedaneṣu ṣaṣṭham aṃśaṃ nivettā labheta dvādaśam aṃśaṃ bhṛtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In reports of mines, gems, and treasure-troves, the informer should receive a sixth share, and the hired worker a twelfth share.
A treasure over one hundred thousand goes to the king.
If it is less, he should give a sixth share.

children.text: paurvapauruṣikaṃ nidhiṃ jānapadaḥ śuciḥ svakaraṇena samagraṃ labheta ||
children.translated_text: A trustworthy country resident should receive in full an ancestral treasure, when it is established by his own proof.
In the absence of his own proof, the fine is five hundred; for taking it secretly, one thousand.

children.text: bhiṣajaḥ prāṇābādhikam anākhyāyopakramamāṇasya vipattau pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ karmāparādhena vipattau madhyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a physician who begins treatment without declaring a danger to life, if mishap occurs, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; if mishap occurs through a fault in the procedure, the middle one applies.
For injury to a vital spot or causing deformity, he should recognize it as bodily violence.
Performers should remain in one place during the rainy season.
They should avoid taking excessive voluntary gifts from one person and also abusive speech.
For transgressing that, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
They may joke freely through ridicule about region, caste, lineage, school, and sexual matters.
The rules for performers, <s>cāraṇa</s>s, and beggars have been set out.

children.text: teṣām ayaḥśūlena yāvataḥ paṇān abhivadeyustāvantaḥ śiphāprahārā daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If they solicit however many <s>paṇa</s>s by means of an iron spike, the penalty is that many blows with a whip.
For the remaining occupations, he should fix artisans' wages according to completion of the work.
Thus thieves, those called non-thieves, merchants, artisans, and performers,
beggars, tricksters, and others he should restrain from oppressing the country.

children.text: saṃsthādhyakṣaḥ paṇyasaṃsthāyāṃ purāṇabhāṇḍānāṃ svakaraṇaviśuddhānām ādhānaṃ vikrayaṃ vā sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: The superintendent of markets should authorize the pledging or sale of old goods in the marketplace when their provenance has been cleared by their own proof.
He should also inspect scales, measures, and vessels for abuses in weighing and measuring.
For the <s>parimāṇī</s> and <s>droṇa</s> measures, deficiency or excess up to half a <s>pala</s> is no offense.
If there is deficiency or excess of a <s>pala</s>, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the increase of the fine for each additional <s>pala</s> is explained.
For a balance, deficiency or excess up to a <s>karṣa</s> is no offense.
If there is deficiency or excess of two <s>karṣa</s>s, the fine is six <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the increase of the fine for each additional <s>karṣa</s> is explained.
For an <s>āḍhaka</s>, deficiency or excess up to half a <s>karṣa</s> is no offense.
If there is deficiency or excess of a <s>karṣa</s>, the fine is three <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the increase of the fine for each additional <s>karṣa</s> is explained.
From this one should infer the rule for other special scales and measures.

children.text: tulāmānābhyām atiriktābhyāṃ krītvā hīnābhyāṃ vikrīṇānasya ta eva dviguṇā daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who buys with excessive scales and measures and sells with deficient ones, those same fines are doubled.
For one who misappropriates one-eighth in countable merchandise or in the value of goods, the fine is ninety-six <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: kāṣṭhalohamaṇimayaṃ rajjucarmamṛṇmayaṃ sūtravalkaromamayaṃ vā jātyam ityajātyaṃ vikrayādhānaṃ nayato mūlyāṣṭaguṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who brings to sale or pledge an ungenuine item, saying it is genuine, whether made of wood, metal, gems, rope, leather, clay, thread, bark, or hair, the fine is eight times the value.

children.text: sārabhāṇḍam ityasārabhāṇḍaṃ tajjātam ityatajjātaṃ rādhāyuktam ityupadhiyuktaṃ samudgaparivartimaṃ vā vikrayādhānaṃ nayato hīnamūlyaṃ catuṣpañcāśatpaṇo daṇḍaḥ paṇamūlyaṃ dviguṇo dvipaṇamūlyaṃ dviśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who brings to sale or pledge a worthless article saying it is valuable, something not of that kind saying it is of that kind, an adulterated thing saying it is properly prepared, or something switched in a casket, the fine is fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s when the value is low, double that when it is worth one <s>paṇa</s>, and two hundred when it is worth two <s>paṇa</s>s.
By this, the increase of fines as price rises is explained.

children.text: kāruśilpināṃ karmaguṇāpakarṣam ājīvaṃ vikrayakrayopaghātaṃ vā sambhūya samutthāpayatāṃ sahasraṃ daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For craftsmen and artisans who combine to cause a decline in workmanship, to manipulate livelihood rates, or to obstruct selling and buying, the fine is one thousand.

children.text: vaidehakānāṃ vā sambhūya paṇyam avarundhatām anargheṇa vikrīṇatāṃ vā sahasraṃ daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, for merchants who combine to withhold merchandise or sell it at an improper price, the fine is one thousand.

children.text: tulāmānāntaram arghavarṇāntaraṃ vā dharakasya māyakasya vā paṇamūlyād aṣṭabhāgaṃ hastadoṣeṇācarato dviśato daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a weigher or measurer who, by sleight of hand, creates a discrepancy in scale or measure, or in price or quality, amounting to one-eighth of a <s>paṇa</s>'s value, the fine is two hundred.
By this, the increase of fines in increments of two hundred is explained.
For adulterating grain, oil, alkali, salt, perfumes, or medicinal substances with materials of the same color, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: yannisṛṣṭam upajīveyustad eṣāṃ divasasaṃjātaṃ saṃkhyāya vaṇik sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever goods have been issued for them to live by, the merchant should count the day's proceeds from them and set them down.
What falls between buyer and seller is treated as distinct from the revenue taken.
Accordingly, they may make authorized stores of grain and merchandise.
Otherwise, the superintendent of merchandise should seize their unauthorized hoard.
By this rule he should conduct the sale of grain and merchandise with favor toward the subjects.

children.text: anujñātakrayād upari caiṣāṃ svadeśīyānāṃ paṇyānāṃ pañcakaṃ śatam ājīvaṃ sthāpayet paradeśīyānāṃ daśakam ||
children.translated_text: Above the authorized purchase price he should set their livelihood margin at five percent for domestic goods and ten percent for foreign goods.

children.text: tataḥ param arghaṃ vardhayatāṃ kraye vikraye vā bhāvayatāṃ paṇaśate pañcapaṇād dviśato daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those who raise the price beyond that, or manipulate it in buying or selling, the fine is two hundred for each rise of five <s>paṇa</s>s per hundred.
By this, the increase of fines as price rises is explained.

children.text: sambhūyakraye caiṣām avikrīte nānyaṃ sambhūyakrayaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: And when they have bought jointly, he should not grant them another joint purchase while the previous goods remain unsold.
When their merchandise is damaged, he should grant them relief.
When there is abundance of merchandise, the superintendent of merchandise should sell all goods through a single agency.
While those goods remain unsold, others should not sell.
They should sell them on daily wages, with favor toward the subjects.

children.text: deśakālāntaritānāṃ tu paṇyānāṃ prakṣepaṃ paṇyaniṣpattiṃ śulkaṃ vṛddhim avakrayam
children.translated_text: But for goods separated by place and time, considering outlay, production of the goods, duty, interest, and hire,

children.text: vyayān anyāṃśca saṃkhyāya sthāpayed argham arghavit ||
children.translated_text: the expert in prices should calculate other expenses as well and set the price.

children.text: daivānyaṣṭau mahābhayāni agnir udakaṃ vyādhir durbhikṣaṃ mūṣikā vyālāḥ sarpā rakṣāṃsīti ||
children.translated_text: The eight great providential dangers are fire, water, disease, famine, rats, wild beasts, snakes, and demons.
He should protect the countryside from them.

children.text: grīṣme bahiradhiśrayaṇaṃ grāmāḥ kuryuḥ daśamūlīsaṃgraheṇādhiṣṭhitā vā ||
children.translated_text: In summer the villages should carry out cooking outside, or else under supervision by a group of ten households.
Fire prevention has been explained in the arrangements for the city superintendent, and also in the arrangements for the royal residence and the king's possessions.
On festival days he should have worship of fire performed with offerings, oblations, and auspicious recitations.
During the rainy season, villages in marshy regions should abandon the flood line and reside elsewhere.
They should secure boats made of wood and bamboo.
They should rescue someone being swept away by means of gourds, skin bags, rafts, floats, and plaited ropes.
For those who do not come to help, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s, except in the case of those who have no raft.
And on festival days he should have worship of rivers performed.
Experts in occult practices, or experts in the Veda, should perform counter-rites against the rain.
When the rain is withheld, he should have worship of <s>Śacīnātha</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the mountains, and <s>Mahākaccha</s> performed.

children.text: vyādhibhayam aupaniṣadikaiḥ pratīkāraiḥ pratikuryuḥ auṣadhaiścikitsakāḥ śāntiprāyaścittair vā siddhatāpasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should counter the danger of disease with esoteric remedies; physicians should do so with medicines, or perfected ascetics with appeasement and expiatory rites.
By this, a deadly epidemic is also explained.

children.text: tīrthābhiṣecanaṃ mahākacchavardhanaṃ gavāṃ śmaśānāvadohanaṃ kabandhadahanaṃ devarātriṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should have performed bathing at sacred fords, the strengthening of <s>Mahākaccha</s>, the milking of cows in the cremation ground, the burning of a headless trunk, and the divine night rite.
In an epidemic of disease among animals, he should have a lustration for the place and worship of their own deities performed.

children.text: durbhikṣe rājā bījabhaktopagrahaṃ kṛtvānugrahaṃ kuryāt durgasetukarma vā bhaktānugraheṇa bhaktasaṃvibhāgaṃ vā deśanikṣepaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: In famine, the king should grant relief after providing seed grain and food; or he should undertake work on forts and irrigation works with food support, or distribute food, or arrange resettlement in another region.

children.text: mitrāṇi vā vyapāśrayeta karśanaṃ vamanaṃ vā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Or he should seek support from allies, or carry out retrenchment or evacuation.

children.text: niṣpannasasyam anyaviṣayaṃ vā sajanapado yāyāt samudrasarastaṭākāni vā saṃśrayeta ||
children.translated_text: Or, together with his population, he should go to another territory where the crop has ripened, or take refuge near seas, lakes, and reservoirs.

children.text: dhānyaśākamūlaphalāvāpān vā setuṣu kurvīta mṛgapaśupakṣivyālamatsyārambhān vā ||
children.translated_text: Or he should establish plantings of grain, vegetables, roots, and fruits at irrigation works, or begin enterprises involving game, livestock, birds, dangerous animals, and fish.
Against danger from mice, there should be a release of cats and mongooses.

children.text: teṣāṃ grahaṇahiṃsāyāṃ dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ śunām anigrahe cānyatrāraṇyacarebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For catching or injuring them, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s; the same applies for failing to restrain dogs, except for dogs that roam in the wilderness.
He should scatter grain smeared with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, or else grain prepared with esoteric compounds.
Or he should impose a <s>mūṣikakara</s>, a rat levy.
Or perfected ascetics should perform appeasement rites.
And on festival days he should have worship of mice performed.
By this, countermeasures against danger from locusts, birds, and insects are explained.
Against danger from savage animals, he should scatter animal carcasses mixed with <s>madana</s> sap, or entrails filled with <s>madana</s> and <s>kodrava</s>.
Hunters, or men with packs of dogs, should range about with traps, cages, and pits.
Men with protective coverings and weapons in hand should kill the savage animals.
For one who does not come to help, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.
That same amount is the reward for the slayer of a savage animal.
And on festival days he should have worship of mountains performed.
By this, countermeasures against attacks by groups of wild animals, livestock, and birds are explained.
Against danger from snakes, experts in snake-poison lore should go about with mantras and medicines.
Or, having assembled together, they should kill the snakes.
Or experts in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> should perform counter-rites.
And on festival days he should have worship of <s>nāga</s>s performed.
By this, countermeasures against danger from aquatic creatures are explained.

children.text: rakṣobhaye rakṣoghnānyatharvavedavido māyāyogavido vā karmāṇi kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Against danger from demons, experts in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> or experts in occult practices should perform demon-destroying rites.
And on festival days he should have worship of shrines performed with platforms, parasols, <s>ullopikā</s>s, hand-banners, and offerings of goats.
In every danger they should go about day and night saying, 'We prepare a <s>caru</s> oblation for you.'
Everywhere he should favor the afflicted like a father.
Therefore experts in occult practices and perfected ascetics in the realm,
honored by the king, should dwell there as counteractors of calamities caused by divine forces.
In the arrangements for the <s>samāhartṛ</s>, the protection of the countryside has been stated.
Now we shall explain its <s>kaṇṭakaśodhana</s>, the removal of thorns.

The <s>samāhartṛ</s> should station in the countryside perfected ascetics, renunciants, wandering mendicants, bards, tricksters, disguised agents, astrologers, omen-readers, time-diviners, physicians, madmen, mutes, deaf persons, dullards, blind persons, traders, artisans, craftsmen, performers, prostitutes, liquor sellers, cake sellers, cooked-meat sellers, rice sellers, and condiment sellers.

children.text: te grāmāṇām adhyakṣāṇāṃ ca śaucāśaucaṃ vidyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should learn the integrity and corruption of the villages and of the superintendents.

children.text: yaṃ cātra gūḍhājīvinaṃ śaṅketa taṃ sattriṇāpasarpayet ||
children.translated_text: And anyone there whom he suspects of living by hidden means, he should have approached through a secret agent.

children.text: dharmasthaṃ viśvāsopagataṃ sattrī brūyād asau me bandhur abhiyuktaḥ tasyāyam anarthaḥ pratikriyatām ayaṃ cārthaḥ pratigṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: After gaining the confidence of a judge, the secret agent should say, 'A relative of mine has been accused; let this misfortune of his be remedied, and let this money be accepted.'

children.text: sa cet tathā kuryād upadāgrāhaka iti pravāsyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he acts accordingly, he should be banished as one who accepts a bribe.
By this, the <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s>s are explained.

children.text: grāmakūṭam adhyakṣaṃ vā sattrī brūyād asau jālmaḥ prabhūtadravyas tasyāyam anarthaḥ tenainam āhārayasva iti ||
children.translated_text: The secret agent should say to a village headman or superintendent, 'That scoundrel has abundant wealth; this misfortune is his, so use it to make him pay.'

children.text: sa cet tathā kuryād utkocaka iti pravāsyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he acts accordingly, he should be banished as an extortioner.
Or a contrived defendant should engage persons known as false witnesses by offering a large sum of money.

children.text: te cet tathā kuryuḥ kūṭasākṣiṇa iti pravāsyeran ||
children.translated_text: If they act accordingly, they should be banished as false witnesses.
By this, those who procure false depositions are explained.

children.text: yaṃ vā mantrayogamūlakarmabhiḥ śmāśānikair vā saṃvadanakārakaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī brūyād amuṣya bhāryāṃ snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ vā kāmaye sā māṃ pratikāmayatām ayaṃ cārthaḥ pratigṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, regarding someone whom he thinks to cause attraction by spells, occult practices, root rites, or cemetery rites, the secret agent should say, 'I desire the wife, daughter-in-law, or daughter of so-and-so; let her desire me in return, and let this money be accepted.'

children.text: sa cet tathā kuryāt saṃvadanakāraka iti pravāsyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he were to do so, he should be banished as a maker of <s>saṃvadana</s> spells.
By this, those habituated to destructive rites and sorcery are explained.

children.text: yaṃ vā rasasya kartāraṃ kretāraṃ vikretāraṃ bhaiṣajyāhāravyavahāriṇaṃ vā rasadaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī brūyād asau me śatruḥ tasyopaghātaḥ kriyatām ayaṃ cārthaḥ pratigṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, to someone whom he considers a maker, buyer, or seller of poison, or a dealer in medicines or food who gives poison, a <s>sattrin</s> agent should say: "So-and-so is my enemy; let harm be done to him, and accept this payment."

children.text: sa cet tathā kuryād rasada iti pravāsyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he were to do so, he should be banished as a poisoner.
By this, a dealer in stupefying preparations is explained.

children.text: yaṃ vā nānālohakṣārāṇām aṅgārabhastrāsaṃdaṃśamuṣṭikādhikaraṇībimbaṭaṅkamūṣāṇām abhīkṣṇakretāraṃ maṣībhasmadhūmadigdhahastavastraliṅgaṃ karmāropakaraṇasaṃsargaṃ kūṭarūpakārakaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī śiṣyatvena saṃvyavahāreṇa cānupraviśya prajñāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Or, regarding someone whom he suspects to be a maker of counterfeit coin because he frequently buys various metals, alkalis, charcoal, bellows, tongs, hammers, anvils, molds, chisels, and crucibles, because his hands, clothes, and signs are smeared with soot, ash, and smoke, and because he is connected with smiths' tools, a <s>sattrin</s> agent should enter upon him as a pupil and through dealings with him make him disclose himself.
Once he is discovered, he should be banished as a maker of counterfeit coin.
By this, one who removes color and a dealer in counterfeit gold are explained.
But the hidden-livelihood men who have begun acts of violence are thirteen in number;
they should be banished, or else pay redemption money according to the particular offense.

children.text: sattriprayogād ūrdhvaṃ siddhavyañjanā māṇavān māṇavavidyābhiḥ pralobhayeyuḥ prasvāpanāntardhānadvārāpohamantreṇa pratirodhakān saṃvadanamantreṇa pāratalpikān ||
children.translated_text: After the employment of <s>sattrin</s> agents, persons disguised as adepts should entice young men with lore for young men: those who resist, with spells for putting to sleep, invisibility, and opening doors; and adulterers, with a spell of attraction.

children.text: teṣāṃ kṛtotsāhānāṃ mahāntaṃ saṃgham ādāya rātrāvanyaṃ grāmam uddiśyānyaṃ grāmaṃ kṛtakastrīpuruṣaṃ gatvā brūyuḥ ihaiva vidyāprabhāvo dṛśyatāṃ kṛcchraḥ paragrāmo gantum iti ||
children.translated_text: When these men have been made eager, the agents should take a large group at night and, while ostensibly heading for one village, go to another village furnished with staged women and men; then they should say, "Let the power of the lore be seen right here; the other village is hard to reach."

children.text: tato dvārāpohamantreṇa dvārāṇyapohya praviśyatām iti brūyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they should say, "By the door-opening spell, force open the doors and enter."

children.text: antardhānamantreṇa jāgratām ārakṣiṇāṃ madhyena māṇavān atikrāmayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the invisibility spell, they should lead the young men through the midst of wakeful guards.

children.text: prasvāpanamantreṇa prasvāpayitvā rakṣiṇaḥ śayābhir māṇavaiḥ saṃcārayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the sleep-inducing spell, after putting the guards to sleep, they should have the young men move about among the beds.
By the attraction spell, women disguised as wives should delight with the young men of others.
When they have perceived the power of the lore, the agents should prescribe preliminary rites and the like as a means of identification.
Or they should have them perform an act in houses where marked objects have been placed.
Agents who have infiltrated should have them arrested there.
Or they should have them arrested while buying, selling, or pledging marked objects, or when intoxicated with doctored liquor.
Those arrested should be interrogated together with the accomplices in their earlier offenses.

children.text: purāṇacoravyañjanā vā corān anupraviṣṭāstathaiva karma kārayeyur grāhayeyuśca ||
children.translated_text: Or agents disguised as old thieves, having infiltrated thieves, should in the same way have them perform an act and have them arrested.

children.text: gṛhītān samāhartā paurajānapadānāṃ darśayet coragrahaṇīṃ vidyām adhīte rājā tasyopadeśād ime corā gṛhītāḥ bhūyaśca grahīṣyāmi vārayitavyo vaḥ svajanaḥ pāpācāra iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>samāhartṛ</s> should display those arrested to the townsmen and country people, saying, "The king has learned the science of catching thieves. By his instruction these thieves have been arrested, and I shall arrest more. Your own people must be restrained from evil conduct."

children.text: yaṃ cātrāpasarpopadeśena śamyāpratodādīnām apahartāraṃ jānīyāt tam eṣāṃ pratyādiśed eṣa rājñaḥ prabhāvaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: And anyone whom he recognizes, through an undercover agent's instruction, as a thief of yokes, goads, and the like, he should point out to them, saying, "This is the king's power."

children.text: purāṇacoragopālakavyādhaśvagaṇinaśca vanacorāṭavikān anupraviṣṭāḥ prabhūtakūṭahiraṇyakupyabhāṇḍeṣu sārthavrajagrāmeṣvenān abhiyojayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Agents disguised as old thieves, cowherds, hunters, and keepers of packs of dogs, after infiltrating forest thieves and forest tribesmen, should induce them to attack caravans, cattle-pens, and villages rich in counterfeit gold and base goods.

children.text: abhiyoge gūḍhabalair ghātayeyuḥ madanarasayuktena vā pathyadanena ||
children.translated_text: During the attack they should have them killed by hidden troops, or by suitable food mixed with <s>madana-rasa</s>.

children.text: gṛhītaloptrabhārān āyatagatapariśrāntān prasvapataḥ prahavaṇeṣu yogasurāmattān vā grāhayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or they should have them arrested while they are carrying loads of seized plunder, exhausted after a long journey, asleep in resting places, or intoxicated with doctored liquor.
Having arrested them as before, the <s>samāhartṛ</s> should proclaim them,
causing the king's reputation for omniscience to be spread among the inhabitants of the realm.
After the use of proven devices comes apprehension by suspicion, appearance, and conduct.

children.text: kṣīṇadāyakuṭumbam alpanirveśaṃ viparītadeśajātigotranāmakarmāpadeśaṃ pracchannavṛttikarmāṇaṃ māṃsasurābhakṣyabhojanagandhamālyavastravibhūṣaṇeṣu prasaktam ativyayakartāraṃ puṃścalīdyūtaśauṇḍikeṣu prasaktam abhīkṣṇapravāsinam avijñātasthānagamanam ekāntāraṇyaniṣkuṭavikālacāriṇaṃ pracchanne sāmiṣe vā deśe bahumantrasaṃnipātaṃ sadyaḥkṣatavraṇānāṃ gūḍhapratīkārakārayitāram antargṛhanityam abhyadhigantāraṃ kāntāparaṃ paraparigrahāṇāṃ parastrīdravyaveśmanām abhīkṣṇapraṣṭāraṃ kutsitakarmaśāstropakaraṇasaṃsargaṃ virātre channakuḍyacchāyāsaṃcāriṇaṃ virūpadravyāṇām adeśakālavikretāraṃ jātavairāśayaṃ hīnakarmajātiṃ vigūhamānarūpaṃ liṅgenāliṅginaṃ liṅginaṃ vā bhinnācāraṃ pūrvakṛtāpadānaṃ svakarmabhir apadiṣṭaṃ nāgarikamahāmātradarśane gūhamānam apasarantam anucchvāsopaveśinam āvignaṃ śuṣkabhinnasvaramukhavarṇaṃ śastrahastamanuṣyasampātatrāsinaṃ hiṃsrastenanidhinikṣepāpahāraparaprayogagūḍhājīvinām anyatamaṃ śaṅketa ||
children.translated_text: One should suspect as one among violent men, thieves, removers of treasure and deposits, users of hostile practices, and hidden-livelihood criminals a person whose inheritance and family resources are exhausted, who has little capital, who gives false statements about his country, birth, lineage, name, occupation, or pretext, whose livelihood and work are concealed, who is attached to meat, liquor, forbidden foods, perfumes, garlands, clothes, and ornaments, who spends excessively, who is attached to loose women, gambling, and taverns, who is frequently away from home, who goes to unknown places, who moves alone in forests, enclosed places, or at improper times, who holds many consultations in concealed or baited places, who has fresh cuts and wounds treated secretly, who constantly enters inner houses, who is devoted to women, who repeatedly asks about others' possessions, wives, goods, and houses, who is connected with manuals and implements of vile acts, who moves at night along hidden walls and shadows, who sells strange goods at the wrong place and time, who harbors established enmity, who conceals a low occupation or birth, who hides his appearance, who wears the marks of an order without belonging to it, or belongs to an order but behaves contrary to it, who has committed former offenses, who is indicated by his own actions, who hides or slips away at the sight of the city officer or high officials, who sits breathlessly, who is agitated, whose voice and complexion are dry and broken, and who is frightened by an encounter with armed men.
Thus, apprehension by suspicion.
As for apprehension by appearance, one should report a lost, stolen, or missing object among those who deal in goods of that kind.

children.text: taccen niveditam āsādya pracchādayeyuḥ sācivyakaradoṣam āpnuyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, after receiving a report about it and coming upon it, they should conceal it, they incur the offense of abetting.
If they did not know, they may be released by surrendering the property.

children.text: na cānivedya saṃsthādhyakṣasya purāṇabhāṇḍānām ādhānaṃ vikrayaṃ vā kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should they pledge or sell old goods without reporting them to the <s>saṃsthādhyakṣa</s> (superintendent of trade establishments).

children.text: taccen niveditam āsādyeta rūpābhigṛhītam āgamaṃ pṛcchet kutaste labdham iti ||
children.translated_text: If, after being reported, that item is obtained and identified by its form, he should ask about its provenance: "From where did you get it?"

children.text: sa cet brūyāt dāyādyād avāptam amuṣmāllabdhaṃ krītaṃ kāritam ādhipracchannam ayam asya deśaḥ kālaścopasamprāpter ayam asyārghaḥ pramāṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ mūlyaṃ ca iti tasyāgamasamādhau mucyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he says, "It was received as inheritance, obtained from such-and-such a person, bought, made to order, or held as a concealed pledge; this is its place and time of acquisition; this is its price, measure, distinguishing mark, and value," then, when his provenance is established, he is released.

children.text: nāṣṭikaścet tad eva pratisaṃdadhyād yasya pūrvo dīrghaśca paribhogaḥ śucir vā deśas tasya dravyam iti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: If the loser connects the same particulars, one should know the property to belong to the person whose possession is earlier and long-standing, or whose place of provenance is clear.

children.text: catuṣpadadvipadānām api hi rūpaliṅgasāmānyaṃ bhavati kim aṅga punar ekayonidravyakartṛprasūtānāṃ kupyābharaṇabhāṇḍānām iti ||
children.translated_text: For even quadrupeds and bipeds may have similarity of form and marks; how much more, then, articles, ornaments, and vessels produced from the same source, material, and craftsman.

children.text: sa ced brūyāt yācitakam avakrītakam āhitakaṃ nikṣepam upanidhiṃ vaiyāvṛtyakarma vāmuṣya iti tasyāpasārapratisaṃdhānena mucyeta ||
children.translated_text: If he says, "This is borrowed, hired, pledged, deposited, a special deposit, or service-work belonging to such-and-such a person," he is released when that transfer is verified.

children.text: naivam ityapasāro vā brūyād rūpābhigṛhītaḥ parasya dānakāraṇam ātmanaḥ pratigrahakāraṇam upaliṅganaṃ vā dāyakadāpakanibandhakapratigrāhakopadraṣṭṛbhir upaśrotṛbhir vā pratisamānayet ||
children.translated_text: If the alleged transferor says, "It is not so," or if the item has been identified by its form, he should corroborate the other person's reason for giving, his own reason for receiving, or the identifying mark through the giver, the one who caused the giving, the recorder, the receiver, eyewitnesses, or persons who heard it.
For an item found as abandoned, lost, or fallen, clearance is obtained through indications of the place, time, manner of finding, and marks.
If he is not cleared, he should pay that property and a fine equal to it.
Otherwise he incurs the penalty for theft.
Thus, <s>rūpābhigraha</s> (apprehension by physical identification).

children.text: karmābhigrahastu muṣitaveśmanaḥ praveśaniṣkasanam advāreṇa dvārasya saṃdhinā bījena vā vedham uttamāgārasya jālavātāyananīpravedham ārohaṇāvataraṇe ca kuḍyasya vedham upakhananaṃ vā gūḍhadravyanikṣepaṇagrahaṇopāyam upadeśopalabhyam abhyantaracchedotkaraparimardopakaraṇam abhyantarakṛtaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: As for <s>karmābhigraha</s> (apprehension by the manner of the act): in a burgled dwelling, if entry and exit were through a non-door; if the door was pierced at a joint or with an implement; if the upper room was pierced through lattice, window, or vent; if the wall was pierced for climbing or descending, or undermined; if the method for placing or taking hidden property is found to have been pointed out; and if the cutting, digging, scraping, and tools are on the inside, one should know that it was done by someone within.
In the opposite case, it was done from outside; when signs are on both sides, it was done by both.

children.text: abhyantarakṛte puruṣam āsannaṃ vyasaninaṃ krūrasahāyaṃ taskaropakaraṇasaṃsargaṃ striyaṃ vā daridrakulām anyaprasaktāṃ vā paricārakajanaṃ vā tadvidhācāram atisvapnaṃ nidrāklāntam āvignaṃ śuṣkabhinnasvaramukhavarṇam anavasthitam atipralāpinam uccārohaṇasaṃrabdhagātraṃ vilūnanighṛṣṭabhinnapāṭitaśarīravastraṃ jātakiṇasaṃrabdhahastapādaṃ pāṃsupūrṇakeśanakhaṃ vilūnabhugnakeśanakhaṃ vā samyaksnātānuliptaṃ tailapramṛṣṭagātraṃ sadyodhautahastapādaṃ vā pāṃsupicchileṣu tulyapādapadanikṣepaṃ praveśaniṣkasanayor vā tulyamālyamadyagandhavastracchedavilepanasvedaṃ parīkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: When it was done from within, he should examine a nearby man, one addicted to vices, one with cruel associates, one connected with thieves' tools, or a woman from a poor family or attached elsewhere, or servants whose conduct is of that kind: someone oversleeping, worn out by sleep, agitated, with dry or broken voice and complexion, unsteady, too talkative, with body strained from climbing high, with body or clothing torn, rubbed, broken, or ripped, with hands and feet irritated by fresh calluses, with hair and nails full of dust, or with hair and nails torn or bent; or someone well bathed and anointed, with body rubbed with oil, with hands and feet freshly washed; or someone whose footprints match in dusty or muddy places, or whose garlands, liquor, scent, torn cloth, unguent, and sweat match at the places of entry and exit.
One should know him to be a thief or an adulterer.
The <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s> officer, together with the <s>gopa</s> and <s>sthānika</s>, should conduct the external search for thieves,
and the <s>nāgarika</s> (city superintendent), inside the fort, should do so on the grounds just specified.
He should examine a suddenly dead person anointed with oil.

children.text: niṣkīrṇamūtrapurīṣaṃ vātapūrṇakoṣṭhatvakkaṃ śūnapādapāṇim unmīlitākṣaṃ savyañjanakaṇṭhaṃ pīḍananiruddhocchvāsahataṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: If urine and feces have been discharged, the belly and skin are filled with air, the feet and hands are swollen, the eyes are open, and the neck bears marks, one should know that he was killed by pressure that obstructed his breathing.
The same person, with arms and thighs contracted, should be known as killed by hanging.
With hands, feet, and belly swollen, eyes displaced, and navel protruding, one should know him as one who was taken down after suspension.
With anus and eyes rigid, tongue bitten, and belly swollen, one should know him as killed by water.

children.text: śoṇitānusiktaṃ bhagnabhinnagātraṃ kāṣṭhair aśmabhir vā hataṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: Smeared with blood and with limbs broken and split, one should know him as killed with sticks or stones.
With limbs shattered and burst, one should know him as thrown down.
With hands, feet, teeth, and nails darkened, flesh, hair, and skin slack, and mouth smeared with foam, one should know him as killed by poison.
The same person, with a bloody bite mark, should be known as killed by a snake or insect.
With clothing and limbs disordered and with excessive vomiting and purging, one should know him as killed by a <s>madana-yoga</s> (emetic preparation).

children.text: ato 'nyatamena kāraṇena hataṃ hatvā vā daṇḍabhayād udbaddhanikṛttakaṇṭhaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should recognize when someone killed by any one of these causes, or killed first and then hanged or with his throat cut, has been so treated out of fear of punishment.
In the case of one killed by poison, he should test the remains of the food with birds.

children.text: hṛdayād uddhṛtyāgnau prakṣiptaṃ ciṭiciṭāyadindradhanurvarṇaṃ vā viṣayuktaṃ vidyāt dagdhasya hṛdayam adagdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vā ||
children.translated_text: Having taken it from the heart and thrown it into fire, if it crackles or has the color of a rainbow, one should know it as mixed with poison; likewise if, when the body is burned, the heart is seen to remain unburned.

children.text: tasya paricārakajanaṃ vāgdaṇḍapāruṣyātilabdhaṃ mārgeta duḥkhopahatam anyaprasaktaṃ vā strījanaṃ dāyavṛttistrījanābhimantāraṃ vā bandhum ||
children.translated_text: He should search among that person's attendants for someone who had suffered excessive verbal abuse, punishment, or harsh treatment; among women for one distressed or attached elsewhere; or among kinsmen for one desiring inheritance, livelihood, or the women.
He should examine the same factors in the case of one killed and then hanged.

children.text: svayam udbaddhasya vā viprakāram ayuktaṃ mārgeta ||
children.translated_text: Or, in the case of one who hanged himself, he should look for mistreatment or improper compulsion.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā strīdāyādyadoṣaḥ karmaspardhā pratipakṣadveṣaḥ paṇyasaṃsthāsamavāyo vā vivādapadānām anyatamad vā roṣasthānam ||
children.translated_text: In all cases, the source of anger may be a fault involving women, heirs, and the like, rivalry in work, hatred of an opponent, association in a trade partnership, or any one of the grounds of dispute.
The killing has anger as its motive.

children.text: svayamādiṣṭapuruṣair vā corair arthanimittaṃ sādṛśyād anyavairibhir vā hatasya ghātam āsannebhyaḥ parīkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: He should investigate from those nearby the killing of the slain man: whether it was by men whom he himself had commissioned, by thieves for gain, or by other enemies because of mistaken resemblance.

children.text: yenāhūtaḥ saha sthitaḥ prasthito hatabhūmim ānīto vā tam anuyuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: He should question the person by whom he had been summoned, with whom he had stayed or set out, or by whom he had been brought to the place where he was killed.

children.text: ye cāsya hatabhūmāvāsannacarās tān ekaikaśaḥ pṛcchet kenāyam ihānīto hato vā kaḥ saśastraḥ saṃgūhamāna udvigno vā yuṣmābhir dṛṣṭaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: And he should ask one by one those who were moving near the place of killing: "By whom was this man brought here or killed? Who, armed, hiding himself, or agitated, was seen by you?"
He should question them further according to what they say.
For a man without protectors, after observing the property and equipment found on his body,

children.text: vastraṃ veṣaṃ vibhūṣāṃ vā dṛṣṭvā tadvyavahāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the clothing, costume, or ornaments, he should question those who deal in those things;
he should ask about association, residence, and the reason for lodging,

children.text: karma ca vyavahāraṃ ca tato mārgaṇam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: and about occupation and transactions; thereafter he should carry out the search.
Whoever, by rope, weapon, poison, or the like, under the sway of desire or anger,

children.text: ghātayet svayam ātmānaṃ strī vā pāpena mohitā ||
children.translated_text: kills himself, or a woman deluded by wrongdoing kills herself,
he should have those persons dragged by a <s>caṇḍāla</s> with a rope along the royal road;
there is no cremation-ground rite for them, nor likewise any rite by relatives.
But whatever kinsman performs the prescribed funeral rites for them,

children.text: tadgatiṃ sa caret paścāt svajanād vā pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: he afterward undergoes their fate, or else is cut off from his own people.
One who associates with a fallen person falls after a year;
and another too falls by associating with them through officiating at sacrifice, teaching, or sexual intercourse.

children.text: muṣitasaṃnidhau bāhyānām abhyantarāṇāṃ ca sākṣiṇām abhiśastasya deśajātigotranāmakarmasārasahāyanivāsān anuyuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: At the scene of a theft, he should question the external and internal witnesses about the accused person's country, caste, <s>gotra</s>, name, occupation, assets, associates, and residence.
He should also test those statements by means of pretexts.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvasyāhnaḥ pracāraṃ rātrau nivāsaṃ ca grahaṇād ityanuyuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: Then he should question him about his movements during the previous day and his lodging at night before the arrest.
If his departure and return are reconciled, he is cleared; otherwise he is subject to <s>karma</s> (coercive interrogation).

children.text: trirātrād ūrdhvam agrāhyaḥ śaṅkitakaḥ pṛcchābhāvād anyatropakaraṇadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: After more than three nights, a suspect is not to be arrested when no questioning has occurred, except when the implements are seen.

children.text: acoraṃ cora ityabhivyāharataścorasamo daṇḍaś coraṃ pracchādayataśca ||
children.translated_text: For one who says of a non-thief, "He is a thief," and for one who conceals a thief, the fine is equal to that for a thief.
One accused by a thief and pointed out through enmity or hatred is cleared.
For one who keeps a cleared person in detention, the fine is the first <s>sāhasa</s> penalty.
In a case where suspicion has materialized, he should determine the implements, advisers, accomplices, appearance, and those who rendered service.
He should check the act by the place, the property, the taking, and the divisions of shares.

children.text: eteṣāṃ kāraṇānām anabhisaṃdhāne vipralapantam acoraṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: When these factors do not connect, he should know that a person speaking incoherently is not a thief.

children.text: dṛśyate hyacoro 'pi coramārge yadṛcchayā saṃnipāte coraveṣaśastrabhāṇḍasāmānyena gṛhyamāṇaścorabhāṇḍasyopavāsena vā yathāṇimāṇḍavyaḥ karmakleśabhayād acoraḥ coro 'smi iti bruvāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For even a non-thief is seen to be arrested on a thief's path by a chance encounter, because of similarity in a thief's dress, weapons, or goods, or by proximity to stolen goods, like <s>Āṇimāṇḍavya</s>, saying, "I am a thief," though not a thief, from fear of the pain of <s>karma</s>.
Therefore he should restrain a man only when the grounds are complete.

children.text: mandāparādhaṃ bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ vyādhitaṃ mattam unmattaṃ kṣutpipāsādhvaklāntam atyāśitam āmakāśitaṃ durbalaṃ vā na karma kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not subject to <s>karma</s> one whose offense is slight, a child, an old man, a sick man, a drunk, an insane person, one exhausted by hunger, thirst, or travel, one who has overeaten, one whose food is undigested, or one who is weak.
He should have him approached by secret agents of similar character, by courtesans, by keepers of public water-stations, and by those who provide conversation, opportunity, or food.

children.text: evam atisaṃdadhyād yathā vā nikṣepāpahāre vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: In this way he should entrap him, or else as explained in the case of theft of deposits.

children.text: āptadoṣaṃ karma kārayenna tveva striyaṃ garbhiṇīṃ sūtikāṃ vā māsāvaraprajātām ||
children.translated_text: He may subject to <s>karma</s> one whose guilt is established, but never a woman who is pregnant, puerperal, or who has given birth less than a month before.
For a woman, however, there is half <s>karma</s>, or verbal interrogation.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and for a learned or ascetic man, there is custody by <s>sattrin</s> agents.

children.text: tasyātikrama uttamo daṇḍaḥ kartuḥ kārayituśca karmaṇā vyāpādanena ca ||
children.translated_text: For transgressing this rule, the highest fine applies to the doer and to the one who orders it, whether by <s>karma</s> or by killing.

children.text: vyāvahārikaṃ karmacatuṣkaṃ ṣaḍ daṇḍāḥ sapta kaśāḥ dvāv uparinibandhau udakanālikā ca ||
children.translated_text: The fourfold judicial <s>karma</s> consists of six blows with rods, seven lashes, two upper bindings, and the water-tube.

children.text: paraṃ pāpakarmaṇāṃ nava vetralatāḥ dvādaśa kaśāḥ dvāv ūruveṣṭau viṃśatir naktamālalatāḥ dvātriṃśattalāḥ dvau vṛścikabandhau ullambane ca dve sūcī hastasya yavāgūpītasya ekaparvadahanam aṅgulyāḥ snehapītasya pratāpanam ekam ahaḥ śiśirarātrau balbajāgraśayyā ca ||
children.translated_text: The harsher set for grave crimes consists of nine cane-strokes, twelve lashes, two thigh-bindings, twenty strokes with <s>naktamāla</s> switches, thirty-two palm-blows, two scorpion-bindings, two suspensions, needles in the hand, burning one finger-joint after the man has drunk gruel, heating after he has drunk oil, and a bed of <s>balbaja</s> grass tips for one day and a winter night.
Thus the <s>karma</s> is eighteenfold.

children.text: tasyopakaraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ praharaṇaṃ pradhāraṇam avadhāraṇaṃ ca kharapaṭṭād āgamayet ||
children.translated_text: He should get from the <s>kharapaṭṭa</s> (rough board/manual) its equipment, measure, mode of striking, duration, and limit.
He should administer each <s>karma</s> on alternate days.

children.text: pūrvakṛtāpadānaṃ pratijñāyāpaharantam ekadeśadṛṣṭadravyaṃ karmaṇā rūpeṇa vā gṛhītaṃ rājakośam avastṛṇantaṃ karmavadhyaṃ vā rājavacanāt samastaṃ vyastam abhyastaṃ vā karma kārayet ||
children.translated_text: By the king's order, he may administer <s>karma</s>, altogether, separately, or repeatedly, to one who confesses and then denies a previously committed offense, to one whose goods have been partly seen, to one caught by the act or by appearance, to one plundering the royal treasury, or to one liable to <s>karma</s> or execution.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not to be tortured for any offense.

children.text: tasyābhiśastāṅko lalāṭe syād vyavahārapatanāya steye śvā manuṣyavadhe kabandho gurutalpe bhagaṃ surāpāne madyadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him, a mark of accusation should be on the forehead for exclusion from legal dealings: in theft, a dog; in killing a human being, a headless trunk; in <s>gurutalpa</s> (violating the teacher's bed), a vulva; and in drinking liquor, a liquor-banner.
Having publicly proclaimed a sinful <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, wounded by branding,

children.text: kuryān nirviṣayaṃ rājā vāsayed ākareṣu vā ||
children.translated_text: the king should make him an exile from the realm, or settle him in the mines.

children.text: samāhartṛpradeṣṭāraḥ pūrvam adhyakṣāṇām adhyakṣapuruṣāṇāṃ ca niyamanaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>samāhartṛ</s> and the <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s>s should first impose regulation on the superintendents and the superintendents' personnel.
From mines and workshops for valuable materials, one who steals valuable material or a jewel is liable to execution outright.

children.text: phalgudravyakarmāntebhyaḥ phalgu dravyam upaskaraṃ vā pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From workshops for common materials, one who steals common material or equipment incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: paṇyabhūmibhyo vā rājapaṇyaṃ māṣamūlyād ūrdhvam ā pādamūlyād ityapaharato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ ā dvipādamūlyād iti caturviṃśatipaṇaḥ ā tripādamūlyād iti ṣaṭtriṃśatpaṇaḥ ā paṇamūlyād ityaṣṭacatvāriṃśatpaṇaḥ ā dvipaṇamūlyād iti pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ ā catuṣpaṇamūlyād iti madhyamaḥ āṣṭapaṇamūlyād ityuttamaḥ ā daśapaṇamūlyād iti vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who steals royal merchandise from market depots, when its value is above a <s>māṣa</s> and up to a <s>pāda</s> (quarter-<s>paṇa</s>), the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s; up to two <s>pāda</s>s, twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s; up to three <s>pāda</s>s, thirty-six <s>paṇa</s>s; up to one <s>paṇa</s>, forty-eight <s>paṇa</s>s; up to two <s>paṇa</s>s, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; up to four <s>paṇa</s>s, the middle; up to eight <s>paṇa</s>s, the highest; and up to ten <s>paṇa</s>s, death.
For thefts of materials, vessels, or equipment from granaries, merchandise stores, raw-material stores, or armories, these same fines apply when the values are half as much.

children.text: kośabhāṇḍāgārākṣaśālābhyaś caturbhāgamūlyeṣu eta eva dviguṇā daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the treasury, storehouse, or gambling hall, at one-quarter the values, these same fines are doubled.
For a violent attack by thieves, there is execution by torture.
Thus the rule for royal possessions has been explained.

children.text: bāhyeṣu tu pracchannam ahani kṣetrakhalaveśmāpaṇebhyaḥ kupyabhāṇḍam upaskaraṃ vā māṣamūlyād ūrdhvam ā pādamūlyād ityapaharatastripaṇo daṇḍaḥ gomayapradehena vā pralipyāvaghoṣaṇam ā dvipādamūlyād iti ṣaṭpaṇaḥ gomayabhasmanā vā pralipyāvaghoṣaṇam ā tripādamūlyād iti navapaṇaḥ gomayabhasmanā vā pralipyāvaghoṣaṇam śarāvamekhalayā vā ā paṇamūlyād iti dvādaśapaṇaḥ muṇḍanaṃ pravrājanaṃ vā ā dvipaṇamūlyād iti caturviṃśatipaṇaḥ muṇḍasyeṣṭakāśakalena pravrājanaṃ vā ā catuṣpaṇamūlyād iti ṣaṭtriṃśatpaṇa ā pañcapaṇamūlyād ityaṣṭacatvāriṃśatpaṇaḥ ā daśapaṇamūlyād iti pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍa ā viṃśatipaṇamūlyād iti dviśata ā triṃśatpaṇamūlyād iti pañcaśata ā catvāriṃśatpaṇamūlyād iti sāhasra ā pañcāśatpaṇamūlyād iti vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In external properties, however, for one who secretly by day steals materials, vessels, or equipment from fields, threshing floors, houses, or shops, when the value is above a <s>māṣa</s> and up to a <s>pāda</s>, the fine is three <s>paṇa</s>s, or smearing with a coating of cow dung and public proclamation; up to two <s>pāda</s>s, six <s>paṇa</s>s, or smearing with cow dung and ashes and proclamation; up to three <s>pāda</s>s, nine <s>paṇa</s>s, or smearing with cow dung and ashes and proclamation, or with a potsherd girdle; up to one <s>paṇa</s>, twelve <s>paṇa</s>s; up to two <s>paṇa</s>s, twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s, or shaving or banishment; up to four <s>paṇa</s>s, thirty-six <s>paṇa</s>s, or banishment of the shaved man with a piece of brick; up to five <s>paṇa</s>s, forty-eight <s>paṇa</s>s; up to ten <s>paṇa</s>s, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; up to twenty <s>paṇa</s>s, two hundred; up to thirty <s>paṇa</s>s, five hundred; up to forty <s>paṇa</s>s, one thousand; and up to fifty <s>paṇa</s>s, death.

children.text: prasahya divā rātrau vāntaryāmikam apaharato 'rdhamūlyeṣu eta eva daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who forcibly steals property kept within by day or night, these same fines apply when the values are half as much.

children.text: prasahya divā rātrau vā saśastrasyāpaharataścaturbhāgamūlyeṣu eta eva dviguṇā daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who forcibly steals by day or night while armed, these same fines are doubled when the values are one-quarter as much.

children.text: kuṭuṃbikādhyakṣamukhyasvāmināṃ kūṭaśāsanamudrākarmasu pūrvamadhyottamavadhā daṇḍāḥ yathāparādhaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: For forged documents, seals, and transactions concerning householders, superintendents, chiefs, or owners, the penalties are the first, middle, and highest <s>sāhasa</s> fines and death, or according to the offense.

children.text: dharmasthaśced vivadamānaṃ puruṣaṃ tarjayati bhartsayatyapasārayatyabhigrasate vā pūrvam asmai sāhasadaṇḍaṃ kuryāt vākpāruṣye dviguṇam ||
children.translated_text: If a <s>dharmastha</s> (judge) threatens, rebukes, drives off, or browbeats a man engaged in litigation, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine should be imposed on him; in the case of verbal abuse, double.

children.text: pṛcchyaṃ na pṛcchati apṛcchyaṃ pṛcchati pṛṣṭvā vā visṛjati śikṣayati smārayati pūrvaṃ dadāti vā iti madhyamam asmai sāhasadaṇḍaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If he does not ask what should be asked, asks what should not be asked, or after asking dismisses the matter, instructs, reminds, or gives prior prompting, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine should be imposed on him.

children.text: deyaṃ deśaṃ na pṛcchati adeyaṃ deśaṃ pṛcchati kāryam adeśenātivāhayati chalenātiharati kālaharaṇena śrāntam apavāhayati mārgāpannaṃ vākyam utkramayati matisāhāyyaṃ sākṣibhyo dadāti tāritānuśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ punar api gṛhṇāti uttamam asmai sāhasadaṇḍaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If he does not inquire into a place that should be considered, asks about a place that should not be considered, carries a case through in an improper place, diverts it by trickery, wears a party out by delay and dismisses him, overturns a statement that has reached the right course, gives witnesses assistance in their thinking, or takes up again a case already decided and instructed, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine should be imposed on him.
On repeated offense, the penalty is double, along with removal from office.

children.text: lekhakaśced uktaṃ na likhati anuktaṃ likhati duruktam upalikhati sūktam ullikhati arthotpattiṃ vā vikalpayati iti pūrvam asmai sāhasadaṇḍaṃ kuryād yathāparādhaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: If a scribe does not write what has been said, writes what has not been said, writes down what was badly stated, erases what was well stated, or alters the arising meaning of the matter, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine should be imposed on him, or a penalty according to the offense.

children.text: dharmasthaḥ pradeṣṭā vā hairaṇyadaṇḍam adaṇḍye kṣipati kṣepadviguṇam asmai daṇḍaṃ kuryāt hīnātiriktāṣṭaguṇaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: If a <s>dharmastha</s> (judge) or <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s> (magistrate) imposes a monetary fine on one who is not liable to punishment, a fine double the imposed amount should be imposed on him; or, where he has imposed too little or too much, eight times the deficiency or excess.

children.text: śarīradaṇḍaṃ kṣipati śārīram eva daṇḍaṃ bhajeta niṣkrayadviguṇaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: If he imposes corporal punishment, he should undergo that very bodily punishment, or pay double the commutation.

children.text: yaṃ vā bhūtam arthaṃ nāśayati abhūtam arthaṃ karoti tadaṣṭaguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or if he destroys a real claim or creates an unreal claim, he should pay an eightfold fine for that.

children.text: dharmasthīye cārake bandhanāgāre vā śayyāsanabhojanoccārasaṃcārarodhabandhaneṣu tripaṇottarā daṇḍāḥ kartuḥ kārayituśca ||
children.translated_text: In a judicial lockup or prison, for abuses concerning bedding, seating, food, evacuation, movement, confinement, or fetters, fines rising by three <s>paṇa</s>s apply to the one who does the act and to the one who orders it.

children.text: cārakād abhiyuktaṃ muñcato niṣpātayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ abhiyogadānaṃ ca bandhanāgārāt sarvasvaṃ vadhaśca ||
children.translated_text: For one who releases an accused person from a lockup or causes him to escape, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies, together with payment of the charge; for doing so from a prison, confiscation of all property and death.

children.text: bandhanāgārādhyakṣasya saṃruddhakam anākhyāya cārayataścaturviṃśatipaṇo daṇḍaḥ karma kārayato dviguṇaḥ sthānānyatvaṃ gamayato 'nnapānaṃ vā rundhataḥ ṣaṇṇavatir daṇḍaḥ parikleśayata utkoṭayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ ghnataḥ sāhasraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a superintendent of the prison who lets a prisoner move about without reporting it, the fine is twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s; for making him work, double; for moving him to another place or withholding food and drink, a fine of ninety-six; for tormenting or extorting from him, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for killing him, one thousand.

children.text: parigṛhītāṃ dāsīm āhitikāṃ vā saṃruddhikām adhicarataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaś coraḍāmarikabhāryāṃ madhyamaḥ saṃruddhikām āryām uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who has intercourse with a detained female slave or pledged woman, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; with the wife of a thief or rebel, the middle; with a detained <s>āryā</s> (free woman), the highest.
For a detained man who does so, execution on the spot.

children.text: tad evākṣaṇagṛhītāyām āryāyāṃ vidyād dāsyāṃ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The same should be understood in the case of a free woman seized at an improper time; in the case of a female slave, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies.

children.text: cārakam abhittvā niṣpātayato madhyamaḥ bhittvā vadhaḥ bandhanāgārāt sarvasvaṃ vadhaśca ||
children.translated_text: For one who lets a prisoner escape from a lockup without breaking it open, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; if he breaks it open, death; from a prison, confiscation of all property and death.

children.text: evam arthacarān pūrvaṃ rājā daṇḍena śodhayet
children.translated_text: Thus the king should first purify officials concerned with wealth by punishment;
and when they have been purified, they in turn should purify the townspeople and country people by penalties.

children.text: tīrthaghātagranthibhedordhvakarāṇāṃ prathame 'parādhe saṃdeśacchedanaṃ catuṣpañcāśatpaṇo vā daṇḍaḥ dvitīye chedanaṃ paṇasya śatyo vā daṇḍas tṛtīye dakṣiṇahastavadhaścatuḥśato vā daṇḍaś caturthe yathākāmī vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For robbers at fords, cutpurses, and pickpockets, on the first offense there is cutting off of the grasping fingers, or a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s; on the second, mutilation, or a fine of one hundred <s>paṇa</s>s; on the third, cutting off the right hand, or a fine of four hundred; on the fourth, death at the ruler's discretion.

children.text: pañcaviṃśatipaṇāvareṣu kukkuṭanakulamārjāraśvasūkarasteyeṣu hiṃsāyāṃ vā catuṣpañcāśatpaṇo daṇḍo nāsāgracchedanaṃ vā caṇḍālāraṇyacarāṇām ardhadaṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In theft or injury of chickens, mongooses, cats, dogs, or pigs worth less than twenty-five <s>paṇa</s>s, the fine is fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s, or cutting off the tip of the nose; for <s>caṇḍāla</s>s and forest dwellers the fines are half.

children.text: pāśajālakūṭāvapāteṣu baddhānāṃ mṛgapaśupakṣivyālamatsyānām ādāne tacca tāvacca daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When deer, domestic animals, birds, serpents, or fish caught in snares, nets, traps, or pits are taken away, the penalty is the thing itself and a fine equal to it.
For taking animal products from preserves of animal products, the fine is one hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
For stealing or injuring deer and birds belonging to shrines and pleasure parks, the fine is double.

children.text: kāruśilpikuśīlavatapasvināṃ kṣudrakadravyāpahāre śatyo daṇḍaḥ sthūlakadravyāpahāre dviśataḥ kṛṣidravyāpahāre ca ||
children.translated_text: For taking small goods belonging to artisans, craftsmen, performers, or ascetics, the fine is one hundred <s>paṇa</s>s; for taking large goods, two hundred, and the same applies to taking agricultural goods.

children.text: durgam akṛtapraveśasya praviśataḥ prākāracchidrād vā nikṣepaṃ gṛhītvāpasarataḥ kāṇḍarāvadho dviśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For someone entering a fort without authorized entry, or going away through a breach in the wall after taking a deposit, there is death by arrows, or a fine of two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: cakrayuktaṃ nāvaṃ kṣudrapaśuṃ vāpaharata ekapādavadhaḥ triśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For stealing a wheeled boat or a small animal, there is cutting off one foot, or a fine of three hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
For one who practises fraud by counterfeit <s>kākaṇī</s> coins, alkalis, molds, rods, or sleight of hand, one hand is cut off, or the fine is four hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: stenapāradārikayoḥ sācivyakarmaṇi striyāḥ saṃgṛhītāyāśca karṇanāsāchedanaṃ pañcaśato vā daṇḍaḥ puṃso dviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a woman caught doing the work of an accomplice for thieves or adulterers, her ears and nose are cut off, or the fine is five hundred <s>paṇa</s>s; for a man it is double.

children.text: mahāpaśum ekaṃ dāsaṃ dāsīṃ vāpaharataḥ pretabhāṇḍaṃ vā vikrīṇānasya dvipādavadhaḥ ṣaṭchato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who steals a single large animal, a male slave, or a female slave, or sells property belonging to the dead, both feet are cut off, or the fine is six hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: varṇottamānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca hastapādalaṅghane rājayānavāhanādyārohaṇe caikahastapādavadhaḥ saptaśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For laying hands or feet upon persons superior in <s>varṇa</s> or upon gurus, and for mounting the king's vehicles, mounts, and the like, one hand and one foot are cut off, or the fine is seven hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: śūdrasya brāhmaṇavādino devadravyam avastṛṇato rājadviṣṭam ādiśato dvinetrabhedinaśca yogāñjanenāndhatvam aṣṭaśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>śūdra</s> claiming to be a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, for one misappropriating property of the gods, for one pointing out a person hated by the king, and for one who destroys both eyes, the punishment is blinding by magical collyrium, or a fine of eight hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: coraṃ pāradārikaṃ vā mokṣayato rājaśāsanam ūnam atiriktaṃ vā likhataḥ kanyāṃ dāsīṃ vā sahiraṇyam apaharataḥ kūṭavyavahāriṇo vimāṃsavikrayiṇaśca vāmahastadvipādavadho navaśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who releases a thief or adulterer, writes a royal command with omissions or additions, abducts a maiden or female slave together with gold, engages in fraudulent legal dealings, or sells forbidden meat, the left hand and both feet are cut off, or the fine is nine hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
For selling human flesh, death.
For one who steals a sacred animal, an image, a person, a field, a house, money, gold, jewels, or grain, the penalty is the highest <s>daṇḍa</s> (fine), or unqualified execution.
The person, the offense, the cause, and the gravity or lightness,

children.text: anubandhaṃ tadātvaṃ ca deśakālau samīkṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: the consequence, the immediate circumstances, and also the place and time, having examined all these,
the <s>pradeṣṭṛ</s> should determine the higher, lower, or middle grade in the work of punishment,

children.text: rājñaśca prakṛtīnāṃ ca kalpayed antarā sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: standing between the king and the subjects.
For one who kills a man in a quarrel, there is a torturous execution.

children.text: saptarātrasyāntarmṛte śuddhavadhaḥ pakṣasyāntar uttamo māsasyāntaḥ pañcaśataḥ samutthānavyayaśca ||
children.translated_text: If the victim dies within seven nights, there is unqualified execution; within a fortnight, the highest fine; within a month, a fine of five hundred <s>paṇa</s>s and the expenses of recovery.
For striking with a weapon, the highest fine.
If it is done through intoxication, cutting off the hand; through delusion, a fine of two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
For killing, death.

children.text: prahāreṇa garbhaṃ pātayata uttamo daṇḍo bhaiṣajyena madhyamaḥ parikleśena pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For causing a fetus to fall by a blow, the highest fine; by medicine, the middle fine; by torment, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: prasabhastrīpuruṣaghātakābhisārakanigrāhakāvaghoṣakāvaskandakopavedhakān pathiveśmapratirodhakān rājahastyaśvarathānāṃ hiṃsakān stenān vā śūlān ārohayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should impale those who violently kill women or men, night-attackers, abductors, public alarm-raisers, raiders, instigators, blockers of roads or houses, injurers of the king's elephants, horses, or chariots, and thieves.

children.text: yaścainān dahed apanayed vā sa tam eva daṇḍaṃ labheta sāhasam uttamaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever burns or removes these should receive that very same penalty, or the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
For giving violent thieves food, lodging, equipment, fire, counsel, or service, the penalty is the highest fine; if they are not known as such, there is only a reprimand for conversing with them.

children.text: hiṃsrastenānāṃ putradāram asamantraṃ visṛjet samantram ādadīta ||
children.translated_text: The sons and wives of violent thieves he should release if they have not shared in the counsel; if they have shared in it, he should seize them.

children.text: rājyakāmukam antaḥpurapradharṣakam aṭavyamitrotsāhakaṃ durgarāṣṭradaṇḍakopakaṃ vā śirohastapradīpikaṃ ghātayet ||
children.translated_text: One who desires the kingdom, violates the harem, incites forest tribes or allies, or provokes revolt in a fort, countryside, or army, he should execute by setting fire to the head and hands.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> he should confine in darkness.
One who kills his mother, father, son, brother, teacher, or an ascetic he should execute by setting fire to the skin and head.
For abusing them, the tongue is cut off; for biting a limb, the corresponding limb is to be removed.
For killing a man at random and for stealing a herd of livestock, there is unqualified execution.
A herd should be known as numbering ten or more.

children.text: udakadhāraṇaṃ setuṃ bhindatastatraivāpsu nimajjanam anudakam uttamaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ bhagnotsṛṣṭakaṃ madhyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who breaks a water-retaining embankment or bridge should be drowned right there in the water; if there is no water, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; if it was already broken and abandoned, the middle fine applies.

children.text: viṣadāyakaṃ puruṣaṃ striyaṃ ca puruṣaghnīm apaḥ praveśayed agarbhiṇīm garbhiṇīṃ māsāvaraprajātām ||
children.translated_text: A man who gives poison, and a woman who kills a man, should be made to enter the water; a woman if she is not pregnant, and if she is pregnant, after she has given birth and a month has passed.

children.text: patiguruprajāghātikām agniviṣadāṃ saṃdhichedikāṃ vā gobhiḥ pāṭayet ||
children.translated_text: A woman who kills her husband, guru, or offspring, gives fire or poison, or cuts a vital joint should be torn apart by cows.
One who sets fire to a pasture, field, threshing floor, house, goods, elephant forest, and the like should be burned with fire.
For one who reviles the king, betrays counsel, promotes what is harmful, or licks in the kitchen of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, he should tear out the tongue.
A thief of weapons or armor who is not a soldier should be killed with arrows.
If he is a soldier, the highest fine applies.
For one who injures the penis or testicles, he should have those very parts cut off.
For injury to the tongue or nose, the penalty is mutilation with tongs.
These painful punishments, applied in the treatises, are for persons of grave offense;

children.text: akliṣṭānāṃ tu pāpānāṃ dharmyaḥ śuddhavadhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but for sinners who are not to be tortured, righteous simple execution is prescribed.

children.text: savarṇām aprāptaphalāṃ prakurvato hastavadhaḥ catuḥśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a man who violates a girl of the same <s>varṇa</s> before she has reached maturity, there is cutting off of the hand, or a fine of four hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
If she dies, the penalty is death.

children.text: prāptaphalāṃ prakurvato madhyamāpradeśinīvadho dviśato vā daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a man who violates one who has reached maturity, there is cutting off of the middle and index fingers, or a fine of two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
And he shall give compensation for the loss to her father.
And he shall not obtain the right of enjoyment over an unwilling woman.
If she is willing, the fine is fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s; for the woman, however, the fine is half.

children.text: paraśulkāvaruddhāyāṃ hastavadhaḥ catuḥśato vā daṇḍaḥ śulkadānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the case of one reserved by another's bride-price, there is cutting off of the hand, or a fine of four hundred <s>paṇa</s>s, and payment of the bride-price.

children.text: saptārtavaprajātāṃ varaṇād ūrdhvam alabhamānaḥ prakṛtya prākāmī syānna ca pitur avahīnaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If, after betrothal, a man does not receive a girl who has had seven menstrual periods, then after approaching her he may have the right of enjoyment, and he need not give compensation for loss to her father.
By those who obstruct the proper seasons, she passes out of the husband's claim.

children.text: trivarṣaprajātārtavāyāstulyo gantum adoṣas tataḥ param atulyo 'pyanalaṃkṛtāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a girl whose menstrual periods have appeared for three years, a man of equal status incurs no fault by going to her; after that, even one not equal may do so, if she has not been adorned in marriage.
If he takes the father's property, he shall incur the offense of theft.
For one who assigns her to one man and has another marry her, the fine is two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s.
And he shall not obtain the right of enjoyment over an unwilling woman.

children.text: kanyām anyāṃ darśayitvānyāṃ prayacchataḥ śatyo daṇḍastulyāyām hīnāyāṃ dviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who shows one maiden and gives another, the fine is one hundred <s>paṇa</s>s if she is equal; if she is inferior, it is double.

children.text: prakarmaṇy akumāryāś catuṣpañcāśatpaṇo daṇḍaḥ śulkavyayakarmaṇī ca pratidadyāt ||
children.translated_text: In the marriage transaction, if she is not a maiden, the fine is fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s, and he shall return the bride-price, expenses, and ritual costs.
If, after establishing that condition, the matter is acted on later, he shall pay double.
For substituting another's blood, the fine is two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s, and the same applies to a man who makes a false accusation.
And he shall lose the bride-price, expenses, and ritual costs.
And he shall not obtain the right of enjoyment over an unwilling woman.

children.text: strīprakṛtā sakāmā samānā dvādaśapaṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt prakartrī dviguṇam ||
children.translated_text: A woman who has been solicited, if willing and of equal status, shall pay a fine of twelve <s>paṇa</s>s; the woman who initiates the act shall pay double.

children.text: akāmāyāḥ śatyo daṇḍa ātmarāgārtham śulkadānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In the case of an unwilling woman, the fine is one hundred <s>paṇa</s>s, and the bride-price must be paid for the sake of his own passion.
A woman who initiates the act herself shall enter royal slavery.

children.text: bahirgrāmasya prakṛtāyāṃ mithyābhiśaṃsane ca dviguṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the case of a woman approached outside the village, and in the case of false accusation, the fine is double.

children.text: prasahya kanyām apaharato dviśataḥ sasuvarṇām uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who forcibly abducts a maiden, the fine is two hundred <s>paṇa</s>s; if she has gold ornaments, the highest fine applies.
For many abductors of a maiden, the stated penalties apply to each separately.

children.text: gaṇikāduhitaraṃ prakurvataścatuṣpañcāśatpaṇo daṇḍaḥ śulkaṃ mātur bhogaḥ ṣoḍaśaguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a man who violates the daughter of a courtesan, the fine is fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s; the fee belongs to the mother, and compensation for enjoyment is sixteenfold.

children.text: dāsasya dāsyā vā duhitaram adāsīṃ prakurvataścaturviṃśatipaṇo daṇḍaḥ śulkāvandhyadānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For a man who violates the free daughter of a male or female slave, the fine is twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s, together with payment of the bride-price and compensation for impairment.

children.text: niṣkrayānurūpāṃ dāsīṃ prakurvato dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍo vastrāvandhyadānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For a man who violates a slave woman proportionate to her redemption-price, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s, together with payment of garments and compensation for impairment.
For assistance or for giving opportunity, the penalty is equal to that of the perpetrator.
A husband's kinsman or his agent may apprehend a woman whose husband is abroad and who is behaving unchastely.
When apprehended, she shall wait for her husband.
If the husband forgives, both are to be released.

children.text: akṣamāyāṃ striyāḥ karṇanāsāchedanaṃ vadhaṃ jāraśca prāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he does not forgive, the woman incurs cutting off of the ears and nose, and the adulterer incurs death.

children.text: jāraṃ cora ityabhiharataḥ pañcaśato daṇḍo hiraṇyena muñcatastadaṣṭaguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who carries off the adulterer as a thief, the fine is five hundred <s>paṇa</s>s; for one who releases him in return for gold, it is eight times that.

children.text: keśākeśikaṃ saṃgrahaṇam upaliṅganād vā śarīropabhogānām tajjātebhyaḥ strīvacanād vā ||
children.translated_text: Apprehension is valid from their being hair-to-hair, from signs of embracing or bodily enjoyment, from traces produced by those acts, or from the woman's statement.

children.text: paracakrāṭavīhṛtām oghapravyūḍhām araṇyeṣu durbhikṣe vā tyaktāṃ pretabhāvotsṛṣṭāṃ vā parastriyaṃ nistārayitvā yathāsaṃbhāṣitaṃ samupabhuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: After rescuing another man's wife who has been carried off by an enemy army or forest people, swept away by a flood, abandoned in forests or in famine, or cast off as dead, a man may enjoy her according to the agreement made.
But if she is of superior caste, unwilling, or has children, he shall hand her over in return for a ransom.
After rescuing a woman from the hands of thieves, from the force of a river, from famine, or from disorder in the country,

children.text: nistārayitvā kāntārān naṣṭāṃ tyaktāṃ mṛteti vā ||
children.translated_text: from wildernesses, or one lost, abandoned, or left as dead,
a man may enjoy another man's woman according to the agreement made,

children.text: na tu rājapratāpena pramuktāṃ svajanena vā ||
children.translated_text: but not one released through the king's power or by her own relatives.

children.text: na cottamāṃ na cākāmāṃ pūrvāpatyavatīṃ na ca
children.translated_text: Nor may he enjoy one who is of higher status, unwilling, or already has children;
such a woman he should send away for an appropriate ransom.

children.text: brāhmaṇam apeyam abhakṣyaṃ vā grāsayata uttamo daṇḍaḥ kṣatriyaṃ madhyamaḥ vaiśyaṃ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ śūdraṃ catuṣpañcāśatpaṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For making a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> swallow something not to be drunk or not to be eaten, the highest fine applies; for a <s>kṣatriya</s>, the middle fine; for a <s>vaiśya</s>, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; and for a <s>śūdra</s>, a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇa</s>s.
Those who swallow such things voluntarily are to be made outcasts from the realm.

children.text: paragṛhābhigamane divā pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍo rātrau madhyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For entering another's house, by day the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies, and by night the middle fine.

children.text: divā rātrau vā saśastrasya praviśata uttamo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who enters armed, whether by day or by night, the highest fine applies.

children.text: bhikṣukavaidehakau mattonmattau balād āpadi cātisaṃnikṛṣṭāḥ pravṛttapraveśāścādaṇḍyāḥ anyatra pratiṣedhāt ||
children.translated_text: Mendicants, merchants, drunk men, madmen, those driven by force or emergency, close associates, and those for whom entry is customary are not punishable, except where there is a prohibition.

children.text: svaveśmano virātrād ūrdhvaṃ parivāram ārohataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ paraveśmano madhyamaḥ grāmārāmavāṭabhedinaśca ||
children.translated_text: For climbing over the enclosure of one's own house after nightfall, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; for that of another's house, the middle fine, as also for breaking into a village, park, or enclosure.
In villages, caravan merchants should lodge inside, with the value of their goods made known.

children.text: muṣitaṃ pravāsitaṃ caiṣām anirgataṃ rātrau grāmasvāmī dadyāt ||
