children.translated_text: Whatever of theirs is stolen or lost at night before they have departed, the village headman shall pay.

children.text: grāmāntareṣu vā muṣitaṃ pravāsitaṃ vivītādhyakṣo dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, if it is stolen or lost between villages, the superintendent of pasture lands shall pay.
For places not under the pasture superintendent, the officer over thieves shall pay.
Even then, in the case of unguarded goods, they shall pay the assessed loss after blocking the boundary.
If the boundary is not blocked, a group of five villages, or else a group of ten villages, is liable.

children.text: durbalaṃ veśma śakaṭam anuttabdhamūrdhastaṃbhaṃ śastram anapāśrayam apraticchannaṃ śvabhraṃ kūpaṃ kūṭāvapātaṃ vā kṛtvā hiṃsāyāṃ daṇḍapāruṣyaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: If someone causes injury by making a weak house, a cart with its upper support unpropped, an unsupported weapon, or an uncovered pit, well, or concealed trap, it should be regarded as <s>daṇḍapāruṣya</s> (violent assault).

children.text: vṛkṣacchedane damyaraśmiharaṇe catuṣpadānām adāntasevane vāhane vā kāṣṭhaloṣṭapāṣāṇadaṇḍabāṇabāhuvikṣepaṇeṣu yāne hastinā ca saṃghaṭṭane apehi iti prakrośann adaṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When cutting a tree, removing the reins of a draft animal, using or riding untamed quadrupeds, throwing wood, clods, stones, sticks, arrows, or one's arm, or colliding with a vehicle or elephant, a man is not punishable if he shouts, "Get away!"

children.text: hastinā roṣitena hato droṇānnaṃ madyakuṃbhaṃ mālyānulepanaṃ dantapramārjanaṃ ca paṭaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man is killed by an enraged elephant, one should give a <s>droṇa</s> of food, a jar of liquor, garlands and unguents, and a cloth for wiping its tusks.

children.text: aśvamedhāvabhṛthasnānena tulyo hastinā vadha iti pādaprakṣālanam ||
children.translated_text: Death by an elephant is equal to the final bath of an <s>aśvamedha</s>; therefore there is washing of the feet.
For a driver who kills a bystander, the highest fine applies.

children.text: śṛṅgiṇā daṃṣṭriṇā vā hiṃsyamānam amokṣayataḥ svāminaḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ pratikruṣṭasya dviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For an owner who does not rescue someone being injured by a horned or tusked animal, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies; if he has been called upon, it is doubled.
For one who makes horned or tusked animals kill one another, the fine is that animal and as much again.

children.text: devapaśum ṛṣabham ukṣāṇaṃ gokumārīṃ vā vāhayataḥ pañcaśato daṇḍaḥ pravāsayata uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who uses as a draft animal a sacred animal, a stud bull, a breeding ox, or a young cow, the fine is five hundred; for driving it away, the highest fine applies.

children.text: lomadohavāhanaprajananopakāriṇāṃ kṣudrapaśūnām ādāne tacca tāvacca daṇḍaḥ pravāsane ca anyatra devapitṛkāryebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For taking small animals useful for wool, milk, transport, or breeding, the fine is the animal and an equal amount, and likewise for driving them away, except for rites to gods or ancestors.

children.text: chinnanasyaṃ bhagnayugaṃ tiryakpratimukhāgataṃ pratyāsarad vā cakrayuktaṃ yātā paśumanuṣyasaṃbādhe vā hiṃsāyām adaṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a vehicle has a cut nose-rope, a broken yoke, is coming crosswise or head-on, or is backing with its wheels, the driver is not punishable for injury amid a crowding of animals and people.
Otherwise he incurs the penalty prescribed for injury to a human life.
For killing a non-human living creature, he must also give another living creature.

children.text: bāle yātari yānasthaḥ svāmī daṇḍyo 'svāmini yānasthaḥ prāptavyavahāro vā yātā ||
children.translated_text: If the driver is a child, the owner seated in the vehicle is liable to the fine; if the owner is not in the vehicle, then the driver, if legally competent, is liable.

children.text: bālādhiṣṭhitam apuruṣaṃ vā yānaṃ rājā haret ||
children.translated_text: The king should seize a vehicle controlled by a child or one without a man in charge.
Whatever harm a person brings upon another by harmful rites or sorcery, that same harm should be brought upon him.

children.text: kāmaṃ bhāryāyām anicchantyāṃ kanyāyāṃ vā dārārthino bhartari bhāryāyā vā saṃvadanakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: A suitor seeking marriage may perform a charm for winning over an unwilling wife or a maiden, and a wife may do so toward her husband.
For harm done otherwise, the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies.

children.text: mātāpitror bhaginīṃ mātulānīm ācāryāṇīṃ snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ bhaginīṃ vādhicaratastriliṅgacchedanaṃ vadhaśca ||
children.translated_text: For one who has intercourse with his mother's or father's sister, his maternal uncle's wife, his teacher's wife, his daughter-in-law, his daughter, or his sister, there is cutting off of the three sexual organs and death.

children.text: sakāmā tad eva labheta dāsaparicārakāhitakabhuktā ca ||
children.translated_text: A consenting woman receives that same punishment, as does a woman enjoyed by a slave, an attendant, or a dependent servant.

children.text: brāhmaṇyām aguptāyāṃ kṣatriyasyottamaḥ sarvasvaṃ vaiśyasya śūdraḥ kaṭāgninā dahyeta ||
children.translated_text: In the case of an unguarded <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman, a <s>kṣatriya</s> receives the highest fine, a <s>vaiśya</s> loses all his property, and a <s>śūdra</s> is to be burned in a straw fire.
In every case, for intercourse with the king's wife, the punishment is boiling in a jar.

children.text: śvapākīgamane kṛtakabandhāṅkaḥ paraviṣayaṃ gacchet śvapākatvaṃ vā śūdraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For intercourse with a <s>śvapākī</s> woman, a <s>śūdra</s>, branded with the mark of a headless trunk, should go to another territory, or else become a <s>śvapāka</s>.
For a <s>śvapāka</s> having intercourse with an <s>āryā</s> woman, death applies; for the woman, cutting off of the ears and nose.
For intercourse with a female renunciant, the fine is twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s.
If she is willing, she receives the same.
For forcibly enjoying a courtesan, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: bahūnām ekām adhicaratāṃ pṛthak caturviṃśatipaṇo daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When many men violate one woman, each separately incurs a fine of twenty-four <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: striyam ayonau gacchataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasadaṇḍaḥ puruṣam adhimehataśca ||
children.translated_text: For one who goes to a woman in a non-vaginal passage, and for one who has intercourse with a man, the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine applies.
For intercourse with animals, the fine is twelve <s>paṇa</s>s;
and for sexually approaching images of deities, it is prescribed as double.
When the king punishes one who should not be punished, a fine thirty times as great is to be placed in the water
and given to <s>Varuṇa</s>; thereafter it is to be given to <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s.

children.text: tena tat pūyate pāpaṃ rājño daṇḍāpacārajam
children.translated_text: By that, the sin arising from the king's misuse of punishment is purified;

children.text: śāstā hi varuṇo rājñāṃ mithyā vyācaratāṃ nṛṣu ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Varuṇa</s> is the chastiser of kings who act falsely among men.

children.text: vāstukapraśaste vāstuni nāyakavardhakimauhūrtikāḥ skandhāvāram vṛttaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vā bhūmivaśena vā caturdvāraṃ ṣaṭpathaṃ navasaṃsthānaṃ māpayeyuḥ khātavaprasāladvārāṭṭālakasampannaṃ bhaye sthāne ca ||
children.translated_text: On ground approved by the architect, the commander, carpenter, and astrologer should lay out a <s>skandhāvāra</s> (military camp), circular, oblong, square, or according to the terrain, with four gates, six roads, and nine divisions, furnished with ditch, rampart, palisade, gates, and watchtowers, according to danger and location.

children.text: madhyamasyottare navabhāge rājavāstukaṃ dhanuḥśatāyāmam ardhavistāram paścimārdhe tasyāntaḥpuram ||
children.translated_text: In the northern ninth part of the central area should be the king's residence, one hundred bows long and half as wide; in its western half should be the inner apartments.
The inner-guard force should be stationed at its end.

children.text: purastād upasthānam dakṣiṇataḥ kośaśāsanakāryakaraṇāni vāmato rājopavāhyānāṃ hastyaśvarathānāṃ sthānam ||
children.translated_text: In front should be the audience hall; to the south, the treasury and administrative offices; on the left, the place for the elephants, horses, and chariots used by the king.
At intervals of one hundred bows from this should be four enclosing barriers made of carts, stakes, extended posts, and palisades.

children.text: prathame purastān mantripurohitau dakṣiṇataḥ koṣṭhāgāraṃ mahānasaṃ ca vāmataḥ kupyāyudhāgāram ||
children.translated_text: In the first enclosure, in front, should be the minister and the priest; to the south, the storehouse and kitchen; on the left, the store of raw materials and the armory.
In the second should be the place of the standing and hired troops, of the horses and chariots, and of the commander-in-chief.
In the third should be the elephants, the guild troops, and the administrator.
In the fourth should be the forced-labor corps, the captain, and the forces of allies, enemies, and forest tribes, placed under the supervision of one's own men.
Merchants and courtesans should be stationed along the main road.
Outside should be hunters and handlers of dog-packs, with drums and fires, and secret guards.
When enemies attack, he should set up pits, concealed traps, and thorn obstacles.
He should have the guard arrangements of the eighteen groups rotated.
He should also institute a daytime patrol for detecting those who slip away.
He should have disputes, liquor sellers, assemblies, and gambling prohibited, and should have passes and seals guarded.
The guard of empty spaces should arrest an armed man who has left the army and has no authorization.
After the road in front has been properly regulated, and after the protections have been arranged,
he should march; and by means of carpenters and corvee laborers he should have water-supplies prepared.

children.text: grāmāraṇyānām adhvani niveśān yavasendhanodakavaśena parisaṃkhyāya sthānāsanagamanakālaṃ ca yātrāṃ yāyāt ||
children.translated_text: On the road, after calculating the encampments in villages and forests according to fodder, fuel, and water, and also the proper times for halting, remaining, and moving, he should undertake the march.
He should have rations and equipment carried in twice the quantity needed to meet those requirements.

children.text: aśakto vā sainyeṣvāyojayet antareṣu vā nicinuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, if he is unable to do so, he should assign them among the troops, or store them at intervals.

children.text: purastān nāyakaḥ madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca pārśvayor aśvā bāhuutsāraḥ cakrānteṣu hastinaḥ prasāravṛddhir vā paścāt senāpatir yāyānniviśeta ||
children.translated_text: The guide should be in front; the household and the king in the middle; the horses and the <s>bāhūtsāra</s> detachments on the flanks; the elephants at the ends of the columns, or else in an expanded deployment; and the commander-in-chief behind: in this order he should march and encamp.
On every side the extended screen should consist of forest-men.
The supply train should follow on from his own country.
The allied force is the reinforcing force.
The place of the household is the place of retreat.

children.text: purastād adhyāghāte makareṇa yāyāt paścācchakaṭena pārśvayor vajreṇa samantataḥ sarvatobhadreṇa ekāyane sūcyā ||
children.translated_text: When there is an attack from the front, he should march in the <s>makara</s> formation; from the rear, in the <s>śakaṭa</s> formation; from the flanks, in the <s>vajra</s> formation; from all sides, in the <s>sarvatobhadra</s> formation; and on a single narrow road, in the <s>sūcī</s> formation.
When the road divides in two, he should march by ground favorable to himself.

children.text: abhūmiṣṭhānāṃ hi svabhūmiṣṭhā yuddhe pratilomā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For those established on their own ground become adverse in battle to those who are not established on suitable ground.

children.text: yojanam adhamā adhyardhaṃ madhyamā dviyojanam uttamā sambhāvyā vā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: A march of one <s>yojana</s> is inferior, one and a half is middling, two <s>yojanas</s> is superior, or the rate should be whatever is possible.

children.text: āśrayakārī sampannaghātī pārṣṇir āsāro madhyama udāsīno vā pratikartavyaḥ saṃkaṭo mārgaḥ śodhayitavyaḥ kośo daṇḍo mitrāmitrāṭavībalaṃ viṣṭiṛtur vā pratīkṣyāḥ kṛtadurgakarmanicayarakṣākṣayaḥ krītabalanirvedo mitrabalanirvedaścāgamiṣyati upajapitāro vā nātitvarayanti śatrur abhiprāyaṃ vā pūrayiṣyati iti śanair yāyāt viparyaye śīghram ||
children.translated_text: He should march slowly when he must counteract a giver of shelter, one who strikes at what has been gained, a rear enemy, a reinforcing force, a middle king, or a neutral king; when a difficult road has to be cleared; when the treasury, army, allied, hostile, or forest forces, corvee labor, or the season have to be awaited; when exhaustion of completed fort-work, stores, and defenses, or disenchantment among hired and allied troops, is expected; when those who have been secretly won over do not press for excessive haste; or when the enemy will fulfill the intended plan. In the contrary circumstances he should march quickly.

He should make the army cross waters by means of elephants, posts, passages, bridge-construction, boats, masses of wood and bamboo, and also floats made from gourds, skins, baskets, skin-bags, rafts, bundles, and plaited reeds.

children.text: tīrthābhigrahe hastyaśvair anyato rātrāv uttārya sattraṃ gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: When a ford is occupied, he should get elephants and horses across elsewhere at night and seize a hidden position.
In a waterless region he should have water carried, according to the length of the road and as far as possible, for wheeled vehicles and four-footed animals.

children.text: dīrghakāntāram anudakaṃ yavasendhanodakahīnaṃ vā kṛcchrādhvānam abhiyogapraskannaṃ kṣutpipāsādhvaklāntaṃ paṅkatoyagambhīrāṇāṃ vā nadīdarīśailānām udyānāpayāne vyāsaktam ekāyanamārge śailaviṣame saṃkaṭe vā bahulībhūtaṃ niveśe prasthite visamnāhaṃ bhojanavyāsaktam āyatagatapariśrāntam avasuptaṃ vyādhimarakadurbhikṣapīḍitaṃ vyādhitapattyaśvadvipam abhūmiṣṭhaṃ vā balavyasaneṣu vā svasainyaṃ rakṣet parasainyaṃ cābhihanyāt ||
children.translated_text: In calamities affecting an army, he should protect his own army and strike the enemy's army when it is in a long wilderness, without water, or lacking fodder, fuel, and water; on a difficult road; shattered by attack; exhausted by hunger, thirst, and travel; entangled in the ascent or descent of rivers, ravines, or mountains deep with mud and water; crowded on a single-track road, uneven mountain ground, or a defile; when it has set out from camp with its equipment disordered; when it is occupied with eating; wearied by a long march; asleep; afflicted by disease, plague, or famine; with its infantry, horses, and elephants sick; stationed on unsuitable ground; or in other military distress.

For an enemy army that has gone along a single-track road, knowledge of its strength is obtained by counting the army's leavings, mouthfuls of fodder, food, spread bedding, fire-places, banners, and weapons.
He should conceal those same indications of his own army.
Having placed behind him, on his own ground, a mountain stronghold or a forest stronghold equipped with retreat and refuge,

children.text: svabhumau pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yudhyeta niviśeta ca ||
children.translated_text: he should fight and also encamp.
For the protection of the four <s>varṇas</s>, he should employ <s>aupaniṣadika</s> secret measures against the most unrighteous.

children.text: kālakūṭādir viṣavargaḥ śraddheyadeśaveṣaśilpabhāṣābhijanāpadeśaiḥ kubjavāmanakirātamūkabadhirajaḍāndhacchadmabhir mlecchajātīyair abhipretaiḥ strībhiḥ puṃbhiśca paraśarīropabhogeṣvavadhātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The class of poisons beginning with <s>kālakūṭa</s> should be deposited in things used on the enemy's body by chosen women and men of <s>mleccha</s> origin, under pretexts of trustworthy country, dress, craft, language, family, and local provenance, and under disguises as hunchbacks, dwarfs, <s>Kirātas</s>, the mute, the deaf, the dull, and the blind.

children.text: rājakrīḍābhāṇḍanidhānadravyopabhogeṣu gūḍhāḥ śastranidhānaṃ kuryuḥ sattrājīvinaśca rātricāriṇo 'gnijīvinaścāgninidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Secret agents should make deposits of weapons among the objects used for the king's sports, utensils, stores, and valuables; and those living by <s>sattra</s> practices, night-wanderers, and those living by fire should make deposits of fire.

children.text: citrabhekakauṇḍinyakakṛkaṇapañcakuṣṭhaśatapadīcūrṇam uccidiṅgakaṃ valīśatakandedhmakṛkalāsacūrṇaṃ gṛhagolikāndhāhikakrakaṇṭhakapūtikīṭagomārikācūrṇaṃ bhallātakāvalgujarasaṃyuktaṃ sadyaḥprāṇaharam eteṣāṃ vā dhūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A powder of citrabheka, kauṇḍinyaka, kṛkaṇa, pañcakuṣṭha, and śatapadī, uccidiṅgaka, a powder of valīśataka, kanda, fuel, and kṛkalāsa, and a powder of house-lizard, andhāhika, krakaṇṭhaka, putrid insects, and gomārikā, mixed with the juices of bhallātaka and avalguja, is instantly life-destroying; or the smoke from these is so.
Or any one insect, heated with black snake and priyaṅgu,
should be dried; this combination is considered instantly life-destroying.
The root of dhāmārgava and yātudhāna, mixed with powdered bhallātaka flowers, is a poison that takes effect within half a month.
The root of vyāghātaka, mixed with powdered bhallātaka flowers and an insect compound, is a poison that takes effect within a month.

children.text: kalāmātraṃ puruṣāṇām dviguṇaṃ kharāśvānām caturguṇaṃ hastyuṣṭrāṇām ||
children.translated_text: The dose is a <s>kalā</s>-measure for men, double that for donkeys and horses, and four times that for elephants and camels.

children.text: śatakardamoccidiṅgakaravīrakaṭutumbīmatsyadhūmo madanakodravapalālena hastikarṇapalāśapalālena vā pravātānuvāte praṇīto yāvaccarati tāvan mārayati ||
children.translated_text: Smoke from śatakardama, uccidiṅga, karavīra, bitter gourd, and fish, conveyed downwind with madana and kodrava straw, or with hastikarṇa and palāśa straw, kills for as far as it travels.

Powder of putrid insects, fish, bitter gourd, śatakardama, fuel, and indragopa, or powder of putrid insects, kṣudrārālā, and hemavidārī, mixed with powder of goat horn and hoof, makes a blinding smoke.
Leaves of putikarañja, orpiment, realgar, guñjā, red cotton straw, āsphoṭa, and kāca, ground in cow-dung juice, make a blinding smoke.
A snake's slough, cow and horse dung, and the head of an andhāhika make a blinding smoke.

children.text: pārāvataplavakakravyādānāṃ hastinaravarāhāṇāṃ ca mūtrapurīṣaṃ kāsīsahiṅguyavatuṣakaṇataṇḍulāḥ kārpāsakuṭajakośātakīnāṃ ca bījāni gomūtrikābhāṇḍīmūlaṃ nimbaśigruphaṇirjakākṣīvapīlukabhaṅgaḥ sarpaśapharīcarma hastinakhaśṛṅgacūrṇam ityeṣa dhūmo madanakodravapalālena hastikarṇapalāśapalālena vā praṇītaḥ pratyekaśo yāvaccarati tāvan mārayati ||
children.translated_text: The urine and feces of pigeons, aquatic birds, carnivores, elephants, men, and boars; <s>kāsīsa</s>, asafoetida, barley husk, broken rice; seeds of cotton, <s>kuṭaja</s>, and <s>kośātakī</s>; <s>gomūtrikā</s>, <s>bhāṇḍīmūla</s>, neem, <s>śigru</s>, <s>phaṇirjaka</s>, <s>akṣīva</s>, <s>pīluka</s>, and hemp; snake skin and <s>śapharī</s> fish skin; and powder of elephant nails and horns: this smoke, prepared with straw of <s>madana</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, or with straw of <s>hastikarṇa-palāśa</s>, kills each creature for as long as it travels.

children.text: kālīkuṣṭhanaḍaśatāvarīmūlaṃ sarpapracalākakṛkaṇapañcakuṣṭhacūrṇaṃ vā dhūmaḥ pūrvakalpenārdraśuṣkapalālena vā praṇītaḥ saṃgrāmāvataraṇāvaskandanasaṃkuleṣu kṛtanejanodakākṣipratīkāraiḥ praṇītaḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ netraghnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A smoke made, as before, from the roots of <s>kālī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>naḍa</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>, or from a powder of snake, <s>pracalāka</s>, <s>kṛkaṇa</s>, and <s>pañcakuṣṭha</s>, prepared with wet or dry straw and used in the confusion of battle-entry and assault, together with protective measures such as washing and water for the eyes, destroys the eyes of all living beings.

children.text: śārikākapotabakabalākāleṇḍam arkākṣipīlukasnuhikṣīrapiṣṭam andhīkaraṇam añjanam udakadūṣaṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The droppings of mynahs, pigeons, cranes, and herons, ground with the milky sap of <s>arka</s>, <s>akṣipīluka</s>, and <s>snuhī</s>, make a blinding eye-salve and a means of polluting water.

A preparation of barley, rice-root, <s>madana</s> fruit, jasmine leaves, and human urine, combined with the roots of <s>plakṣa</s> and <s>vidārī</s>, or with a decoction of <s>mūka</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>madana</s>, and <s>kodrava</s>, or with a decoction of <s>hastikarṇa-palāśa</s>, is a <s>madana-yoga</s> (madana preparation).

children.text: śṛṅgigautamavṛkakaṇṭakāramayūrapadīyogo guñjālāṅgalīviṣamūlikeṅgudīyogaḥ karavīrākṣipīlukārkamṛgamāraṇīyogo madanakodravakvāthayukto hastikarṇapalāśakvāthayukto vā madanayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A preparation of <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>gautama</s>, <s>vṛkakaṇṭaka</s>, and <s>mayūrapadī</s>; or of <s>guñjā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>viṣamūlikā</s>, and <s>iṅgudī</s>; or of oleander, <s>akṣipīluka</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>mṛgamāraṇī</s>, combined with a decoction of <s>madana</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, or with a decoction of <s>hastikarṇa-palāśa</s>, is also a <s>madana-yoga</s>.
Or, taken all together, these are pollutants for fodder, fuel, and water.
A smoke made from <s>kṛtakaṇḍaka</s>, the chameleon, the house-lizard, and the blind snake causes destruction of the eyes and madness.
A preparation of the chameleon and the house-lizard produces <s>kuṣṭha</s> (a skin disease).

children.text: sa eva citrabhekāntramadhuyuktaḥ prameham āpādayati manuṣyalohitayuktaḥ śoṣam ||
children.translated_text: That same preparation, combined with the entrails of a spotted frog and with honey, causes <s>prameha</s> (urinary disease); combined with human blood, it causes wasting.
<s>Dūṣīviṣa</s> (latent poison), powder of <s>madana</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, and <s>apajihvikā</s> form another preparation.
A preparation of <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>, <s>āñjalikāra</s>, <s>pracalāka</s>, frog, and <s>akṣipīluka</s> causes <s>viṣūcikā</s> (acute intestinal disorder).
A preparation of <s>pañcakuṣṭhaka</s>, <s>kauṇḍinyaka</s>, flowers of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, and honey causes fever.
A preparation of the tongues of a vulture and a mongoose with <s>granthikā</s>, ground in she-ass's milk, causes muteness and deafness for a month or half-month.
For men, the measure is a single <s>kalā</s>; this is the same as in the preceding rule.

children.text: bhaṅgakvāthopanayanam auṣadhānām cūrṇaṃ prāṇabhṛtām sarveṣāṃ vā kvāthopanayanam evaṃ vīryavattaraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If the powder of the drugs is administered with a decoction of hemp, or with a decoction made from all living creatures, it becomes more potent in this way.
Thus the successful compounding of preparations.

children.text: śālmalīvidārīdhānyasiddho mūlavatsanābhasaṃyuktaś cucchundarīśoṇitapralepena digdho bāṇo yaṃ vidhyati sa viddho 'nyān daśapuruṣān daśati te daṣṭā daśānyān daśanti puruṣān ||
children.translated_text: An arrow prepared with <s>śālmalī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and grain, joined with root and <s>vatsanābha</s>, and smeared with the blood of a musk-shrew: whomever it pierces, that wounded man bites ten other men, and those who have been bitten bite ten other men each.

children.text: bhallātakayātudhānāvānudhāmārgavabāṇānāṃ puṣpair elakākṣigugguluhālāhalānāṃ ca kaṣāyaṃ bastanaraśoṇitayuktaṃ daṃśayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A decoction of the flowers of <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>yātudhāna</s>, <s>avānudha</s>, <s>dhāmārgava</s>, and arrow-plants, and of <s>elakākṣi</s>, bdellium, and <s>hālāhala</s>, mixed with goat's blood and human blood, is a biting preparation.

children.text: tato 'rdhadharaṇiko yogaḥ saktupiṇyākābhyām udake praṇīto dhanuḥśatāyāmam udakāśayaṃ dūṣayati ||
children.translated_text: From that, a preparation measuring half a <s>dharaṇa</s>, put into water with roasted meal and oilcake, pollutes a reservoir one hundred bows in length.

children.text: matsyaparamparā hyetena daṣṭābhimṛṣṭā vā viṣībhavati yaścaitad udakaṃ pibati spṛśati vā ||
children.translated_text: For a succession of fish, bitten or merely touched by this, becomes poisonous, as does anyone who drinks or touches that water.

children.text: raktaśvetasarṣapair godhātripakṣamuṣṭikāyāṃ bhūmau nikhātāyāṃ nihitā vadhyenoddhṛtā yāvat paśyati tāvan mārayati kṛṣṇasarpo vā ||
children.translated_text: With red and white mustard seeds, when it has been placed in a pit in the ground and dug up by the intended victim, it kills for as far as he sees; or a black snake does so.

children.text: vidyutpradagdho 'ṅgāro jvālo vā vidyutpradagdhaiḥ kāṣṭhair gṛhītaścānuvāsitaḥ kṛttikāsu bharaṇīṣu vā raudreṇa karmaṇābhihuto 'gniḥ praṇītaśca niṣpratīkāro dahati ||
children.translated_text: A coal burned by lightning, or a flame taken from wood burned by lightning and treated with fumigation, when offered to by a fierce rite under the <s>Kṛttikā</s> or <s>Bharaṇī</s> lunar mansion and then set forth, burns irresistibly.

children.text: karmārād agnim āhṛtya kṣaudreṇa juhuyāt pṛthak
children.translated_text: Having brought fire from a smith, he should make a separate oblation with honey.

children.text: surayā śauṇḍikād agniṃ mārgato 'gniṃ ghṛtena ca ||
children.translated_text: He should offer to fire from a liquor-seller with liquor, and to fire from the road with ghee.
He should offer to the fire of a woman with one husband with a garland, and to the fire of a promiscuous woman with mustard seeds.

children.text: dadhnā ca sūtikāsvagnim āhitāgniṃ ca taṇḍulaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should offer to fire from a puerperal chamber with curds, and to an established sacred fire with rice grains.

children.text: caṇḍālāgniṃ ca māṃsena citāgniṃ mānuṣeṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: He should offer to the fire of an outcaste with meat, and to funeral-pyre fire with human flesh.
He should offer to all of them together with goat fat and with the human <s>dhruva</s> substance.
With the fire-mantra and with wood of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, he should make the oblation.
This irresistible fire bewilders the eyes of enemies.

children.text: adite namaste anumate namaste sarasvati namaste deva savitar namaste ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Aditi</s>; homage to <s>Anumati</s>; homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>; homage to the god <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: agnaye svāhā somāya svāhā bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>; <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s>; <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Bhūḥ</s>; <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>.
Powder of <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, and <s>śamī</s>, mixed with ghee, is a hunger-suppressing preparation for half a month.
A preparation cooked with <s>kaśeruka</s>, lotus tuber, sugarcane root, lotus fiber, <s>dūrvā</s>, milk, and the scum of ghee lasts for a month.

children.text: māṣayavakulatthadarbhamūlacūrṇaṃ vā kṣīraghṛtābhyām vallīkṣīraghṛtaṃ vā samasiddham sālapṛśniparṇīmūlakalkaṃ payasā pītvā payo vā tatsiddhaṃ madhughṛtābhyām aśitvā māsam upavasati ||
children.translated_text: Or powder of black gram, barley, horse gram, and <s>darbha</s> root, prepared with milk and ghee, or creeper-milk and ghee cooked together: after drinking a paste of <s>sāla</s> and <s>pṛśniparṇī</s> roots with milk, or milk cooked with that paste, and after eating honey and ghee, he fasts for a month.

children.text: śvetabastamūtre saptarātroṣitaiḥ siddhārthakaiḥ siddhaṃ tailaṃ kaṭukālābau māsārdhamāsasthitaṃ catuṣpadadvipadānāṃ virūpakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Oil cooked with white mustard seeds that have soaked for seven nights in the urine of a white goat, and kept in a bitter bottle-gourd for a month or half-month, causes disfigurement of quadrupeds and bipeds.

children.text: takrayavabhakṣasya saptarātrād ūrdhvaṃ śvetagardabhasya leṇḍayavaiḥ siddhaṃ gaurasarṣapatailaṃ virūpakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: For one whose food is buttermilk and barley, after seven nights, white-mustard oil cooked with the dung and barley of a white donkey causes disfigurement.

children.text: etayor anyatarasya mūtraleṇḍarasasiddhaṃ siddhārthakatailam arkatūlapataṅgacūrṇapratīvāpaṃ śvetīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Oil of <s>siddhārthaka</s> (white mustard), cooked in the urine and dung-juice of either of these, with powder of arka-floss and <s>pataṅga</s> added, is a whitening preparation.
A compound of the dung of a white cock and a python is a whitening preparation.

children.text: śvetabastamūtre śvetasarṣapāḥ saptarātroṣitās takram arkakṣīralavaṇaṃ dhānyaṃ ca pakṣasthito yogaḥ śvetīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: White mustard seeds kept for seven nights in the urine of a white goat, with buttermilk, arka latex, salt, and grain, and left in the mixture for a fortnight, form a whitening preparation.

children.text: kaṭukālābau valīgate gatam ardhamāsasthitaṃ gaurasarṣapapiṣṭaṃ romṇāṃ śvetīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: What has been placed in a bitter gourd after it has become wrinkled, kept for half a month, and ground with white mustard, whitens hair.

children.text: alojuneti yaḥ kīṭaḥ śvetā ca gṛhagolikā
children.translated_text: The insect called <s>alojuna</s>, and a white house lizard,
when ground and used as an anointing, make the hair conch-white.

children.text: gomayena tindukāriṣṭakalkena vā marditāṅgasya bhallātakarasānuliptasya māsikaḥ kuṣṭhayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A month-long <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin-disease) formula is this: the body is rubbed with cow dung, or with a paste of <s>tinduka</s> and <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and smeared with <s>bhallātaka</s> juice.

children.text: kṛṣṇasarpamukhe gṛhagolikāmukhe vā saptarātroṣitā guñjāḥ kuṣṭhayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guñjā</s> seeds kept for seven nights in the mouth of a black snake or of a house lizard are a <s>kuṣṭha</s> formula.
An anointing with parrot bile and egg-fluid is a <s>kuṣṭha</s> formula.
The countermeasure for <s>kuṣṭha</s> is a decoction made from <s>priyāla</s> paste.
One who is fed food mixed with the roots of <s>kukkuṭa</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s> becomes fair in a month.
After bathing in a decoction of banyan and being smeared with <s>sahacara</s> paste, one becomes dark.
Orpiment and realgar mixed with <s>śakunakaṅgu</s> oil make a darkening preparation.
Firefly powder mixed with mustard oil glows at night.

children.text: khadyotagaṇḍūpadacūrṇaṃ samudrajantūnāṃ bhṛṅgakapālānāṃ khadirakarṇikārāṇāṃ puṣpacūrṇaṃ vā śakunakaṅgutailayuktaṃ tejanacūrṇam ||
children.translated_text: Powder of fireflies and earthworms, or powder of sea-creatures, beetle-shells, or the flowers of <s>khadira</s> and <s>karṇikāra</s>, mixed with <s>śakunakaṅgu</s> oil, is a luminous powder.
Soot from the bark of <s>pāribhadraka</s>, mixed with frog fat, makes the limbs blaze when fire is applied.
A body smeared with a paste of <s>pāribhadraka</s> bark and sesame blazes when fire is applied.
A lump made from soot of <s>pīlu</s> bark burns in the hand.
One smeared with frog fat blazes when fire is applied.

children.text: tena pradigdham aṅgaṃ kuśāmraphalatailasiktaṃ samudramaṇḍūkīphenakasarjarasacūrṇayuktaṃ vā jvalati ||
children.translated_text: A limb smeared with that, sprinkled with oil of <s>kuśāmra</s> fruit, or mixed with powder of <s>samudramaṇḍūkī</s> foam and <s>sarja</s> resin, blazes.

children.text: maṇḍūkakulīrādīnāṃ vasayā samabhāgaṃ tailaṃ siddham abhyaṅgaṃ gātrāṇām agniprajvālanam ||
children.translated_text: Oil cooked with equal parts of the fat of frogs, crabs, and the like, used as an anointing for the limbs, causes blazing by fire.
A limb smeared with bamboo root and algae, and coated with frog fat, blazes when fire is applied.
With his feet anointed by oil cooked with frog fat and a paste of the roots of <s>pāribhadraka</s>, <s>pratibalā</s>, <s>vañjula</s>, and <s>vajrakadalī</s>, one walks over embers.
<s>Upodakā</s>, <s>pratibalā</s>, <s>vañjula</s>, and <s>pāribhadraka</s>:
with the root paste of these, together with frog fat,
one should cook oil; after anointing clean feet with it,
one may move over a heap of embers as over a heap of flowers.

children.text: haṃsakrauñcamayūrāṇām anyeṣāṃ vā mahāśakunīnām udakaplavānāṃ puccheṣu baddhā naladīpikā rātrāvulkādarśanam ||
children.translated_text: A reed lamp tied to the tails of geese, cranes, peacocks, or other large water birds produces at night the appearance of firebrands.
Ash produced by lightning is for extinguishing fire.

children.text: strīpuṣpapāyitā māṣā vrajakulīmūlaṃ maṇḍūkavasāmiśraṃ cullyāṃ dīptāyām apācanam ||
children.translated_text: Black gram soaked in menstrual fluid, mixed with <s>vrajakulī</s> root and frog fat, prevents cooking on a blazing hearth.
Cleaning the hearth is the countermeasure.

children.text: pīlumayo maṇir agnigarbhaḥ suvarcalāmūlagranthiḥ sūtragranthir vā picupariveṣṭito mukhyād agnidhūmotsargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A bead made of <s>pīlu</s> wood with fire enclosed, or a knot of <s>suvarcalā</s> root or a knot of thread, wrapped in cotton, makes fire and smoke issue from the mouth.
Fire sprinkled with oil of <s>kuśāmra</s> fruit burns in rain and strong wind.
Sea-foam mixed with oil burns while floating on water.

children.text: plavamānānām asthiṣu kalmāṣaveṇunā nirmathito 'gnir nodakena śāmyati udakena jvalati ||
children.translated_text: Fire kindled by friction, with mottled bamboo, in the bones of floating bodies is not quenched by water; it burns with water.

children.text: śastrahatasya śūlaprotasya vā puruṣasya vāmapārśvaparśukāsthiṣu kalmāṣaveṇunā nirmathito 'gniḥ striyāḥ puruṣasya vāsthiṣu manuṣyaparśukayā nirmathito 'gnir yatra trir apasavyaṃ gacchati na cātrānyo 'gnir jvalati ||
children.translated_text: Fire kindled with mottled bamboo in the left-side rib bones of a man killed by a weapon or impaled, or fire kindled with a human rib in the bones of a woman or a man: wherever it is carried counterclockwise three times, no other fire burns there.
A shrew, a <s>khañjarīṭa</s>, and a <s>khārakīṭa</s> insect are ground up
and mixed with horse urine; this is for breaking fetters.
Or a magnet-stone, with a coating of the fat of crabs, frogs, and <s>khārakīṭa</s> insects, is twice as effective.
<s>Nārakagarbha</s>, ground with flank material from <s>kaṅka</s> and <s>bhāsa</s> birds and with lotus-water, is a foot-ointment for quadrupeds and bipeds.

children.text: ulūkagṛdhravasābhyām uṣṭracarmopānahāvabhyajya vaṭapattraiḥ praticchādya pañcāśadyojanānyaśrānto gacchati ||
children.translated_text: After anointing camel-hide shoes with the fats of owls and vultures and covering them with banyan leaves, one walks fifty <s>yojana</s>s without fatigue.

children.text: śyenakaṅkakākagṛdhrahaṃsakrauñcavīcīrallānāṃ majjāno retāṃsi vā yojanaśatāya siṃhavyāghradvīpakākolūkānāṃ majjāno retāṃsi vā ||
children.translated_text: For a hundred <s>yojana</s>s, use the marrows or semen of hawks, <s>kaṅka</s> birds, crows, vultures, geese, cranes, and <s>vīcīralla</s> birds, or the marrows or semen of lions, tigers, panthers, crows, and owls.

children.text: sārvavarṇikāni garbhapatanānyuṣṭrikāyām abhiṣūya śmaśāne pretaśiśūn vā tatsamutthitaṃ medo yojanaśatāya ||
children.translated_text: For a hundred <s>yojana</s>s, use the fat produced from miscarried embryos of all classes deposited in a she-camel, or from dead infants in a cremation ground.
With unwelcome marvels and portents one should produce alarm in the enemy,

children.text: ā rājyāyeti nirvādaḥ samānaḥ kopa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the rumor being, "It is for the kingdom"; this is called a common provocation to anger.

children.text: mārjāroṣṭravṛkavarāhaśvāvidvāgulīnaptṛkākolūkānām anyeṣāṃ vā niśācarāṇāṃ sattvānām ekasya dvayor bahūnāṃ vā dakṣiṇāni vāmāni cākṣīṇi gṛhītvā dvidhā cūrṇaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Taking the right and left eyes of one, two, or many nocturnal creatures, such as cats, camels, wolves, boars, porcupines, bats, <s>naptṛ</s>s, crows, owls, or others, he should have them made into two powders.

children.text: tato dakṣiṇaṃ vāmena vāmaṃ dakṣiṇena samabhyajya rātrau tamasi ca paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Then, after anointing the right eye with the left powder and the left eye with the right powder, one sees at night and in darkness.
<s>Ekāmlaka</s>, <s>varāhākṣi</s>, a firefly, and black <s>śārivā</s>...
With his eyes anointed with this, he sees forms at night.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa śastrahatasya śūlaprotasya vā puṃsaḥ śiraḥkapāle mṛttikāyāṃ yavān āvāsyāvikṣīreṇa secayet ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should sow barley in earth placed in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled on a stake, and should water it with ewe's milk.
Then, after tying on a garland of the sprouted barley, he moves about with his shadow and visible form lost.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa śvamārjārolūkavāgulīnāṃ dakṣiṇāni vāmāni cākṣīṇi dvidhā cūrṇaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should have the right and left eyes of dogs, cats, owls, and bats made separately into powder.
Then, with his eyes anointed each according to its own powder, he moves about with his shadow and visible form lost.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa puruṣaghātinaḥ kāṇḍakasya śalākām añjanīṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should have an applicator-stick and a collyrium case made from a spike that has killed a man.
Then, with his eyes anointed by any one of the eye-powders, he moves about with his shadow and visible form lost.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa kālāyasīm añjanīṃ śalākāṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should have a collyrium case and applicator-stick made of black iron.

children.text: tato niśācarāṇāṃ sattvānām anyatamasya śiraḥkapālam añjanena pūrayitvā mṛtāyāḥ striyā yonau praveśya dāhayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after filling the skull of any one of the night-roaming creatures with collyrium and inserting it into the vagina of a dead woman, he should burn it.

children.text: tad añjanaṃ puṣyeṇoddhṛtya tasyām añjanyāṃ nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should take out that collyrium and place it in that collyrium case.
With his eyes anointed with it, he moves about with his shadow and visible form lost.

children.text: yatra brāhmaṇam āhitāgniṃ dagdhaṃ dahyamānaṃ vā paśyet tatra trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa svayaṃmṛtasya vāsasā prasevaṃ kṛtvā citābhasmanā pūrayitvā tam ābadhya naṣṭacchāyārūpaścarati ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he sees a Brahmin who maintains the sacred fires either cremated or being cremated, there, having fasted for three nights under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should make a pouch from the garment of someone who died naturally, fill it with the pyre-ashes, tie it on, and move about with his shadow and visible form lost.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya pretakārye yo gaur māryate tasyāsthimajjacūrṇapūrṇāhibhastrā paśūnām antardhānam ||
children.translated_text: At a Brahmin's funeral rite, a snake-skin bag filled with powder of the bones and marrow of the cow that is killed there brings concealment from domestic animals.

children.text: sarpadaṣṭasya bhasmanā pūrṇā pracalākabhastrā mṛgāṇām antardhānam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>pracalāka</s> bag filled with the ashes of someone bitten by a snake brings concealment from wild animals.
A snake-skin bag filled with powder of the tails, excrement, and knee-bones of owls and bats brings concealment from birds.
Thus there are eight formulas for disappearance.

children.text: baliṃ vairocanaṃ vande śatamāyaṃ ca śambaram
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Vairocana</s>, and <s>Śambara</s> of a hundred illusions;

children.text: bhaṇḍīrapākaṃ narakaṃ nikumbhaṃ kumbham eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṇḍīrapāka</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, <s>Nikumbha</s>, and <s>Kumbha</s> as well.
I praise <s>Devala</s> and <s>Nārada</s>; I praise <s>Sāvarṇi</s> and <s>Gālava</s>.

children.text: eteṣām anuyogena kṛtaṃ te svāpanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: Through the application of these, a great sleep-charm has been made for you.
As pythons sleep, and as the <s>camūkhala</s> creatures also sleep,

children.text: tathā svapantu puruṣā ye ca grāme kutūhalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so may the men sleep, and those in the village who are curious.
With a thousand vessels and with a hundred chariot-rims,

children.text: imaṃ gṛhaṃ pravekṣyāmi tūṣṇīm āsantu bhāṇḍakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall enter this house; let the household articles remain silent.
After bowing to <s>Manu</s> and tying on the <s>śunakaphelaka</s> amulets,

children.text: ye devā devalokeṣu mānuṣeṣu ca brāhmaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gods who are in the divine worlds, and the Brahmins among human beings,
the perfected ones who have mastered study, and the ascetics of <s>Kailāsa</s>,

children.text: etebhyaḥ sarvasiddhebhyaḥ kṛtaṃ te svāpanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: through all these perfected beings, a great sleep-charm has been made for you.
May those who come upon me pass by; may those who are gathered go away.
Svāhā to <s>Alita</s>, <s>Valita</s>, and <s>Manu</s>.
The procedure for this is as follows.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ puṣyayoginyāṃ śvapākīhastād vilekhāvalekhanaṃ krīṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for three nights, on a dark-fortnight fourteenth day conjoined with <s>Puṣya</s>, he should buy a <s>vilekhāvalekhana</s> scraping implement from the hand of an outcaste woman.

children.text: tanmāṣaiḥ saha kaṇḍolikāyāṃ kṛtvāsaṃkīrṇa ādahane nikhānayet ||
children.translated_text: Putting that together with black gram beans in a small basket, he should bury it in a secluded cremation ground.

children.text: dvitīyasyāṃ caturdaśyām uddhṛtya kumāryā peṣayitvā gulikāḥ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: On the second fourteenth day, after digging it up, he should have it ground by a maiden and made into pills.

children.text: tata ekāṃ gulikām abhimantrayitvā yatraitena mantreṇa kṣipati tat sarvaṃ prasvāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, after consecrating one pill by mantra, wherever he throws it with this mantra, it puts all there to sleep.

children.text: etenaiva kalpena śvāvidhaḥ śalyakaṃ trikālaṃ triśvetam asaṃkīrṇa ādahane nikhānayet ||
children.translated_text: By this same procedure, he should bury a porcupine's <s>śalyaka</s> quill, <s>triśveta</s> and treated at the three times, in a secluded cremation ground.

children.text: dvitīyasyāṃ caturdaśyām uddhṛtyādahanabhasmanā saha yatraitena mantreṇa kṣipati tat sarvaṃ prasvāpayati ||
children.translated_text: On the second fourteenth day, after digging it up together with cremation-ground ashes, wherever he throws it with this mantra, it puts all there to sleep.
I praise <s>Suvarṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> with the kuśa-banner,

children.text: sarvāśca devatā vande vande sarvāṃśca tāpasān ||
children.translated_text: and I praise all the deities; I praise all the ascetics.

children.text: vaśaṃ me brāhmaṇā yāntu bhūmipālāśca kṣatriyāḥ
children.translated_text: May the Brahmins come under my control, and the Kṣatriya protectors of the earth;

children.text: vaśaṃ vaiśyāśca śūdrāśca vaśatāṃ yāntu me sadā ||
children.translated_text: may the Vaiśyas and Śūdras also always come under my control.

children.text: svāhā amile kimile vayucāre prayoge phakke vayuhve vihāle dantakaṭake svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Svāhā: amile, kimile, vayucāre, prayoge, phakke, vayuhve, vihāle, dantakaṭake, svāhā.

children.text: sukhaṃ svapantu śunakā ye ca grāme kutūhalāḥ
children.translated_text: May the dogs sleep happily, and those in the village who are curious.
And this porcupine quill, <s>triśveta</s>, fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: prasuptāḥ sarvasiddhā hi etat te svāpanaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: for all the perfected ones are indeed asleep; this sleep-charm has been made for you,
as far as the boundary of the village, until the rising of the sun.
Svāhā.
The procedure for this is as follows.

children.text: śvāvidhaḥ śalyakāni triśvetāni saptarātropoṣitaḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ khādirābhiḥ samidhābhir agnim etena mantreṇāṣṭaśatasampātaṃ kṛtvā madhughṛtābhyām abhijuhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having fasted for seven nights, on the dark-fortnight fourteenth day, he should take the <s>triśveta</s> porcupine quills, kindle a fire with khadira fuel-sticks, perform an eight-hundredfold consecration with this mantra, and offer oblations of honey and ghee.

children.text: tata ekam etena mantreṇa grāmadvāri gṛhadvāri vā yatra nikhanyate tat sarvaṃ prasvāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Then wherever one of them is buried with this mantra, at a village gate or a house door, it puts all there to sleep.

children.text: baliṃ vairocanaṃ vande śatamāyaṃ ca śambaram
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Vairocana</s>, and <s>Śambara</s> of a hundred illusions;
<s>Nikumbha</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, and the great asura <s>Tantukaccha</s>;
<s>Armālava</s>, <s>Pramīla</s>, <s>Maṇḍolūka</s>, and <s>Ghaṭobala</s>;
and <s>Kṛṣṇakaṃsopacāra</s> and the famous <s>Paulomī</s>.
Having consecrated it by mantra, I take the <s>śavaśārikā</s> for the sake of success.

children.text: jayatu jayati ca namaḥ śalakabhūtebhyaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: May it conquer; it does conquer. Homage to the <s>śalakabhūtas</s>; svāhā.

children.text: sukhaṃ svapantu śunakā ye ca grāme kutūhalāḥ
children.translated_text: May the dogs sleep happily, and those in the village who are curious.

children.text: sukhaṃ svapantu siddhārthā yam arthaṃ mārgayāmahe
children.translated_text: May the accomplished ones sleep happily, for the aim that we seek.

children.text: yāvad astam ayād udayo yāvadarthaṃ phalaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: As far as sunrise goes to sunset, so far may the desired fruit be mine.
Thus, <s>svāhā</s>.
The application of this is as follows.

children.text: caturbhaktopavāsī kṛṣṇacaturdaśyām asaṃkīrṇa ādahane baliṃ kṛtvaitena mantreṇa śavaśārikāṃ gṛhītvā pautrīpoṭṭalikaṃ badhnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: After fasting through four meals, on the dark fourteenth lunar day, in an unmixed cremation ground, he should make an offering and, with this mantra, take a corpse-śārikā and tie it in a <s>pautrī</s> packet.

children.text: tanmadhye śvāvidhaḥ śalyakena viddhvā yatraitena mantreṇa nikhanyate tat sarvaṃ prasvāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Having pierced it in the middle with a porcupine quill, wherever it is buried with this mantra, it puts everything there to sleep.

children.text: upaimi śaraṇaṃ cāgniṃ daivatāni diśo daśa
children.translated_text: I approach <s>Agni</s> for refuge, and the deities and the ten directions.

children.text: apayāntu ca sarvāṇi vaśatāṃ yāntu me sadā ||
children.translated_text: Let all things depart, and let them always come under my control.
<s>Svāhā</s>.
The application of this is as follows.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa śarkarā ekaviṃśatisampātaṃ kṛtvā madhughṛtābhyām abhijuhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: After fasting for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, he should perform twenty-one consecrations over pebbles and make oblations with honey and ghee.
Then, after honoring them with perfume and garlands, he should bury them.

children.text: dvitīyena puṣyeṇoddhṛtyaikāṃ śarkarām abhimantrayitvā kapāṭam āhanyāt ||
children.translated_text: At the second <s>Puṣya</s>, he should dig up one pebble, consecrate it with a mantra, and strike the door-panel.
By means of four pebbles placed inside, a door is opened.

children.text: caturbhaktopavāsī kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ bhagnasya puruṣasyāsthnā ṛṣabhaṃ kārayet abhimantrayeccaitena ||
children.translated_text: After fasting through four meals, on the dark fourteenth lunar day, he should have a bull made from the bone of a man whose body was broken, and he should consecrate it with this mantra.
A cattle-cart yoked with two oxen then comes.
After that it stops in the highest sky.
Having the scent of the sun, it strikes all around and fills everything.
You are the flood of <s>caṇḍālī</s>, <s>kumbhī</s>, gourd, and pungent essence, possessing a woman's vulva; <s>svāhā</s>.
This is for opening locks and for inducing sleep.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa śastrahatasya śūlaprotasya vā puṃsaḥ śiraḥkapāle mṛttikāyāṃ tuvarīrāvāsyodakena secayet ||
children.translated_text: After fasting for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled, he should sow <s>tuvarī</s> seeds in soil and sprinkle them with water.
When they have grown, he should take them under that same <s>Puṣya</s> and twist them into a cord.

children.text: tataḥ sajyānāṃ dhanuṣāṃ yantrāṇāṃ ca purastācchedanaṃ jyāchedanaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, placed before strung bows and engines, it causes cutting in front and cutting of bowstrings.

children.text: udakāhibhastrām ucchvāsamṛttikayā striyāḥ puruṣasya vā pūrayennāsikābandhanaṃ mukhagrahaśca ||
children.translated_text: He should fill the bladder of a water-snake with the breath-earth of a woman or a man; this causes stopping of the nose and seizure of the mouth.
Having filled a boar's bladder with breath-earth, he should bind it with monkey sinew; this causes abdominal obstruction.

children.text: kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ śastrahatāyā goḥ kapilāyāḥ pittena rājavṛkṣamayīm amitrapratimām añjyāt andhīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: On the dark fourteenth lunar day, he should anoint an enemy-effigy made of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> wood with the bile of a tawny cow killed by a weapon; this causes blindness.

children.text: caturbhaktopavāsī kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ baliṃ kṛtvā śūlaprotasya puruṣasyāsthnā kīlakān kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After fasting through four meals, on the dark fourteenth lunar day, and making an offering, he should have pegs made from the bone of an impaled man.

children.text: eteṣām ekaḥ purīṣe mūtre vā nikhāta ānāhaṃ karoti pade 'syāsane vā nikhātaḥ śoṣeṇa mārayati āpaṇe kṣetre gṛhe vā vṛtticchedaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: One of these, buried in feces or urine, causes obstruction; buried in his footprint or seat, it kills by wasting; buried in a market, field, or house, it causes loss of livelihood.

children.text: etenaiva kalpena vidyuddagdhasya vṛkṣasya kīlakā vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this same procedure, pegs made from a tree struck by lightning are also explained.

children.text: punar navam avācīnaṃ nimbaḥ kāmamadhuśca yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s> turned downward, neem, and what is called <s>kāmamadhu</s>,
monkey hair and human bone, tied with the garment of a dead person,

children.text: nikhanyate gṛhe yasya dṛṣṭvā vā yat padaṃ nayet
children.translated_text: when buried in someone's house, or when carried to the footprint that has been seen,
that man, together with sons, wife, and wealth, does not pass beyond three fortnights.

children.text: punar navam avācīnaṃ nimbaḥ kāmamadhuśca yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s> turned downward, neem, and what is called <s>kāmamadhu</s>,
<s>svayaṃguptā</s> and human bone, when buried in someone's footprint,

children.text: dvāre gṛhasya senāyā grāmasya nagarasya vā
children.translated_text: at the gate of a house, army, village, or city,
that man, together with sons, wife, and wealth, does not pass beyond three fortnights.
He should obtain the hairs of a goat and monkey, and also of a cat and mongoose,
and those of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>śvapākas</s>, crows, and owls.
Feces kneaded with this mixture immediately brings about destruction.
Ferment from a corpse's discarded offering, and the hair of a mongoose,
together with <s>vṛścikālī</s> and snake-slough, when buried in someone's footprint,
make him impotent at once, until that is removed.

children.text: trirātropoṣitaḥ puṣyeṇa śastrahatasya śūlaprotasya vā puṃsaḥ śiraḥkapāle mṛttikāyāṃ guñjā āvāsyodakena secayet ||
children.translated_text: After fasting for three nights, under <s>Puṣya</s>, in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled, he should sow <s>guñjā</s> seeds in soil and sprinkle them with water.

children.text: jātānām amāvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vā puṣyayoginyāṃ guñjavallīr grāhayitvā maṇḍalikāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: When they have grown, on a new-moon or full-moon day joined with <s>Puṣya</s>, he should have the <s>guñjā</s> vines gathered and made into small circles.
Food and drink vessels placed on them do not become depleted.

children.text: rātriprekṣāyāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ pradīpāgniṣu mṛtadhenoḥ stanān utkṛtya dāhayet ||
children.translated_text: When a night spectacle has begun, he should cut off the udders of a dead cow and burn them in the flames of lamps.
Having ground the burned pieces with bull's urine, he should smear the inside of a new pot.

children.text: taṃ grāmam apasavyaṃ pariṇīya yat tatra nyastaṃ navanītam eṣāṃ tat sarvam āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: After carrying that counterclockwise around the village, all the fresh butter of those people that has been placed there comes to it.

children.text: kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ puṣyayoginyāṃ śuno lagnakasya yonau kālāyasīṃ mudrikāṃ preṣayet ||
children.translated_text: On the dark fourteenth lunar day joined with <s>Puṣya</s>, he should insert a black-iron ring into the yoni of a mating dog.
He should take it when it has fallen out by itself.
With it, tree-fruits that have been summoned come to him.
With preparations joined with mantra and medicine, and with those made by magic,
he should injure enemies and protect his own people.
Countermeasures on one's own side against <s>dūṣīviṣa</s> (latent poison) and <s>gara</s> (compound poison) applied by others are as follows.

children.text: śleṣmātakakapitthadantidantaśaṭhagojiśirīṣapāṭalībalāsyonāgapunarnavāśvetavāraṇakvāthayuktam candanasālāvṛkīlohitayuktaṃ nejanodakaṃ rājopabhogyānāṃ guhyaprakṣālanaṃ strīṇām senāyāśca viṣapratīkāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Washing-water mixed with a decoction of <s>śleṣmātaka</s>, <s>kapittha</s>, <s>danti</s>, <s>dantaśaṭha</s>, <s>goji</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>syonāga</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, and white <s>vāraṇa</s>, and mixed with <s>candana</s>, <s>sālāvṛkī</s>, and <s>lohita</s>, is an antidote to poison for things used by the king, for washing the private parts of women, and for the army.

Powder of <s>mahīrājī</s> mixed with the bile of spotted deer, mongoose, <s>nīlakaṇṭha</s>, and iguana, combined with <s>sinduvārita</s>, <s>varaṇa</s>, <s>vāruṇī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, tips of <s>śataparvan</s>, and <s>piṇḍītaka</s>, removes the harmful effect of <s>madana</s>.

children.text: sṛgālavinnāmadanasinduvāritavaraṇavāraṇavalīmūlakaṣāyāṇām anyatamasya samastānāṃ vā kṣīrayuktaṃ pānaṃ madanadoṣaharam ||
children.translated_text: A drink made with milk from the decoction of the roots of any one of <s>sṛgālavinnā</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>sinduvārita</s>, <s>varaṇa</s>, and <s>vāraṇavalī</s>, or of all of them together, removes the disorder caused by <s>madana</s>.
Oil of <s>kaiḍarya</s> and <s>pūtitila</s>, used as a nasal treatment, removes madness.
A preparation of <s>priyaṅgu</s> and <s>naktamālā</s> removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease).
A preparation of the herbs <s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>lodhra</s> removes suppuration and wasting.
Powder of <s>kaṭphala</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, used as a nasal treatment, removes diseases of the head.

A preparation of <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>lākṣārasa</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>haridrā</s>, and honey is for bringing back to consciousness those who have lost consciousness through strangulation, drowning, poison, a blow, or a fall.

children.text: manuṣyāṇām akṣamātram gavāśvānāṃ dviguṇam caturguṇaṃ hastyuṣṭrāṇām ||
children.translated_text: For humans the dose is one <s>akṣa</s>; for cattle and horses it is double, and for elephants and camels fourfold.
For these, the gem called <s>rukmagarbha</s> removes all poison.
The <s>maṇi</s> (amulet) of an <s>aśvattha</s> grown on <s>akṣīva</s>, associated with <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>muṣkaka</s>, and <s>puṣpavandāka</s>, removes all poison.
The sound of musical instruments smeared with these destroys poison.

children.text: liptadhvajaṃ patākāṃ vā dṛṣṭvā bhavati nirviṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One becomes free from poison on seeing a standard or banner smeared with them.
Having used these to make countermeasures for his own troops and then for himself,
he should employ poisons, toxic smokes, and water-polluting agents against enemies.
